plan.title: Pacific Coast Highway: San Francisco to Los Angeles
plan.summary: An unforgettable 3-day coastal cruise down California's legendary Route 1, featuring the soaring cliffs of Big Sur, sweeping ocean vistas, and classic seaside towns.

days.title: San Francisco to Monterey via Santa Cruz
days.summary: Leave San Francisco behind and cruise down the rugged Pacific coastline through Half Moon Bay and the dramatic cliffs of Pacifica. The road hugs the ocean before dipping inland through redwood forests into the vibrant surf town of Santa Cruz, setting the stage for a relaxed coastal evening in Monterey.
days.stay: Stay near Cannery Row or downtown Monterey for easy access to the waterfront and local seafood spots, choosing from historic inns, boutique motels, or classic coastal lodges.

days.title: Big Sur Coast to San Luis Obispo
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Big Sur Coast Highway where the Santa Lucia Mountains plunge directly into the roaring Pacific Ocean. You will sweep through tight turns and cross the iconic Bixby Creek Bridge on a masterclass of coastal engineering, ending the day in the rolling hills of San Luis Obispo.
days.stay: Stay in downtown San Luis Obispo near the historic Mission Plaza to enjoy the lively college-town atmosphere, where comfortable motels, boutique hotels, and charming B&Bs await.

days.title: Central Coast to Los Angeles
days.summary: Cruise past the sweeping dunes of Pismo Beach before joining the fast stretch down to the Mediterranean-style elegance of Santa Barbara. The final push runs right along the Malibu coastline, delivering you directly into the sprawling energy of Los Angeles as the sun dips into the Pacific.
days.stay: Stay in Santa Monica or West Hollywood for the quintessential Los Angeles experience, featuring everything from stylish design hotels to upscale beachside resorts.

roads.drive: A demanding, winding two-lane road with sheer drop-offs, tight hairpins, frequent narrow sections, and heavy tourist traffic during midday.
roads.tips: Check Caltrans for slide closures before heading out. Drive southbound to stay in the ocean-side lane for easy pullouts, and fill your tank in Carmel.

roads.tips: Watch for morning fog and seasonal storm-related slip-outs. Keep your fuel topped up before leaving major hubs.

plan.title: Denver to Moab via the San Juan Skyway
plan.summary: This 3-day journey from Denver to Moab takes you across the rugged Rocky Mountains via the Million Dollar Highway and the San Juan Skyway. You will experience soaring high-altitude passes, dramatic cliff-hanging descents, and deep red rock canyons.

days.title: Denver to Ouray
days.summary: Climbing out of the Denver metro area, you ascend rapidly into the high Rockies via high-altitude passes and sweeping mountain valleys. The highlight is the sweeping expanse of the Top of the Rockies scenic byway before dropping down into the dramatic box canyon of Ouray. It is a day of massive elevation changes, transitioning from foothill pines to towering alpine peaks.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Ouray within walking distance of the historic main drag, choosing from rustic historic lodges, Victorian bed-and-breakfasts, or classic motor courts.

days.title: Ouray to Silverton
days.summary: This short-distance day packs an incredible punch, taking you across the most famous section of the San Juan Skyway to Telluride and back over the heart of the Million Dollar Highway. You will navigate sheer drops, dramatic mountain passes, and stunning alpine vistas at every turn. The driving is intense, rewarding focus with some of the most dramatic scenery in North America.
days.stay: Stay right in historic downtown Silverton near Blair Street to soak in the rugged 19th-century mining town atmosphere, featuring cozy local inns and historic hotels.

days.title: Silverton to Moab
days.summary: Leaving the high peaks of the San Juan Mountains behind, the route drops south toward Cortez before cutting northwest into the surreal red rock desert of Utah. The landscape shifts dramatically from alpine pine forests to deep canyons and towering sandstone monoliths. The final stretch along US 191 delivers you right into the red rock adventure capital of Moab.
days.stay: Stay close to downtown Moab for easy access to the local restaurants and shops, picking from modern adventure motels, upscale desert resorts, or scenic campgrounds.

roads.name: Top of the Rockies

official.name: Top of the Rockies
official.description: Scenic high-altitude drive through the Rocky Mountains and historic Leadville

roads.why: This route showcases massive alpine vistas, sweeping high-altitude meadows, and historical mining towns nestled high in the Rocky Mountains.
roads.drive: Long steady climbs and descents with well-paved two-lane highway. Grades are manageable, but expect high altitudes exceeding 10,000 feet that can affect vehicle power.
roads.tips: Best driven between June and September. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer; check vehicle brakes before descending.

info.title: Top of the Rockies National Scenic Byway

roads.name: Million Dollar Highway

official.name: Million Dollar Highway
official.description: Ouray to Silverton over Red Mountain Pass, a cliff-hugging road with no guardrails and huge drops

roads.why: Renowned for its sheer drops, lack of guardrails, and jaw-dropping mountain views over Red Mountain Pass, it is a bucket-list drive for enthusiasts.
roads.drive: Steep 6-to-8 percent grades, tight unbanked switchbacks, and narrow lanes carved directly into cliff faces with zero guardrails in many sections.
roads.tips: Drive north from Silverton to Ouray to stay on the mountain wall side of the road. Avoid in severe winter weather unless equipped for extreme mountain driving.

roads.name: San Juan Skyway
roads.segment: from Ouray through Durango to Cortez

official.name: San Juan Skyway
official.description: Loop through the San Juan Mountains, Colorado's most rugged and isolated mountain range

roads.why: It forms a massive loop through the heart of the San Juan Mountains, offering a stunning variety of alpine peaks, rushing rivers, and historic towns.
roads.drive: A mix of winding mountain passes, sweeping canyon curves, and relatively flat desert stretches near Cortez. Watch out for slow RV traffic and wildlife.
roads.tips: Allow extra time for tourist traffic, especially around Telluride and Durango. Keep an eye on fuel levels as gas stations can be spaced out.

plan.title: Desert Canyons and High Plateaus Loop
plan.summary: This 4-day loop takes you from the neon of Las Vegas through the majestic red rocks of Zion and Bryce Canyon, past Lake Powell to the Grand Canyon's North Rim, showcasing some of the American Southwest's most iconic landscapes and driving roads.

days.title: From Las Vegas to Zion and Bryce Canyon
days.summary: Leave the neon glow of Las Vegas behind for the striking desert expanses and red rock monoliths of southern Utah. The highlight is climbing the Zion Scenic Byway through the tight turns of the Mt. Carmel Tunnel, followed by a transition onto the dramatic high-desert terrain leading toward Bryce Canyon. It is a day of vivid color shifts, from pale sandstone cliffs to deeply saturated canyon walls.
days.stay: Stay near the park entrance in rustic canyon lodges or comfortable standard motels that put you within minutes of the hoodoos. Expect typical national park gateway pricing.

days.title: Through Grand Staircase to Page
days.summary: Tackle the legendary twists of Scenic Byway 12 as it crests high alpine ridges and plunges through stark, otherworldly rock formations near Escalante and Boulder. The driving is demanding and deeply rewarding, offering sweeping panoramic drop-offs and naked slickrock vistas. Finish the day by descending toward the desert basin of Page near Lake Powell.
days.stay: Look for standard contemporary chain hotels or roadside motels clustered right along the main thoroughfare in Page for easy access to nearby canyon tours. Prices are moderate for the area.

days.title: To the North Rim of the Grand Canyon
days.overnight: Grand Canyon National Park North Rim, Arizona
days.summary: Head west through the Vermilion Cliffs before climbing the Kaibab Plateau on Arizona State Route 67, a stunning, high-altitude forest drive. The road cuts through dense stands of golden aspens and ponderosa pines before abruptly terminating at the remote North Rim of the Grand Canyon. The driving is peaceful and shaded, offering a stark contrast to the red rock deserts left behind.
days.stay: Secure a historic timber cabin or lodge room directly on the canyon rim inside the park, booking well in advance. These unique properties command a premium for their unmatched sunset views.

days.title: Back to Las Vegas via Virgin River Gorge
days.summary: Cruise north through the high desert of northern Arizona and into Utah, navigating the sweeping curves of the Kaibab Plateau descent toward Fredonia. Rejoin the interstate system near St. George, then power through the dramatic red rock chasm of the Virgin River Gorge on I-15. The final stretch brings you back into the bright lights of Las Vegas with plenty of daylight to spare.
days.stay: Unwind on the Las Vegas Strip at a mega-resort with sweeping valley views, choosing from luxury high-rises or lively entertainment-themed hotels. Prices vary wildly depending on the weekend.

roads.name: Zion Scenic Byway
roads.segment: from Hurricane to Mount Carmel Junction

official.name: Zion Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic route through Zion Canyon, the Mt. Carmel Tunnel, and the red rock country of southern Utah

roads.why: It winds directly through the heart of Zion Canyon's towering sheer cliffs, passing massive stone monoliths and terminating in the engineering marvel of the Mt. Carmel Tunnel.
roads.drive: The road features tight switchbacks, low-speed limits, and strict size restrictions inside the historic tunnel. Traffic can be heavy with shuttle buses and pedestrians, so patience is required.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning to beat the visitor traffic and secure parking. Watch out for bighorn sheep stepping onto the asphalt.

roads.name: Scenic Byway 12
roads.segment: from Bryce Canyon Junction to Torrey

official.name: Scenic Byway 12 (Journey Through Time)
official.description: Scenic drive through canyons, plateaus, and valleys
official.wiki: Utah's Scenic Byway 12 - A Journey Through Time

roads.why: Widely celebrated as one of America's greatest drives, it traverses high-elevation forests, razor-thin ridge lines with sheer drops on both sides, and undulating slickrock canyons.
roads.drive: Expect steep grades, sharp switchbacks, and areas like 'The Hogback' where the road narrows atop a thin spine of rock with no shoulders. Take it slow and watch the road.
roads.tips: Ensure your fuel tank is full before leaving Torrey or Escalante, as gas stations are sparse. High winds can buffet vehicles on exposed ridges.

roads.name: Kaibab Plateau–North Rim Parkway
roads.segment: from Jacob Lake to Grand Canyon North Rim

official.name: Kaibab Plateau–North Rim Parkway
official.description: Scenic drive through ponderosa pine forests to the North Rim of the Grand Canyon

roads.why: A breathtaking forested corridor that climbs past 9,000 feet, transitioning from desert scrub into thick alpine stands of ponderosa pine, spruce, and aspen.
roads.drive: A smooth, well-paved two-lane highway with gentle curves, moderate grades, and occasional wildlife crossings. Driving here is deeply relaxing compared to the technical desert routes.
roads.tips: Open only seasonally from mid-May to mid-October due to heavy winter snowpacks. Fuel up in Jacob Lake before heading south to the rim.

plan.title: Grand Teton, Yellowstone and the Beartooth Highway
plan.summary: This breathtaking 3-day road trip takes you from Jackson Hole through the dramatic peaks of Grand Teton National Park and the geothermal wonders of Yellowstone, culminating on the legendary Beartooth Highway into Billings.

days.title: Through Grand Teton to Yellowstone
days.summary: Begin with an inspiring drive past the jagged peaks of the Teton Range before climbing into the volcanic expanse of Yellowstone National Park. The best stretch hugs the shore of Jackson Lake and winds along the Yellowstone River toward the magnificent Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. The feel of the day transitions from alpine serenity to geothermal wonder as you navigate park traffic and forest corridors.
days.stay: Stay in a rustic woodland lodge or cabin near the canyon rim to be steps away from the waterfalls at dawn. Lodges and camper cabins are the standard accommodation here, booking out months in advance.

days.title: Yellowstone Geysers and Wildlife
days.summary: Traverse the interior of Yellowstone past immense thermal basins, roaming bison herds, and bubbling mud pots along the Grand Loop Road. The best stretch climbs northeast through the Lamar Valley where wildlife viewing is legendary, ending with a thrilling ascent into the high mountain mining town of Cooke City. The day offers a wonderful contrast of park wildlife and wild mountain terrain.
days.stay: Stay in a classic mountain cabin, rustic motel, or historic inn nestled high in the rugged Cooke City-Silver Gate area. Accommodations are rugged and vintage, reflecting the historic mining roots of the mountain pass.

days.title: Over the Beartooth Highway to Montana
days.summary: Conquer the legendary Beartooth Highway, one of America's highest and most breathtaking paved mountain passes, featuring dizzying switchbacks and alpine tundra. The best stretch crosses the absolute roof of the Beartooth Plateau above tree line with staggering views in every direction before dropping steeply into Red Lodge. From there, cruise easy high-speed interstate miles north across the plains to Billings.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Billings near the historic Skaggs Building and vibrant local steakhouses to celebrate the end of an epic drive. You will find comfortable modern hotels, historic boutique properties, and reliable highway motels.

roads.name: Teton Park Road
roads.segment: from Jackson to Colter Bay Village
roads.why: Offers up-close, uninterrupted views of the towering Grand Teton peaks rising directly from the valley floor without the obstruction of the main highway.
roads.drive: An easy, scenic two-lane park road with gentle curves, rolling hills, and occasional wildlife crossings. Speed limits are moderate, and traffic can be heavy with sightseers during summer.
roads.tips: Watch out for bison and elk standing on or near the asphalt, especially early in the morning. Keep your headlights on.

roads.name: Grand Loop Road
roads.segment: from Colter Bay Village to Mammoth Hot Springs
roads.why: The ultimate spine of Yellowstone National Park, connecting major geothermal basins, massive lakes, deep canyons, and sweeping wildlife valleys.
roads.drive: A mix of winding forest roads and high plateau stretches with rolling grades. Expect significant summer RV traffic, bison jams, and frequent delays.
roads.tips: Fill up your tank whenever you see a gas station inside the park, as distances are deceiving and fuel prices are high. Patience is essential for wildlife traffic jams.

roads.name: Beartooth Highway
roads.segment: from Cooke City to Red Lodge

official.name: Beartooth Highway
official.description: Scenic high-elevation highway to Yellowstone National Park's northeast entrance

roads.why: A masterpiece of highway engineering featuring glacial lakes, permanent snowfields, sheer drop-offs, and 360-degree views above 10,000 feet.
roads.drive: Thrilling and exposed, featuring the famous switchbacks known as the 'Idea Creek' section and the 'Beartooth Z's'. Grades reach up to 10 percent with dramatic drop-offs and no guardrails in many high sections.
roads.tips: Open only during summer months (typically late May through September). Weather changes instantly; expect fierce wind, snow, and intense sun at high altitude. Check conditions before setting out.

plan.title: Glacier National Park Loop from Missoula
plan.summary: Experience the rugged grandeur of the Northern Rockies on this 3-day loop from Missoula. Drive over the legendary Going-to-the-Sun Road across Glacier National Park and cruise through stunning alpine passes.

days.title: From Missoula to Flathead Lake
days.summary: Head north from Missoula following the roaring Clark Fork River before opening up onto the dramatic, island-dotted expanse of Flathead Lake. The drive along the east shore on US 93 offers sweeping water views framed by the Mission Mountains, leading into the fertile Flathead Valley. It is an effortless, scenic transition from mountain town culture to big-sky lake country.
days.stay: Stay in Kalispell's historic downtown core, where you will find comfortable boutique hotels, traditional motels, and inviting historic inns within easy walking distance of local restaurants and microbreweries.

days.title: Across Going-to-the-Sun Road
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Going-to-the-Sun Road, a masterwork of engineering carved directly into the sheer alpine cliffs of the Continental Divide. You will climb through dense cedar forests before breaking out above tree line at Logan Pass, navigating tight switchbacks with dizzying drop-offs. The descent down the east side reveals windswept glacial valleys and the striking turquoise waters of St. Mary Lake.
days.stay: Stay in the St. Mary area right outside the park's eastern boundary, choosing between rustic cabins, comfortable motor lodges, or scenic campgrounds offering front-row seats to the dramatic mountain backdrop.

days.title: Return via the Rocky Mountain Front
days.summary: Return south along the rugged Rocky Mountain Front where the massive Lewis Range abruptly crashes into the rolling plains. US 89 provides an open, cinematic cruise past ranch lands and wide-open skies before cutting west on I-90 through the Blackfoot River valley. The contrast between towering limestone cliffs and endless horizon defines the essence of big sky country.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Missoula near the buzzing university district and riverfront parks, offering a vibrant mix of contemporary boutique hotels, historic inns, and comfortable lodges.

official.name: Going-to-the-Sun Road
official.description: Across Glacier National Park over Logan Pass, carved into the cliffs of the Garden Wall; open about July to mid October

roads.why: Universally celebrated as one of the most breathtaking alpine drives in North America, offering sheer cliff exposure, glacier-carved valleys, and crossing the Continental Divide at Logan Pass.
roads.drive: Narrow, two-lane road featuring steep 6% grades, sharp switchbacks, and rock overhangs with exposed drop-offs and no guardrails in historic sections. Heavy summer tourist traffic and vehicle length restrictions (under 21 feet) require patience, and driving east-to-west puts you on the mountain wall side.
roads.tips: Open typically from early July through mid-October depending on snowpack. Shuttle reservations or timed-entry vehicle permits are required during peak summer months. Fill up your tank before entering the park.

spots.name: Flathead Lake
spots.why: The largest natural freshwater lake west of the Mississippi in the contiguous US, offering sparkling glacier-fed waters framed by high mountain peaks.

spots.name: Bigfork, Montana
spots.why: A charming arts village nestled where the Swan River empties into Flathead Lake, featuring wooden boardwalks, local galleries, and great bakeries.

spots.name: Conrad Mansion Museum
spots.why: An impeccably preserved 1895 Victorian mansion built by Kalispell founder Charles E. Conrad, showcasing the opulent frontier history of the Flathead Valley.

spots.name: Apgar Village
spots.why: A picturesque lakeside village at the foot of Lake McDonald offering classic park cabins, general stores, and stunning waterfront reflections.

spots.name: Logan Pass
spots.why: The highest point on the road at 6,646 feet, serving as the trailhead for alpine hikes and offering prime mountain goat and bighorn sheep viewing.

spots.name: Jackson Glacier Overlook
spots.why: A dramatic roadside pullout providing a clear view of the massive Jackson Glacier clinging to the flanks of Mount Jackson.

spots.name: Choteau, Montana
spots.why: A historic frontier town known as the 'Front Porch of the Rockies' and a major hub for paleontological discoveries in the region.

spots.name: Giant Springs State Park
spots.why: Home to one of the largest freshwater springs in the country, pouring millions of gallons of crystal-clear water directly into the Missouri River.

plan.title: Skyline Drive and Blue Ridge Parkway
plan.summary: Drive south from Washington D.C. into the Blue Ridge Mountains, traversing the entire length of Skyline Drive through Shenandoah National Park. Continue onto the scenic Blue Ridge Parkway through Virginia and North Carolina to Asheville.

days.title: Into Shenandoah National Park
days.summary: Leave the traffic of Washington D.C. behind and climb onto the ridge for a masterclass in ridge-running views. Skyline Drive crests the Blue Ridge Mountains with sweeping vistas east over the Piedmont and west into the Shenandoah Valley. The curves are gentle and sweeping, offering an easy introduction to mountain driving before dropping down into Luray.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Luray near the main street or tucked against the mountain foothills, choosing between cozy historic B&Bs, traditional roadside lodges, or comfortable motels.

days.title: Through Shenandoah to Roanoke
days.summary: Continue south down the final stretches of Skyline Drive before seamlessly transitioning onto the northern reaches of the Blue Ridge Parkway. The road traces high ridges through dense hardwood forests and past rocky outcroppings like the Peaks of Otter. The drive feels remote, winding through deep hollows and offering endless blue-hazed mountain panoramas.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Roanoke near the historic city market district, featuring a mix of boutique hotels, renovated historic properties, and classic urban motels.

days.title: Blue Ridge Parkway to Galax
days.summary: Roll past high pastures and through the quirky, music-rich Appalachian plateau around Floyd before descending into the pastoral hills of Galax. This section of the Blue Ridge Parkway rewards drivers with rolling farmland views, slower-paced scenic cruising, and deep roots in traditional mountain culture. The curves open up, letting you settle into a relaxed rhythm.
days.stay: Stay close to downtown Galax or along the scenic byway approaches, choosing from cozy local motor inns, rustic rental cabins, or traditional B&Bs.

days.title: Into Asheville via Mount Mitchell
days.summary: Tackle the grand finale of the Parkway, climbing to its highest elevations as you skirt beneath the shadow of Mount Mitchell and wind around Grandfather Mountain. This is the most dramatic driving of the trip, featuring steep grades, tight engineering marvels like the Linn Cove Viaduct, and sheer drops. You finish by descending into the vibrant, creative hub of Asheville.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Asheville near the South Slope or historic Montford district, choosing among trendy boutique hotels, vibrant arts-district inns, or historic bed-and-breakfasts.

roads.name: Skyline Drive
roads.segment: from Front Royal to Rockfish Gap

official.name: Skyline Drive
official.description: Scenic drive through Shenandoah National Park

roads.why: Runs along the entire crest of Shenandoah National Park with nearly 75 overlooks providing uninterrupted views of the Shenandoah Valley and the Virginia Piedmont.
roads.drive: Strict 35 mph speed limit enforced by rangers, with rolling elevation changes and frequent wildlife crossings. Best driven southbound from Front Royal to Rockfish Gap.
roads.tips: Watch out for deer and bears, especially at dawn and dusk. Park entrance fee required. Foliage peaks in mid-to-late October.

roads.name: Blue Ridge Parkway

official.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
official.description: Scenic drive along America's longest linear park and the winding spine of the Blue Ridge Mountains

roads.why: America's longest linear park connects Shenandoah to the Great Smoky Mountains, offering legendary motorcycling and driving curves atop the highest ridges in the East.
roads.drive: Generally capped at 45 mph, featuring numerous tunnels, tight switchbacks, steep grades, and occasional sections prone to heavy fog and sudden cloud cover.
roads.tips: No commercial traffic allowed. Check for winter weather closures at high elevations. Gas stations are sparse directly on the parkway, so top off beforehand.

spots.name: Dickey Ridge Overlook
spots.why: Provides an immediate, stunning introduction to the northern Shenandoah Valley views just miles after entering the park.

spots.name: Stonyman Trail
spots.why: A short, rewarding hike through lush woods to a dramatic rocky summit with panoramic western vistas.

spots.name: Luray Caverns
spots.why: Explore massive subterranean chambers filled with towering stalactites and the famous world-playing Stalacpipe Organ.

spots.name: The Great Meadow
spots.why: A sprawling mountain basin that frequently attracts grazing white-tailed deer and soaring hawks against a dramatic skyline backdrop.

spots.name: Peaks of Otter
spots.why: Historic grouping of three sharp mountain peaks framing Abbott Lake with iconic vistas.

spots.name: Floyd Country Store
spots.why: A legendary roadside stop famous for traditional Appalachian comfort food and live Friday night Jamboree old-time music.

spots.name: Mabry Mill
spots.why: The most photographed spot on the entire parkway, featuring a rustic historic water-powered gristmill and blacksmith shop.

spots.name: Linn Cove Viaduct
spots.why: An engineering masterpiece that snakes gracefully around the rugged boulder-strewn flanks of Grandfather Mountain.

spots.name: Craggy Gardens
spots.why: Stunning high-elevation ridge walk through wind-swept rhododendrons and dramatic 360-degree mountain drop-offs.

spots.name: Biltmore Estate
spots.why: America's largest private home set amidst vast manicured gardens and rolling Blue Ridge foothills.

plan.title: New England Fall Foliage Loop
plan.summary: A 4-day autumn driving tour through Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Vermont, featuring the iconic Kancamagus Highway and the winding scenic byways of the White Mountains and Green Mountains.

days.title: From Boston to the White Mountains
days.summary: Leave the Boston traffic behind as you head north toward the Seacoast and into the pine-covered foothills of New Hampshire. The final stretch on NH-16 climbs gradually along the edge of the White Mountain National Forest, offering early previews of autumn foliage. It is an easy, scenic transition from the city to the mountains.
days.stay: Stay in downtown North Conway near the historic scenic railway or in a cozy mountain lodge just outside the bustle. You will find classic New England inns, family-run motels, and alpine resorts.

days.title: Across the Kancamagus and White Mountains
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Kancamagus Highway, a masterpiece of paved elevation changes that swoops through dense forests and over river valleys. The road is a continuous ribbon of sweeping curves, rolling hills, and dramatic lookouts framing endless seas of red, orange, and yellow canopy. It is widely considered one of the premier fall foliage drives in the United States.
days.stay: Stay in Lincoln near the western terminus of the Kancamagus, where you can unwind in a rustic timber-frame lodge or a comfortable roadside motel surrounded by towering peaks.

days.title: Into the Green Mountains of Vermont
days.summary: Roll west out of the mountains and cross the Connecticut River into the gentle, pastoral landscapes of Vermont's Green Mountains. You will sweep along high-speed interstate stretches before dropping onto curving country byways that thread through covered bridges and hillside farms. The light filtering through the changing leaves makes the Vermont hills look like an oil painting.
days.stay: Stay in Woodstock village near the historic town green, featuring upscale historic village inns, classic bed-and-breakfasts, and boutique country retreats.

days.title: Back to Boston via Connecticut River Valley
days.summary: Wind south along the scenic Connecticut River Valley before cutting across southern Massachusetts back toward Boston. The final hours blend relaxed valley cruising with faster highway miles as the rural landscape gradually gives way to suburban and urban sprawl. It is a smooth, satisfying conclusion to a quintessential New England loop.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Boston or the historic Back Bay area, choosing between grand historic hotels, modern high-rises, or stylish boutique properties.

roads.name: Kancamagus Scenic Byway

official.name: Kancamagus Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic drive through the heart of the White Mountains

roads.why: A purely scenic, federally designated highway cutting through a remote mountain pass with zero commercial development along its core stretch. Drivers love the continuous sweeping elevation changes and the breathtaking canyon vistas.
roads.drive: A well-paved, two-lane highway with steady, moderate grades and sweeping curves. No steep switchbacks or extreme exposure, but expect heavy leaf-peeping traffic and RVs during October weekends.
roads.tips: Drive it early in the morning to beat the crowds and catch the best morning light on the foliage. No gas stations on the highway, so fill up in Conway or Lincoln.

roads.name: White Mountain Trail
roads.segment: from North Conway through White Mountain National Forest

official.name: White Mountain Trail
official.description: Passes through the White Mountains and past Mount Washington

roads.why: An iconic loop that guides motorists past deep notches, roaring rivers, and the looming bulk of Mount Washington. The road delivers classic mountain scenery framed by towering granite cliffs and dense northern hardwoods.
roads.drive: Mixes fast highway sections with winding, rolling two-lane stretches through notches and river valleys. Watch for pedestrians near trailheads and sudden weather shifts in the higher elevations.
roads.tips: Peak foliage hits here earlier than the rest of the route, usually late September to early October. Check local weather for mountain fog.

roads.name: Connecticut River Byway

official.name: Connecticut River Byway
official.description: Scenic drive on both sides of New England's longest river

roads.why: Follows New England's longest river past historic riverside towns, fertile agricultural fields, and rolling hillsides. It offers a relaxed, picturesque driving experience away from major freight corridors.
roads.drive: A relaxed two-lane secondary highway with gentle bends, flat stretches, and occasional rolling hills. Very straightforward and easy to navigate.
roads.tips: Great alternative to the interstate when you want to take your time and explore local farm stands and antique shops.

spots.name: Portsmouth Harbor Trail
spots.why: A great coastal stretch to stretch your legs and grab coffee before heading inland toward the mountains.

spots.name: Diana's Baths
spots.why: A series of small waterfalls and rock pools nestled in the woods, reached via an easy, flat woodland walk.

spots.name: Settlers Green
spots.why: Convenient hub with plenty of local dining options and cafes right at the doorstep of the White Mountains.

spots.name: CPA
spots.why: Popular panoramic overlook offering sweeping views of the Swift River Valley and surrounding mountain ridges.

spots.name: Sabbaday Falls
spots.why: A gorgeous three-tiered waterfall accessible via a short, well-maintained forest trail with wooden bridges and stairs.

spots.name: Pemigewasset Overlook
spots.why: Perched near the western crest of the highway, this pullout looks out over miles of unbroken forest canopy.

spots.name: Quechee Gorge
spots.why: Vermont's deepest gorge carved by the Ottauquechee River, viewable from a high bridge and surrounding trails.

spots.name: Woodstock Village Green
spots.why: One of the most picturesque New England towns, featuring Federal-style architecture, a covered bridge, and local boutiques.

spots.name: Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park
spots.why: A historic conservation-themed park featuring managed forests, carriage roads, and sweeping hillside views.

spots.name: Windsor-Cornish Covered Bridge
spots.why: One of the longest wooden covered bridges in the world, spanning the Connecticut River between Vermont and New Hampshire.

spots.name: Brattleboro Food Co-op
spots.why: A vibrant local hub offering fresh Vermont cheeses, baked goods, and hot foods for a scenic roadside lunch.

spots.name: Old Sturbridge Village
spots.why: A massive outdoor living history museum depicting a 1830s New England rural community, located right off the Massachusetts Turnpike.

plan.title: New York City to Acadia National Park Coastal Drive
plan.summary: A 4-day coastal road trip heading north from New York City through New England, utilizing scenic shore routes and historic parkways up to the rugged mountains of Acadia National Park in Maine.

days.title: Through New England to Cape Cod
days.summary: Leave the city bustle behind for the lush, tree-lined curves of the Merritt Parkway, passing elegant stone bridges before cutting inland across Connecticut. The final push uses efficient interstates to get you down onto Cape Cod just as the light softens over the salt marshes.
days.stay: Stay right in Barnstable village near the harbor in a classic coastal B&B or historic inn.

days.title: Along Old Kings Highway to Boston and Portsmouth
days.summary: Cruise the historic Old Kings Highway through Cape Cod's quiet historic districts before making the big highway jump north toward Boston and up into Portsmouth. The driving balances scenic New England small towns with fast stretches of coastal interstate.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Portsmouth near the historic Prescott Park and the lively waterfront dining scene, choosing a boutique hotel or a restored colonial inn.

days.title: Down East Maine to Bar Harbor
days.summary: Sail up the Maine coastline on US-1, winding past rocky inlets, working harbors, and classic lighthouses through Down East Maine. The road alternates between fast modern bypasses and scenic coastal sections that demand a lighter foot on the throttle.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Bar Harbor within walking distance of the shore path, choosing a traditional coastal lodge or seaside inn.

days.title: Exploring Acadia National Park
days.summary: Tackle the classic coastal and mountain loops of Acadia National Park, where granite peaks drop straight down into the cold Atlantic. Expect a mix of sweeping ocean vistas, dense pine forests, and dramatic coastal granite.
days.stay: Stay in Bar Harbor to celebrate the end of your journey with fresh Maine lobster and easy access to the park's eastern entrance.

roads.name: Merritt Parkway

official.name: Merritt Parkway
official.description: Historic parkway through Connecticut's Gold Coast known for its elaborate Art Deco bridges

roads.why: Famous for its unique Art Deco concrete overpasses and deep woodland cuts that shield drivers from commercial sprawl.
roads.drive: Moderate traffic with gentle sweepers and rolling elevation changes; watch for short merging lanes at vintage on-ramps.
roads.tips: Avoid during morning and evening rush hours; commercial trucks are strictly prohibited.

roads.name: Old Kings Highway

official.name: Old Kings Highway (Route 6A)
official.description: Route through Cape Cod traversing numerous National Historic Districts

roads.why: One of America's great historical corridors, lined with centuries-old captains' houses and dense native canopies.
roads.drive: Two-lane local road with low speed limits, frequent pedestrian crossings, and tight residential clustering.
roads.tips: Drive in the morning to beat local tourist traffic and enjoy the dappled sunlight through the trees.

roads.name: Bold Coast Scenic Byway

official.name: Bold Coast Scenic Byway
official.description: Coastal route through Down East Maine to the Canadian border

roads.why: Delivers classic Maine coastal character, crossing tidal rivers, rocky headlands, and authentic fishing villages.
roads.drive: A mix of fast two-lane highway sections and slower village center runs with excellent long-range visibility.
roads.tips: Keep an eye out for sudden fog banks near Wiscasset and Ellsworth, especially in the late afternoon.

roads.name: Acadia All-American Road
roads.segment: from Hulls Cove to Seal Harbor

official.name: Acadia All-American Road
official.description: Scenic drive providing access to the coastal mountains of Acadia National Park

roads.why: An engineering masterpiece featuring historic granite guardrails and breathtaking panoramic mountain-to-ocean overlooks.
roads.drive: Hilly with some steep grades, tight coastal curves, and heavy pedestrian and cyclist presence during peak summer.
roads.tips: Vehicle reservations are required for Cadillac Mountain; drive the loop counterclockwise for the best ocean views.

spots.name: Greenwich Point Park
spots.why: A lovely peninsula offering early morning views across Long Island Sound before starting your road trip.

spots.name: Stct 169 Historic Corridor
spots.why: A designated scenic byway passing through quintessential Connecticut agricultural valleys and stone-wall farms.

spots.name: Sandy Neck Beach
spots.why: Six miles of pristine barrier beach dunes framing the entrance to Barnstable Harbor.

spots.name: Sandwich Glass Museum
spots.why: Celebrates the town's rich 19th-century glassmaking heritage with stunning blown-glass exhibits.

spots.name: The Freedom Trail
spots.why: A red-brick walking path leading through 16 historically significant sites in downtown Boston.

spots.name: Strawbery Banke Museum
spots.why: An outdoor history museum featuring centuries of preserved waterfront neighborhood architecture in Portsmouth.

spots.name: Portland Head Light
spots.why: Maine's oldest and most iconic lighthouse perched dramatically on a rugged headland in Cape Elizabeth.

spots.name: Red's Eats
spots.why: Legendary roadside shack famous for serving massive, overflowing fresh Maine lobster rolls.

spots.name: Cadillac Mountain
spots.why: The highest point along the North Atlantic seaboard offering the first sunrise view in the United States.

spots.name: Jordan Pond House
spots.why: Famous historic restaurant known for traditional popovers and tea overlooking a glacial tarn.

spots.name: Thunder Hole
spots.why: A natural rock inlet where incoming waves compress air and water to produce a thunderous roar.

plan.title: Texas Hill Country and Twisted Sisters Loop
plan.summary: This two-day weekend escape from Austin plunges deep into the rolling limestone canyons of the Texas Hill Country. You will tackle legendary motorcycling and driving favorites like the Twisted Sisters, pairing thrilling twists with authentic Hill Country hospitality.

days.title: From Austin to the Twisted Sisters and Leakey
days.summary: Leave the capital behind and cruise west past rolling oak-studded hills into Fredericksburg for a taste of German heritage and hill country hospitality. The afternoon ramps up on RM 337, sweeping you through dramatic limestone canyons and white-knuckle twisters all the way into Leakey. It is a legendary riding and driving playground that demands your full attention.
days.stay: Look for a rustic riverside cabin or a comfortable motel right along the Frio River in Leakey to soak in the peaceful evening atmosphere.

days.title: Through the Canyons Back to Austin
days.summary: Tackle the remaining legs of the Twisted Sisters, heading north on RM 335 and east on RM 336 over undulating ridges with vast panoramic ranchland views. Loop back through Bandera, the Cowboy Capital of the World, before hitting the fast highway stretches back to Austin. It is a high-mileage finale that trades tight canyons for wide-open Texas skies.
days.stay: Celebrate the end of your loop in Austin with a boutique hotel downtown or a lively spot near South Congress to enjoy the city's legendary food and music scene.

roads.name: Twisted Sisters
roads.segment: from Medina through Leakey to Camp Wood and across RM 335 and RM 336

official.name: Twisted Sisters
official.description: Ranch roads 335, 336 and 337 through the Texas Hill Country canyons around Leakey, a motorcycle favourite

roads.why: Comprising Ranch Roads 335, 336, and 337, this trio forms the holy grail of Texas driving with relentless elevation changes, blind crests, and tight sweepers carved through rugged limestone canyons.
roads.drive: Expect narrow lanes with little to no shoulder, steep grades up to 15 percent, and sharp switchbacks. Traffic is generally light on weekdays but heavy with motorcycles and sports cars on weekends; drive defensively and watch for loose gravel.
roads.tips: Ride or drive between October and April for ideal temperatures. Fill up your tank whenever you see a station, as services are extremely limited between small towns.

spots.name: Wildseed Farms
spots.why: A sprawling working wildflower farm offering local plants, walking trails, and a tasting room featuring blackberry wine.

spots.name: Fredericksburg Historic District
spots.why: Stroll down Main Street to explore 19th-century Sunday houses, unique German bakeries, and local boutiques.

spots.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area
spots.why: Famous for its vibrant bigtooth maples, towering canyon walls, and crisp spring-fed streams ideal for a short leg-stretch.

spots.name: Garner State Park
spots.why: A classic Hill Country retreat on the crystal-clear Frio River surrounded by towering cypress trees and rugged hills.

spots.name: Bandera Historic Courthouse
spots.why: Soak in the authentic cowboy culture in the self-proclaimed Cowboy Capital of the World, complete with rustic saloons and western storefronts.

plan.title: Arizona Red Rocks and Grand Canyon
plan.summary: A 3-day journey from the desert up to the red rocks of Sedona, the switchbacks of Oak Creek Canyon, and the majestic depths of the Grand Canyon.

days.title: Phoenix to Sedona via Red Rocks
days.summary: Leave the Phoenix sprawl behind on Interstate 17 as it climbs steadily onto the high Colorado Plateau, trading flat desert for rugged scrub-oak country. The real magic begins when you peel off onto the Red Rock Scenic Byway, where towering crimson monoliths rise sharply against the bright blue Arizona sky. It is a striking transition from city heat to cinematic desert grandeur as you drop into the valley surrounding Sedona.
days.stay: Look for lodging right in uptown Sedona or tucked away in the quieter Oak Creek area for easy access to the trails. Options range from rustic resort lodges and boutique motels to bed-and-breakfasts.

days.title: Sedona to Grand Canyon via Flagstaff
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Oak Creek Canyon drive as it twists aggressively up steep switchbacks through a heavily wooded gorge before opening up into the cool pine forests of Flagstaff. From there, head northwest across wide-open high desert flats toward the rim of the continent's most famous chasm. The afternoon rewards your driving efforts with your first sweeping, awe-inspiring glimpse into the colossal depths of the Grand Canyon.
days.stay: Stay directly inside the historic park village to catch the sunset and sunrise over the canyon rim, choosing between classic park lodges and rustic historic cabins.

days.title: Grand Canyon and Return
days.summary: Spend the morning soaking in the endless canyon overlooks along Desert View Drive or the Village rim before pointing your hood south toward Williams. Cruise down a scenic stretch of the old high-desert highway before jumping onto I-40 to finish the loop back into Flagstaff. It is an easy, relaxing driving finale that balances iconic roadside nostalgia with smooth high-speed cruising.
days.stay: Base yourself in downtown Flagstaff near the historic railroad district, where you will find a great mix of indie motels, converted brick hotels, and mountain lodges.

roads.name: Red Rock Scenic Byway

official.name: Red Rock Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic drive through the red sandstone canyons of the Coconino National Forest

roads.why: It serves up an immediate, unobstructed introduction to Arizona's famous red sandstone geology, cutting right past massive landmarks like Bell Rock and Courthouse Butte.
roads.drive: A smooth, well-paved two-lane highway with gentle curves, occasional roundabouts, and heavy tourist traffic midday. Drive northbound for the best frontal views of the red rocks.
roads.tips: Expect heavy congestion on weekends; visit early in the morning for clear light and light traffic. A Red Rock Pass is required if you park along the road for hikes.

roads.name: Oak Creek Canyon

official.name: Oak Creek Canyon
official.description: From Sedona up red-rock Oak Creek Canyon and the switchbacks to Flagstaff

roads.why: This classic mountain pass packs dramatic elevation changes, tight hairpin turns, and towering canyon walls covered in lush pine and sycamore trees into a few breathtaking miles.
roads.drive: Features a famous series of steep, tight switchbacks near the top of the canyon with dramatic drop-offs and narrow shoulders. South-to-north means you are climbing the cliff face.
roads.tips: Watch out for overheating engines on the climb, cyclists sharing the narrow lane, and slow-moving RVs. Early morning is the best time to drive before the tourist parking creates bottlenecks.

spots.name: Bell Rock
spots.why: A massive, bell-shaped sandstone formation right off the highway that makes an incredible first impression and popular vortex stop.

spots.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
spots.why: An architectural marvel built directly into the red rock cliffs, offering panoramic views over the surrounding valley.

info.title: Chapel of the Holy Cross (Sedona, Arizona)

spots.name: Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village
spots.why: A charming, Spanish-style arts village shaded by giant sycamore trees along Oak Creek, perfect for lunch or a coffee break.

spots.name: Slide Rock State Park
spots.why: A historic homestead and natural water slide carved into the slick red sandstone of Oak Creek.

spots.name: West Fork Trail
spots.why: Widely considered one of the best canyon walks in the Southwest, winding through a shaded gorge beneath towering cliff walls.

spots.name: Grand Canyon Visitor Center
spots.why: The ultimate introduction to the South Rim, providing your first footpath approach to the edge of the abyss.

spots.name: Mather Point
spots.why: A dramatic, jutting promontory offering one of the most expansive and accessible sunrise and sunset panoramas on the South Rim.

spots.name: Hopi House
spots.why: A historic structure designed by Mary Colter in 1904, built to mimic traditional Hopi pueblo architecture and showcasing Native American crafts.

spots.name: Grand Canyon Railway Depot
spots.why: A charming log-cabin style train station in downtown Williams that has welcomed rail travelers since the early 2000s and historic steam eras.

plan.title: Oregon Volcanic Peaks and Pacific Coast Loop
plan.summary: This 5-day driving enthusiast loop takes you from Portland through the high cascades of Mount Hood, down the dramatic Oregon volcanic legacy, to Crater Lake, and returns via the breathtaking Pacific Coast Scenic Byway and the scenic Columbia River Gorge.

days.title: Mount Hood and the Cascades
days.summary: Climb out of the Willamette Valley on the sweeping curves of the Mt. Hood Scenic Byway, passing dense pine forests and volcanic peaks before dropping into the high desert. The stretch over the pass offers grand alpine vistas, followed by an open, fast run down toward the high-desert plateau of Bend. It is a day of dramatic climate shifts from lush evergreen forests to dry ponderosa pines.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Bend or along the Deschutes River, choosing from trendy boutique motels, modern alpine lodges, or cozy local B&Bs.

days.title: Volcanic Legacy to Crater Lake
days.summary: Cruise south along the Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway across high-desert flats and evergreen timberlands before climbing steeply into the Cascade Range toward the caldera of Crater Lake. The rim drive treats drivers to sweeping, high-altitude curves perched high above deep blue volcanic waters. Finish with a smooth, fast descent through the southern timber country toward Klamath Falls.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Klamath Falls or near the lakefront, featuring classic roadside motels, comfortable inns, and quiet lakeside lodges.

days.title: Through the Southern Oregon Coast Range
days.summary: Cross the rugged Southern Oregon Coast Range on winding river highways before hitting the wild and dramatic Pacific Coast Scenic Byway. The southern Oregon coast delivers towering sea stacks, winding cliffside roads, and sweeping ocean views with very little traffic. The day blends technical river valley curves with classic coastal cruising.
days.stay: Stay in Coos Bay near the downtown waterfront or closer to the dunes, with choices ranging from historic coastal inns to reliable motels and ocean-view lodges.

days.title: North Along the Pacific Coast Highway
days.summary: Roll north along the Pacific Coast Scenic Byway past shifting sand dunes, rocky headlands, and endless ocean vistas. This classic highway rewards steady pacing with sweeping coastal curves, sweeping bridge crossings, and miles of dramatic shoreline. Expect a relaxing, scenic drive punctuated by historic coastal towns and dramatic lookouts.
days.stay: Stay near the beachfront or in the historic core of Lincoln City, choosing from classic beach motels, cozy coastal B&Bs, and full-service oceanfront resorts.

days.title: Return via the Oregon Coast and Columbia River
days.summary: Complete the loop by hugging the dramatic northern Oregon coast past massive capes and cheese country before turning inland along the mighty Columbia River. The final stretch on US 101 and the historic highway offers a mix of sweeping coastal curves and a fast, multi-lane interstate run back into Portland. It is a fittingly diverse grand finale to a world-class Pacific Northwest road trip.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Portland or the vibrant Pearl District, featuring historic boutique hotels, modern urban lodges, and upscale guesthouses.

roads.name: Mt. Hood Scenic Byway

official.name: Mt. Hood Scenic Byway
official.description: Provides scenic views of Mount Hood

roads.why: Offers a continuous climb through dense national forests with stunning lookouts of Oregon's highest peak.
roads.drive: Consistent grades and well-paved sweeping curves with good visibility; watch for weekend tourist traffic near Government Camp.
roads.tips: Best driven in the morning for clear mountain views; winter tires or chains may be required outside of summer.

roads.name: Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway

official.name: Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic drive through the Cascade Volcanic Arc

roads.why: Traverses the dramatic volcanic spine of the Cascades, linking high desert plateaus with alpine calderas.
roads.drive: Wide, fast high-desert straights transition into steep mountain climbs with tighter switchbacks around Crater Lake.
roads.tips: Crater Lake rim roads can hold snow well into July; check park service updates before heading up.

roads.name: Rogue-Umpqua Scenic Byway

official.name: Rogue-Umpqua Scenic Byway
official.description: Follows two scenic rivers through southwestern Oregon

roads.why: Follows roaring white-water rivers through narrow, tree-lined canyon gorges in the heart of the southern mountains.
roads.drive: Twisty, engaging road hugging the river banks with moderate elevation changes and occasional logging truck traffic.
roads.tips: Keep headlights on and watch for wet leaves and mist in shaded canyon corners.

roads.name: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway

official.name: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway-Oregon
official.description: Scenic drive along the entire length of Oregon's Pacific coast

roads.why: One of the world's great coastal drives, featuring towering sea stacks, dramatic cliffs, and endless ocean panoramas.
roads.drive: A mix of gentle sweepers and tight shelf roads carved into headlands; speeds vary from 35 to 55 mph.
roads.tips: Watch out for slow RVs and erratic drivers stopping suddenly at viewpoints; fuel up regularly in remote stretches.

plan.title: Door Peninsula and Lake Michigan Shore
plan.summary: A scenic three-day loop from Chicago up along the eastern shore of Lake Michigan and across to Wisconsin's picturesque Door Peninsula, returning down the Green Bay coast. Features great lakeside driving, charming coastal towns, and the Door County Coastal Byway.

days.title: Chicago to Door County via Lake Michigan Shore
days.summary: You head north out of the Chicago sprawl via I-94, bypassing Milwaukee traffic to pick up the open stretch of I-43 running parallel to Lake Michigan. After cutting past Green Bay, you transition onto WI-57 for a swift, smooth approach across the Sturgeon Bay ship canal into the gateway of the Door Peninsula. The drive evolves from heavy interstate commuter arteries into tranquil two-lane country roads framed by orchards and cedar forests.
days.stay: Stay in Sturgeon Bay near the historic downtown or along the waterfront ship canal, where you will find cozy boutique inns, local B&Bs, and classic lakeside motels.

days.title: Exploring the Door County Coastal Byway
days.summary: This day is all about the classic Door County Coastal Byway loop, tracing the dramatic limestone cliffs of the Niagara Escarpment on the Green Bay side and returning through the wilder, dune-swept shorelines of Lake Michigan. The driving is relaxed and scenic, characterized by winding canopy roads, sudden glimpses of blue water, and picturesque harbor villages. You will navigate rolling hills and shaded stretches that demand a slower pace and encourage frequent pullouts.
days.stay: Stay in Fish Creek close to Peninsula State Park, offering a range of rustic-charming lodges, woodland B&Bs, and cozy resort motels within walking distance of the water.

days.title: Green Bay and Return to Chicago
days.summary: You head south down the quiet spine of the peninsula on WI-42, tracing the shoreline through maritime towns before reconnecting with the high-speed efficiency of I-43 and I-94 for the return to Chicago. The morning offers a peaceful, low-traffic coastal cruise past lighthouses and beaches, while the afternoon settles into a straightforward interstate drive back into the heart of the city.
days.stay: Return to Chicago, staying in vibrant central neighborhoods like River North or the Loop, featuring full-service hotels, historic high-rises, and boutique urban properties.

roads.name: Door County Coastal Byway

official.name: Door County Coastal Byway
official.description: Loop along the coast of Green Bay and Lake Michigan, through the forests and Niagara Escarpment of Door County

roads.why: This designated national scenic byway loops the entire Door Peninsula, offering an incredible contrast between the sheltered, sunset-facing Green Bay coast and the rugged, wave-battered Lake Michigan shore.
roads.drive: A mix of smooth two-lane state highways and winding county roads with gentle curves, rolling terrain, and shaded tree canopies. Traffic can be heavy with tourists during summer weekends, so patience is required.
roads.tips: Peak foliage in mid-to-late October brings heavy traffic; early morning drives offer the best light and empty roads. Fuel is readily available in every major town.

plan.title: Florida Keys Overseas Highway Getaway
plan.summary: A leisurely two-day coastal drive down the famous Florida Keys Scenic Highway from Miami to Key West, crossing dozens of open-ocean bridges and tropical island communities.

days.title: Miami to Marathon
days.summary: Leave the sprawl of Miami behind as you cross onto the Overseas Highway, stretching over turquoise waters and island hopping through the upper and middle Keys. The best stretch is the iconic Seven Mile Bridge, where you feel completely suspended between the Atlantic and the Gulf. It is a classic tropical cruise of a drive, flanked by swaying palms and endless blue horizons.
days.stay: Stay in the heart of Marathon near the harbor, where you will find a mix of relaxed waterfront motels, quiet island inns, and fishing lodges.

days.title: Marathon to Key West
days.summary: Continue down the remainder of the island chain past remote keys and mangrove forests before arriving at the vibrant end of the road. The best driving is found on the smaller historic bridges connecting the lower keys, offering sweeping ocean vistas on both sides. The day culminates in the electric, laid-back atmosphere of Key West.
days.stay: Stay in Key West near Old Town within walking distance of Mallory Square, featuring historic conch house guesthouses, boutique bed and breakfasts, and classic island inns.

roads.name: Florida Keys Scenic Highway
roads.segment: from Key Largo to Key West

official.name: Florida Keys Scenic Highway
official.description: Scenic route across a system of open ocean bridges connecting the numerous tropical islands of the Florida Keys

roads.why: It is one of the most famous drives in the world, carrying you across a string of coral islands via an incredible series of 42 bridges over open ocean.
roads.drive: Completely flat with straight stretches and sweeping bridge approaches, subject to heavy tourist traffic and strict speed limits, best driven heading south with the afternoon sun over the water.
roads.tips: Watch out for speed traps near settlements, fuel up before hitting the longer bridge stretches, and drive during midday for the best turquoise water colors.

plan.title: Sierra Nevada Alpine Loop
plan.summary: This 4-day loop takes you from San Francisco into the heart of Yosemite National Park, over the high-altitude Tioga Pass, and north along the Eastern Sierra to Lake Tahoe. Experience world-class alpine vistas, dramatic granite canyons, and legendary mountain passes.

days.title: Into Yosemite Valley
days.summary: Leave the Bay Area behind and power through the Central Valley before climbing into the stunning foothills of the Sierra Nevada. The final approach on CA-120 offers sweeping canyon views as you wind your way past groves of pines and deep into the dramatic granite heart of Yosemite Valley. The driving shifts from mundane highway cruising to rolling, rhythmic mountain curves that set the stage for alpine adventure.
days.stay: Stay right in the heart of the valley within walking distance of the major monoliths, choosing between historic rustic lodges, canvas tent cabins, or nearby campsites nestled beneath towering pines.

days.title: Over Tioga Pass to Lee Vining
days.summary: Conquer one of the highest and most breathtaking mountain passes in California as you ascend Tioga Road out of Yosemite. The landscape rapidly transforms from dense forests to stark, otherworldly sub-alpine granite wilderness dotted with crystal-clear lakes. After cresting the summit at nearly 10,000 feet, you will plunge down the dramatic eastern escarpment toward the high desert moonscape of Mono Lake.
days.stay: Look for a quiet, retro roadside motel or a cozy cabin tucked into the dramatic high-desert landscape near the shores of Mono Lake.

days.title: North to Lake Tahoe
days.summary: Head north along the eastern shadow of the Sierra Nevada on a fast, scenic highway framed by massive jagged peaks to your left and volcanic basins to your right. The route climbs through rolling ranch lands and mountain passes before delivering you to the deep blue alpine bowl of Lake Tahoe. It is a fantastic day of cruising wide-open high-desert straights that transition smoothly into pine-scented mountain sweepers.
days.stay: Base yourself on the bustling south shore of the lake, where lively casino-hotels, alpine lodges, and cozy mountain inns offer easy access to both the water and the surrounding peaks.

days.title: Return via Silicon Valley
days.summary: Descend the western slopes of the Sierra via sweeping alpine curves on CA-88 before transitioning onto the swift highways that bridge the Central Valley and Silicon Valley. The drive offers a brilliant mix of challenging mountain descents with excellent sightlines, followed by an efficient highway run back to the Bay. It is a satisfying loop that takes you from sea level to the high alpine and back in just a few days.
days.stay: Celebrate the end of your alpine loop by staying in a vibrant neighborhood like the Mission or near Alamo Square, choosing from boutique hotels or classic urban inns.

roads.name: Tioga Road
roads.segment: from Groveland to Lee Vining through Yosemite National Park

official.name: Tioga Road/Big Oak Flat Road
official.description: High mountain pass through Yosemite National Park

roads.why: This is one of America's premier alpine drives, offering uninterrupted views of granite domes, jagged peaks, pristine glacial lakes, and sweeping sub-alpine meadows.
roads.drive: Expect a well-paved two-lane mountain highway with sustained steep grades, tight switchbacks near the pass, and occasional steep drop-offs without guardrails. Traffic can be heavy with RVs and slow-moving tourists, so patience is required.
roads.tips: Open typically from late May or June through November depending on snowpack. Fill up your tank before entering the park as there is no reliable fuel inside.

official.name: Eastern Sierra Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic route past natural landmarks like the Inyo National Forest, Sierra Nevada mountains, Sequoia National Forest, Mono Lake, and the Owens Valley

roads.why: Stretching along the base of the eastern Sierra Nevada, this route provides jaw-dropping vistas of some of the highest and most dramatic mountain escarpments in the contiguous United States.
roads.drive: A fast, wide, and well-maintained US highway with long sweeping straights and gentle rolling grades that allow for relaxed, highly scenic cruising.
roads.tips: Watch out for sudden crosswinds and local wildlife, especially deer. Keep an eye on fuel levels as remote stretches can have widely spaced stations.

plan.summary: A 4-day driving loop from Los Angeles through the Mojave Desert, across Death Valley National Park, north along the dramatic Eastern Sierra on US 395, and back south via the Angeles Crest Highway.

days.title: Into Death Valley
days.summary: Leave the sprawl of Los Angeles behind via I-15 before plunging into the stark, otherworldly expanses of the Mojave Desert and Death Valley. The highlight is the dramatic descent into the basin via CA-127 and CA-190, transitioning from barren ranges to the lowest and hottest place in North America. The feel of the day is an epic transition from urban congestion to absolute, silent isolation.
days.stay: Stay in the historic oasis at the center of the park, featuring classic desert resort lodges and ranch-style accommodations that serve as the main hub for travelers.

days.title: Across the Desert to Lone Pine
days.summary: Drive across the floor of Death Valley past salt flats and sand dunes before climbing steeply out of the basin over Panamint Pass. Once past the mountains, the route opens up into the dramatic Owens Valley framed by the towering wall of the Sierra Nevada. The day offers an astonishing contrast between deep desert depressions and alpine giants.
days.stay: Stay in the historic mountaineering town nestled right beneath the sheer eastern face of Mount Whitney, offering classic motels, outdoor lodges, and climber-friendly inns.

days.title: Along the Eastern Sierra
days.summary: Cruise north on US-395, one of the finest driving highways in the American West, running parallel to the jagged Sierra crest. You will pass volcanic fields, ancient lakes, and groves of giant aspens as you ascend toward the high-altitude resort community of Mammoth Lakes. The driving here is fast, smooth, and framed by jaw-dropping mountain backdrops.
days.stay: Stay in the alpine village area of Mammoth Lakes, featuring a wide selection of resort condos, ski lodges, and comfortable mountain motels.

days.title: Back to Los Angeles over Angeles Crest
days.summary: The final stretch combines a high-speed cruise down US-395 past Mono Lake with one of the most legendary motorcycle and sports car roads in Southern California: the Angeles Crest Highway. You will tackle endless sweeping curves, deep canyons, and towering ridge lines before descending back into the Los Angeles basin. It is a thrilling finale that moves from high desert to alpine forest and finally back to the city.
days.stay: Stay in the heart of Los Angeles in trendy central neighborhoods or near the Westside, ranging from boutique design hotels to classic urban lodgings.

roads.name: Death Valley Scenic Byway
roads.segment: from Death Valley Junction through Furnace Creek to Panamint Springs

official.name: Death Valley Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic drive through the expansive desert basin of the lowest place in North America

roads.why: Offers a surreal driving experience through vast salt pans, eroded badlands, and stark mountain ranges dropping thousands of feet below sea level.
roads.drive: Generally wide and well-paved, but features long sustained grades, sharp dips, and extreme heat that tests vehicle cooling systems. Watch for flash flood dips.
roads.tips: Avoid summer due to extreme heat; fill up with fuel at every opportunity as gas stations are sparse and expensive inside the park.

roads.name: Eastern Sierra Scenic Byway
roads.segment: from Lone Pine past Bishop to Mammoth Lakes and Lee Vining

official.name: Eastern Sierra Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic route past natural landmarks like the Inyo National Forest, Sierra Nevada mountains, Sequoia National Forest, Mono Lake, and the Owens Valley

roads.why: Widely regarded as one of the most scenic driving corridors in the United States, running directly beneath the sheer eastern escarpment of the Sierra Nevada.
roads.drive: High-speed multi-lane and two-lane highway with gentle sweepers, excellent pavement, and minimal traffic outside of peak holiday weekends.
roads.tips: Keep an eye on weather in winter and spring when mountain passes can experience sudden snow squalls. Watch for deer at dusk.

roads.name: Angeles Crest Highway (CA 2)
roads.segment: from Wrightwood to La Cañada Flintridge
roads.why: A masterpiece of mountain engineering with continuous tight radius turns, steep elevation changes, and panoramic views stretching from the Mojave Desert to downtown LA.
roads.drive: Technical and demanding with steep drop-offs, numerous switchbacks, and no guardrails in many sections. Popular with sports cars and motorcyclists, so watch out for fast traffic.
roads.tips: Check Caltrans for winter closures due to snow near Dawson Saddle; heavily patrolled by CHP on weekends.

spots.name: Zabriskie Point
spots.why: A classic viewpoint overlooking a maze of golden, highly eroded badland hills with the Panamint Range in the background.

spots.name: Badwater Basin
spots.why: Walk out onto the surreal, endless hexagonal salt polygons at the lowest point in North America, 282 feet below sea level.

spots.name: Furnace Creek Visitor Center
spots.why: The central hub of the national park where you can check current road conditions and view the iconic outdoor thermometer.

spots.name: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
spots.why: Waving sand dunes surrounded by dramatic mountain peaks, offering exceptional morning lighting for photography.

info.title: Places of interest in the Death Valley area

spots.name: Alabama Hills
spots.why: A unique landscape of rounded movie-set rock formations sitting right against the towering granite wall of Mount Whitney.

spots.name: Lo-In Cafe
spots.why: A classic local diner in Lone Pine serving hearty American comfort food and great milkshakes after a day in the desert.

spots.name: Manzanar National Historic Site
spots.why: A poignant historical site preserving one of the ten concentration camps where Japanese Americans were incarcerated during WWII.

spots.name: Coombs Hot Spring
spots.why: Natural geothermal pools nestled in the Owens Valley offering a relaxing soak with views of the Eastern Sierra.

spots.name: Devil's Postpile National Monument
spots.why: An unusual geological formation of symmetrical basalt columns created by a cooling lava flow thousands of years ago.

spots.name: Mono Lake Tufa State Natural Reserve
spots.why: Explore the eerie, otherworldly limestone tufa towers rising out of an ancient, hyper-saline inland sea.

spots.name: WooDee Diner
spots.why: A beloved stop near the mountain communities for coffee, burgers, and classic road trip atmosphere.

spots.name: Newcomb's Ranch
spots.why: The legendary historic weekend gathering spot for motorists and motorcyclists tackling the Angeles Crest Highway.

plan.title: Canadian Rockies Grand Loop
plan.summary: A stunning 4-day alpine loop from Calgary through Banff, Lake Louise, the majestic Icefields Parkway, and Jasper, returning via David Thompson Highway. Experience dramatic peaks, turquoise glacial lakes, and some of the world's greatest mountain drives.

days.title: Into Banff and Lake Louise
days.summary: Leave Calgary behind on the fast Trans-Canada before peeling off onto the quieter Bow Valley Parkway, tracking the river beneath jagged limestone peaks. The afternoon takes you through Banff National Park toward the iconic turquoise waters of Lake Louise. It is a classic Canadian Rockies introduction blending easy freeway cruising with scenic alpine byways.
days.stay: Look for mountain lodges, cabins, or historic chophouse-style hotels clustered near the lake or village center, offering a classic alpine atmosphere. Expect high demand and premium pricing throughout the summer season.

days.title: The Icefields Parkway to Jasper
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Icefields Parkway north toward Jasper, a sublime stretch of tarmac cutting deep between massive glaciers and rock walls. You will climb past iridescent blue lakes and sprawling icefields with sweeping pullouts designed to let the sheer scale sink in. The driving is effortless on a well-paved highway, though you will want to keep speeds moderate to soak in the endless views.
days.stay: Base yourself in the mountain town of Jasper, choosing between cozy alpine chalets, wooded cabins, or comfortable village motels. Book well in advance as options are limited within the national park boundaries.

days.title: Jasper to Abraham Lake
days.summary: Retrace your tracks south down the Icefields Parkway before hanging a left onto the dramatic David Thompson Highway along Abraham Lake. This quieter mountain corridor features sweeping curves, dramatic river valleys, and far fewer crowds than the main parks. The afternoon flattens out slightly as you drop out of the alpine and into the rugged pine forests near Nordegg.
days.stay: Stay in rustic wilderness lodges, forest cabins, or local motels around Nordegg and the surrounding foothills. Accommodations here are much more laid-back and outdoors-oriented compared to Banff or Jasper.

days.title: Back to Calgary via Cowboy Trail
days.summary: Head south along the Cowboy Trail, rolling through vast ranchlands where the prairie meets the dramatic eastern wall of the Rockies. The road winds through historic ranch towns and wide-open foothills with sweeping vistas of cattle country before curving back into Calgary. It is an easy, scenic driving day that trades alpine peaks for rolling golden pastures.
days.stay: Book a trendy boutique hotel or upscale high-rise in downtown Calgary or vibrant neighborhoods like Kensington or Inglewood. You will find everything from luxury modern builds to historic inns.

roads.name: Icefields Parkway

official.name: Icefields Parkway
official.description: Lake Louise to Jasper along the Continental Divide past Bow Lake, Peyto Lake and the Columbia Icefield, one of the world's great drives

roads.why: Widely considered one of the absolute greatest road trips on earth, linking Banff and Jasper through a continuous gauntlet of jagged peaks, ancient icefields, and emerald lakes.
roads.drive: A pristine two-lane highway with wide shoulders, long sweeping sweepers, and steady mountain grades. Watch out for tour buses, RVs, and wildlife wandering onto the tarmac.
roads.tips: Gas stations are extremely limited along this 230-kilometre stretch, so fill up before you leave Lake Louise or Jasper. Cell service is non-existent.

roads.name: Bow Valley Parkway

official.name: Bow Valley Parkway
official.description: Slower, wildlife-rich alternative to the Trans-Canada between Banff and Lake Louise, past Johnston Canyon

roads.why: This slower alternative to the main highway hugs the base of Castle Mountain and offers a more intimate encounter with the valley floor. It is famous for high probabilities of wildlife sightings, including bighorn sheep, elk, and bears.
roads.drive: Narrower two-lane road with lower speed limits, gentle curves, and numerous pullouts. Expect heavy bicycle traffic and slow drivers rubbernecking for animals.
roads.tips: Seasonal vehicle restrictions apply on certain sections during spring to protect wildlife corridors. Drive early in the morning for the best chance of spotting wildlife.

roads.name: David Thompson Highway
roads.segment: from Saskatchewan River Crossing to Rocky Mountain House

official.name: David Thompson Highway
official.description: Saskatchewan River Crossing to Nordegg past turquoise Abraham Lake, the quiet back door into the Rockies

roads.why: The rugged, less-traveled back door to the Rockies that treats drivers to stunning roadside views of the violently turquoise, wind-swept Abraham Lake and deep river canyons.
roads.drive: Fast, rolling two-lane highway with excellent pavement, light traffic, and sweeping curves that make for an engaging and relaxed drive.
roads.tips: Wind gusts can be exceptionally strong near Abraham Lake, so keep both hands on the wheel of high-profile vehicles.

roads.name: Cowboy Trail
roads.segment: from Rocky Mountain House to Longview

official.name: Cowboy Trail
official.description: Foothills ranch country west of Calgary along the Rockies, through Longview, Black Diamond and Turner Valley

roads.why: A fantastic foothills route that captures the authentic spirit of western Canada, running parallel to the front ranges of the Rockies through historic ranch country.
roads.drive: Rolling two-lane highway with gentle elevation changes, long straightaways, and stunning western views of the mountains.
roads.tips: Watch for slow-moving farm machinery and livestock near the highway, especially around Longview and Turner Valley.

spots.name: Cochrane RancheHouse
spots.why: Historic ranch site overlooking the Bow River valley, marking your official transition out of the city and into the foothills.

spots.name: Johnston Canyon
spots.why: A breathtaking walk along steel catwalks bolted directly into vertical limestone walls above a rushing turquoise river and deep gorge.

spots.name: Lake Louise
spots.why: The quintessential postcard view of bright turquoise glacial water backed by the towering Victoria Glacier.

spots.name: Crowfoot Glacier
spots.why: A dramatic roadside viewpoint showcasing a massive hanging glacier clinging to Crowfoot Mountain.

spots.name: Peyto Lake
spots.why: Features a short uphill walk to an overlook revealing a bright turquoise lake shaped remarkably like a wolf.

spots.name: Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre
spots.why: The prime base to view the Athabasca Glacier and learn about the massive hydrological reserve feeding three oceans.

spots.name: Athabasca Falls
spots.why: A powerful, thunderous waterfall forcing its way through a narrow gorge of ancient quartzite rock.

spots.name: Sunwapta Falls
spots.why: A stunning twin-channel waterfall plunging into a deep limestone canyon framed by dense alpine forest.

spots.name: Big Bend viewpoint
spots.why: Offers an impressive panoramic look at the massive hairpin curve of the Icefields Parkway against sheer mountain walls.

spots.name: Abraham Lake
spots.why: Famous for its striking artificial turquoise waters set against the dramatic backdrop of the David Thompson range.

spots.name: Nordegg Heritage Centre
spots.why: Fascinating museum detailing the coal-mining history of this remote foothills community.

spots.name: Rocky Mountain House National Historic Site
spots.why: Explore reconstructed fur-trade posts and the history of explorers like David Thompson along the North Saskatchewan River.
spots.wiki: Rocky Mountain House National Historic Site

spots.name: Longview jerky shop
spots.why: Legendary roadside stop famous for its massive selection of locally made beef jerky and authentic small-town atmosphere.

spots.name: Okotoks Erratic
spots.why: A massive, multi-ton quartzite boulder transported by ancient glaciers onto the flat prairie landscape.
