plan.title: Vancouver Island Wild Coast Road Trip
plan.summary: A 3-day driving adventure across Vancouver Island, tackling the winding Malahat Drive and the rugged Pacific Rim Highway through ancient rainforests to the wild shores of Tofino.

days.title: Victoria to Ucluelet
days.summary: Leave Victoria behind and climb the twisty Malahat Drive before cutting across the rugged spine of Vancouver Island through ancient forests. The Pacific Rim Highway takes over for the final stretch, offering a sweeping, roller-coaster descent toward the wild, wave-battered west coast. It is a transition from pastoral southern valleys to raw, moody coastal wilderness.
days.stay: Base yourself on the rocky outer edge of town or near the small boat harbor for prime access to the rugged coastline and wild beaches. Lodging ranges from rustic oceanfront lodges and independent motels to upscale rainforest resorts and private B&Bs.

days.title: Ucluelet to Ucluelet
days.summary: Spend the day exploring the immediate surroundings of the rugged west coast, navigating short spur roads that lead to hidden trailheads and dramatic headlands. The driving is relaxed and local, punctuated by frequent stops at surf beaches and misty rainforest boardwalks. The atmosphere is entirely laid-back, dictated by the rhythm of the Pacific tides.
days.stay: Return to your western coastal base for a second night, letting you settle in without packing bags. Choose a cozy lodge with a wood-burning stove or an ocean-facing cabin tucked into the cedar trees.

days.title: Ucluelet to Victoria
days.summary: Retrace your tracks eastward along the Pacific Rim Highway, marveling at how the massive Douglas firs and mountain passes look completely different in morning light. Drop down to the east coast at Nanaimo before cruising down the Malahat Highway back to Victoria. The contrast between the moody west coast and the sunnier, sheltered eastern shore defines the final push home.
days.stay: Finish back in the provincial capital around the historic Inner Harbour or heritage districts. Accommodation options here include grand historic hotels, charming Victorian bed-and-breakfasts, and modern waterfront apartments.

roads.name: Malahat Drive

official.name: Malahat Drive
official.description: The Trans-Canada's climb over the Malahat north of Victoria, with lookouts over Saanich Inlet

roads.why: It is the classic gateway out of Victoria, offering sweeping elevation gains and occasional glimpses of the Saanich Inlet through the dense evergreens. Enthusiasts appreciate the recently upgraded median-divided highway that still retains enough brisk sweepers to keep things engaging.
roads.drive: A well-paved, multi-lane highway with steady climbs and descents, featuring notable vertical grade changes. Traffic can be heavy during morning and evening commuter hours, so timing your run mid-morning is ideal.
roads.tips: Watch out for wildlife and sudden fog patches over the summit. Fuel up in Victoria or Langford before heading north.

roads.name: Pacific Rim Highway

official.name: Pacific Rim Highway
official.description: Across Vancouver Island from Parksville past Cathedral Grove and Kennedy Lake to Tofino and Ucluelet

roads.why: A legendary Vancouver Island route that cuts through the dramatic Beaufort Range and hugs the shores of massive alpine lakes before winding through old-growth temperate rainforests. Drivers love the relentless series of tight curves, steep roller-coaster sections, and moody coastal microclimates.
roads.drive: Paved two-lane highway with significant vertical climbs, sharp hairpin turns, and occasional narrow shoulders. The section through Kennedy Lake and Junction to Tofino demands continuous concentration and patience behind slower tourist traffic.
roads.tips: Prone to heavy winter storm damage, seasonal delays, and summer congestion. Fuel stations are sparse once you pass Port Alberni, so top up before heading west.

spots.name: Goldstream Provincial Park
spots.why: A stunning pocket of ancient Douglas fir and western red cedar right off the highway, featuring impressive waterfalls and dramatic canyon walls.

spots.name: Honeymoon Bay
spots.why: Provides a gorgeous elevated vantage over the shimmering waters of Sproat Lake as you transition into the rugged interior mountains.

spots.name: Wild Pacific Trail
spots.why: An awe-inspiring coastal walk hugging the jagged cliffs of the Ucluelet peninsula, offering dramatic wave-crash viewpoints and gnarled shore pines.

spots.name: Ucluelet Aquarium
spots.why: A fantastic catch-and-release marine discovery center highlighting the rich biodiversity of Barkley Sound's cold-water ecosystems.

spots.name: Long Beach, Pacific Rim National Park Reserve
spots.why: The ultimate sweeping expanse of pounding surf and white sand backed by lush temperate rainforest, world-famous for storm watching and beachcombing.

spots.name: Radar Hill
spots.why: A short drive and walk up to a historic WWII radar site providing panoramic views across Clayoquot Sound and the outer islands.

spots.name: Cathedral Grove
spots.why: Walk among Douglas fir trees that are over 800 years old and measure up to nine meters in circumference in this breathtaking roadside forest.

spots.name: Coombs Old Country Market
spots.why: Famous for its quirky grass-roofed market where goats graze overhead, offering incredible fresh baked goods, gelato, and local treats.

spots.name: Nanaimo Harbour
spots.why: A vibrant eastern-shore waterfront offering sweeping views across the Strait of Georgia toward the mainland mountains.

plan.title: Ontario to Quebec Scenic Arc
plan.summary: A delightful grand tour from Toronto through the lush forests of Algonquin Park, along the island-dotted St. Lawrence, and over the dramatic coastal rollercoasters of Charlevoix.

days.title: Into the Heart of Algonquin
days.summary: Escape Toronto's concrete grid via ON 11 before diving into the Canadian Shield on ON 60. The highlight is the sweeping parkway corridor through Algonquin Provincial Park, where dense pine forests and pristine lakes unfold around every bend. Expect smooth asphalt, rolling hills, and a classic wilderness feel.
days.stay: Immerse yourself fully in nature by staying at a rustic woodland lodge, backcountry cabin, or well-equipped campground right inside or just outside the park gates.

days.title: East to the Ottawa Valley
days.summary: Cruise eastward out of the park along the fast-flowing Madawaska valley on ON 60, transitioning smoothly toward the rugged Ottawa River watershed. The drive features wide-open stretches mixed with rolling farmland and forested ridges, keeping the pace relaxed and scenic.
days.stay: Unwind in Pembroke's riverside motels or cozy local inns situated close to the historic downtown and the shores of the majestic Ottawa River.

days.title: Down to the Thousand Islands
days.summary: Head south through the agricultural expanse of the Ottawa Valley before joining the gorgeous Loyalist Parkway through Prince Edward County. The final stretch treats you to a charming lake crossing on the Glenora Ferry and tranquil lakeside views right into Kingston.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Kingston within walking distance of the historic limestone architecture, vibrant waterfront, and bustling local bistros, choosing between boutique hotels or charming B&Bs.

days.title: St. Lawrence River to Montreal
days.summary: Follow the heritage-rich Thousand Islands Parkway as it hugs the St. Lawrence River past grand island estates and shimmering blue water. Afterward, merge onto fast regional highways to make good time toward the vibrant, cosmopolitan energy of Montreal.
days.stay: Book a trendy boutique hotel or upscale urban apartment in downtown Montreal or the historic Old Port, keeping you steps away from world-class dining and nightlife.

days.title: Historic Chemin du Roy
days.summary: Step back in time by cruising Canada's oldest route, Chemin du Roy (QC 138), as it winds along the north shore of the St. Lawrence River. You will pass through centuries-old French-Canadian villages, historic stone churches, and sweeping river vistas with minimal traffic.
days.stay: Experience authentic Quebec hospitality by staying in a historic downtown inn or a charming heritage B&B in Trois-Rivières overlooking the river.

days.title: Into the Charlevoix
days.summary: Head northeast on QC 138, climbing steadily out of the St. Lawrence lowlands toward the dramatic Laurentian Highlands. The road cuts through rugged shield country before dropping sharply into the artistic sanctuary of Baie-Saint-Paul nestled in a dramatic glacial crater.
days.stay: Indulge in a scenic mountainside resort, cozy chalet, or artistic village inn in Baie-Saint-Paul featuring stunning views of the St. Lawrence estuary.

days.title: The Charlevoix Rollercoaster to Quebec City
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Charlevoix Rollercoaster (QC 362) from Baie-Saint-Paul to La Malbaie, a rollercoaster of sheer cliffs, hairpin turns, and soaring panoramic views high above the St. Lawrence. Finish the journey by cruising southwest on fast divided highways straight into the heart of historic Quebec City.
days.stay: Celebrate the end of your road trip by staying in a historic European-style hotel inside the iconic fortified walls of Old Quebec.

roads.name: Highway 60 through Algonquin

official.name: Highway 60 through Algonquin
official.description: The Parkway Corridor across Algonquin Provincial Park, lakes and forest with moose sightings and famous fall colour

roads.why: It is the classic gateway across Ontario's most famous wilderness, offering endless vistas of pine forests, granite shields, and pristine lakes with frequent wildlife sightings.
roads.drive: A smooth, well-maintained two-lane highway with gentle rolling grades and clear sightlines, though reduced speed limits apply inside the park to protect wildlife.
roads.tips: Watch out for moose licking salt off the road in spring; autumn brings peak leaf-peeping traffic jams, so arrive early.

roads.name: Loyalist Parkway

official.name: Loyalist Parkway
official.description: Along Lake Ontario from Trenton through Prince Edward County to Kingston, with the Glenora ferry

roads.why: This historic drive bypasses the highway rush to showcase the bucolic charm of Prince Edward County, limestone heritage homes, and vineyards.
roads.drive: An easygoing secondary route featuring flat to gently rolling terrain, peaceful rural stretches, and a classic cable ferry crossing.
roads.tips: Factor in wait times for the Glenora Ferry during peak summer weekends, and watch for slow-moving farm vehicles.

roads.name: Thousand Islands Parkway

official.name: Thousand Islands Parkway
official.description: Along the St. Lawrence River between Gananoque and Brockville, past the Thousand Islands

roads.why: It runs right alongside the island-studded St. Lawrence River, offering sparkling water views and glimpses of opulent Gilded Age mansions.
roads.drive: A leisurely, scenic alternative to the 401 freeway, featuring smooth asphalt, wide shoulders, and a parallel paved multi-use recreational trail.
roads.tips: Speed limits are strictly enforced; keep your camera ready for the many well-maintained riverfront turnouts and picnic spots.

roads.name: Chemin du Roy

official.name: Chemin du Roy
official.description: Canada's oldest road, along the north shore of the St. Lawrence from Montreal to Quebec City through historic villages

roads.why: Established in 1737, it is Canada's oldest highway, connecting historic French-Canadian parishes, colonial architecture, and river views.
roads.drive: A flat, low-stress coastal road that winds through the main streets of historic villages with frequent stop signs and local traffic.
roads.tips: Take your time to explore the heritage interpretive plaques and local bakeries along the route rather than rushing.

roads.name: Route 362 in Charlevoix

official.name: Route 362 in Charlevoix
official.description: Rollercoaster coast road from Baie-Saint-Paul to La Malbaie high above the St. Lawrence

roads.why: Famously dubbed the Charlevoix Rollercoaster, it clings to steep cliffs high above the St. Lawrence River with heart-stopping panoramic drops.
roads.drive: A thrilling succession of dramatic elevation changes, blind crests, sweeping curves, and sharp switchbacks best driven west-to-east or vice versa for maximum views.
roads.tips: Exercise caution in wet or icy weather due to steep grades; engine braking is recommended for manual or heavy vehicles.

spots.name: Lake of Two Rivers, Algonquin Park
spots.why: A stunning wide-open sandy beach and lake vista surrounded by dense boreal forest, perfect for a quick leg stretch.

spots.name: Algonquin Logging Museum
spots.why: An outdoor interpretive trail featuring reconstructed logging camps, an authentic steam alligator tug, and rich local history.

spots.name: Algonquin Visitor Centre
spots.why: Features world-class exhibits on park ecology and a massive observation deck overlooking a breathtaking spruce bog valley.

spots.name: Petawawa National Forestry Institute Trail
spots.why: Offers peaceful nature walks through diverse pine plantations and mixed forests right near the Ottawa River valley.

spots.name: Pembroke Waterfront
spots.why: Features stunning outdoor murals depicting local history, manicured green spaces, and sweeping views of the Ottawa River.

spots.name: Glenora Ferry
spots.why: A free, historic cable ferry service that carries cars and passengers across the picturesque deep waters of the Bay of Quinte.

spots.name: Sandbanks Provincial Park
spots.why: Boasts the world's largest baymouth barrier dune formation and breathtaking golden sand beaches along Lake Ontario.

spots.name: Bellevue House
spots.why: A striking mid-19th-century Italianate villa that once served as the home of Canada's first prime minister, Sir John A. Macdonald.

spots.name: 1000 Islands Tower

plan.title: Nova Scotia Coastal & Cabot Trail Loop
plan.summary: This 4-day loop takes you from Halifax along the rugged South Shore to Peggy's Cove, then north toward Cape Breton Island to drive the legendary Cabot Trail. Experience dramatic coastal cliffs, sweeping ocean lookouts, and charming Acadian and Gaelic fishing villages.

days.title: Halifax to New Glasgow
days.summary: Head southwest from Halifax along the rugged coast to the colorful historic port of Lunenburg before cutting north across the province. The driving features a mix of tight coastal curves on the Peggy's Cove stretch and fast highway cruising across the interior. You will experience dramatic granite barrens transitioning to rolling agricultural valleys.
days.stay: Stay in New Glasgow near the central commercial district in traditional motels or comfortable local inns suited for a convenient overnight stop.

days.title: New Glasgow to Ingonish
days.summary: Drive north onto Cape Breton Island and tackle the legendary Cabot Trail counter-clockwise for the ultimate coastal mountain experience. The road clings to steep cliff sides, plunging down into tight hairpin turns overlooking the Gulf of St. Lawrence. It is a world-class driving day with breathtaking ocean panoramas and dramatic highland plateaus.
days.stay: Stay in Ingonish near the national park entrance in cozy coastal lodges, chalets, or oceanfront resorts.

days.title: Ingonish to Baddeck
days.summary: Continue along the remaining southern loop of the Cabot Trail along St. Ann's Bay before cruising down toward the lakeside town of Baddeck. The road winds through peaceful forested valleys and along sheltered waters, offering a much more relaxed driving pace than the northern headlands. Enjoy the charming maritime atmosphere of Alexander Graham Bell's historic summer home.
days.stay: Stay in Baddeck near the downtown waterfront in historic bed-and-breakfasts, inns, or lakeside motels.

days.title: Baddeck to Halifax
days.summary: Leave Cape Breton behind and cruise south down Highway 104 and 102 through the heart of Nova Scotia back to Halifax. The drive is efficient and straightforward, utilizing divided multi-lane highways to make quick work of the interior miles. Arrive back in the capital with plenty of time to enjoy the vibrant harborfront city life.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Halifax near the historic waterfront or the vibrant Spring Garden Road area in upscale boutique hotels or classic urban inns.

roads.why: Winds intimately along a stark, glacier-scoured granite coastline with constant ocean views and crashing surf.
roads.drive: Rolling and twisting two-lane road with numerous hidden dips, crests, and heavy tourist traffic during peak hours.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning to beat tour buses; watch for pedestrians near the lighthouse.

roads.name: Lighthouse Route
roads.why: Connects picturesque fishing villages and quiet coves through classic maritime landscapes.
roads.drive: A relaxed two-lane highway with gentle sweepers and well-maintained asphalt.
roads.tips: Keep an eye out for local lobster pounds and craft shops along the way.

official.name: Cabot Trail
official.description: Loop around Cape Breton Island's highlands and coast, through Cape Breton Highlands National Park and Acadian and Gaelic villages

roads.why: Widely regarded as one of the most scenic and exhilarating drives in North America, scaling high mountain headlands with sheer drops to the ocean.
roads.drive: Features severe 14% grades and tight switchbacks, particularly through the Cape Breton Highlands National Park. Driving counter-clockwise keeps you on the ocean side.
roads.tips: Check park websites for seasonal closures in winter; ensure your brakes are in top shape; watch for wildlife like moose on the road.

plan.title: Sydney to Melbourne via Blue Mountains, Snowy Mountains and Great Ocean Road
plan.summary: This 5-day journey takes you from Sydney through the dramatic gorges of the Blue Mountains and across the lofty Snowy Mountains via the Alpine Way. You will then cruise through Victoria's alpine high country before finishing with a legendary coastal drive along the Great Ocean Road from Lorne to Allansford.

days.title: Sydney to Bathurst
days.summary: Escape the Sydney sprawl via the scenic Bells Line of Road, climbing through the eucalyptus forests and sandstone cliffs of the Blue Mountains. The route levels out across the central tablelands, ending in the historic gold rush city of Bathurst. It is a relaxed start that trades the freeway for sweeping mountain tarmac.
days.stay: Look for accommodation near the historic heart of Bathurst or close to Mount Panorama. Options range from traditional motor inns and comfortable motels to heritage B&Bs.

days.title: Bathurst to Jindabyne
days.summary: Drive south through pastoral New South Wales before climbing onto the rooftop of Australia via the Snowy Mountains Highway. You will traverse rolling high-altitude plains and descend forested ridges towards the historic timber town of Tumut, before looping back down to the alpine resort of Jindabyne. Expect crisp mountain air and vast, rolling vistas.
days.stay: Stay close to the shores of Lake Jindabyne for easy access to the town's restaurants and alpine views. The area offers a mix of modern resort lodges, chalets, and standard motor inns.

days.title: Jindabyne to Wangaratta
days.summary: Conquer the legendary Alpine Way as it twists past Australia's highest peaks and drops dramatically into the Murray River valley at Khancoban. From there, cruise through rolling Victorian farmlands and past Hume Reservoir before finishing in the historic rural hub of Wangaratta. It is a big day of contrasting landscapes, from rugged alpine switchbacks to pastoral valleys.
days.stay: Stay near the Merriwa Park area or the town center of Wangaratta. Accommodation primarily consists of comfortable country motels, historic pubs, and motor lodges.

days.title: Wangaratta to Apollo Bay
days.summary: Cut across Victoria to the coast at Allansford, then tackle the world-famous Great Ocean Road in reverse from west to east. You will marvel at the limestone pillars of the Twelve Apostles and cruise along cliff-hugging tarmac before finishing the day in the charming seaside village of Apollo Bay. The afternoon treats you to dramatic Southern Ocean views.
days.stay: Stay within walking distance of the beachfront in Apollo Bay. The town features relaxed motels, boutique coastal apartments, and traditional guesthouses.

days.title: Apollo Bay to Melbourne
days.summary: Savor the final stretch of the Great Ocean Road as it clings to the cliffside between Apollo Bay and Lorne, featuring some of the best driving curves on the coast. After passing Torquay, transition onto the freeway system for a smooth, direct run into the heart of Melbourne. It's an iconic coastal finale to an epic driving journey.
days.stay: Stay in Melbourne's central business district or vibrant inner-city neighborhoods like Fitzroy or Southbank. You will find everything from boutique design hotels to serviced apartments.

roads.name: Bells Line of Road

official.name: Bells Line of Road
official.description: Quieter, twisting crossing of the Blue Mountains from Richmond to Lithgow past orchards and Mount Tomah

roads.why: A fantastic driving alternative to the Great Western Highway, offering sweeping curves, excellent pavement, and dramatic lookouts over the northern Blue Mountains without the heavy tourist congestion of Katoomba.
roads.drive: Consistent moderate grades and sweeping sweepers with some tight sections as you descend into the valleys. Watch out for weekend motorcycle traffic and local wildlife.
roads.tips: Fill up in Richmond before you start. Fog can reduce visibility in the early morning, so depart after 09:00 if mist is heavy.

roads.name: Snowy Mountains Highway

official.name: Snowy Mountains Highway
official.description: Crosses the Snowy Mountains via Cooma, Adaminaby, Kiandra and Tumut, with the Brown Mountain descent toward the coast

roads.why: Takes drivers over the highest paved passes in Australia, cutting through glacial valleys, snow gums, and vast alpine plains with phenomenal long-range views.
roads.drive: Long climbs, sweeping high-speed bends, and a thrilling descent down the Talbingo grade. Pavement is generally good, but livestock on the road can be a hazard.
roads.tips: Check for snow chains requirements in winter. Fuel is limited once you leave Cooma, so top up early.

roads.name: Alpine Way

official.name: Alpine Way
official.description: Mountain road from Jindabyne past Thredbo and Dead Horse Gap to Khancoban through Kosciuszko National Park

roads.why: A technical, demanding, and utterly breathtaking motorcycle and sports car favorite that snakes right past the base of Australia's highest peaks.
roads.drive: Steep grades up to 8%, tight hairpins, narrow sections with sheer drops, and sweeping forest corners. Best driven from east to west for optimal views of the descending valleys.
roads.tips: Beware of wandering wombats and kangaroos, especially near dawn and dusk. Mobile reception is patchy; carry offline maps.

roads.name: Great Ocean Road

official.name: Great Ocean Road
official.description: Clifftop coastal road from Torquay to Allansford past Lorne, Apollo Bay and the Twelve Apostles, built by returned WWI soldiers

roads.why: Built by returned soldiers, this engineering marvel hugs vertical sea cliffs, carved directly out of the rockface overlooking the roaring Southern Ocean, offering world-class coastal scenery.
roads.drive: A mix of tight cliff-hugging turns, undulating straights, and sweeping coastal bends. Driving west-to-east puts you on the ocean side of the road with easy pull-off access.
roads.tips: Tour bus traffic peaks midday between the Twelve Apostles and Apollo Bay. Do the coastal driving early in the morning to enjoy empty tarmac.

spots.name: Mount Tomah Botanic Garden
spots.why: A cool-climate botanic garden perched high on a basalt-capped extinct volcanic neck with expansive views across the Blue Mountains wilderness.

spots.name: Mount Panorama Circuit
spots.why: Drive your own car around the actual public racing circuit that hosts the famous Bathurst 1000, including tackling the steep incline of Conrod Straight and the dipper.

spots.name: Adaminaby

spots.name: Yarrangobilly Caves

spots.name: Khancoban
spots.why: A quiet alpine valley settlement that marks the end of the grueling mountain descent and the gateway to the Snowy Hydro scheme.

spots.name: Twelve Apostles
spots.why: Iconic limestone stacks rising majestically from the Southern Ocean, offering one of Australia's most dramatic coastal vistas.

spots.name: Loch Ard Gorge
spots.why: A stunning and tragic shipwreck site featuring sheer cliff walls, a hidden sandy beach, and crashing turquoise waves.

spots.name: Gibson Steps
spots.why: Descend a historic staircase carved into the cliff face directly onto the roaring beach beside towering limestone stacks.

spots.name: Maits Rest Rainforest Walk
spots.why: A short, beautiful boardwalk trail through a cool-temperate rainforest filled with giant ancient Myrtle Beech trees and tree ferns.

spots.name: Teddy's Lookout
spots.why: Provides a classic bird's-eye view looking back down over the winding Great Ocean Road as it hugs the coastline near Lorne.

plan.title: Melbourne Coast and Grampians Loop
plan.summary: A 4-day driving enthusiast loop from Melbourne out along the stunning clifftop Great Ocean Road past the Twelve Apostles, cutting inland to the rugged Grampians ranges, and returning via the country roads of central Victoria.

days.title: Along the Great Ocean Road to Apollo Bay
days.summary: Leave the city behind and head southwest toward the coast, where the famous Great Ocean Road officially begins at Torquay. Carve through cliff-hugging curves with sweeping ocean vistas, passing through the vibrant surf towns of Lorne and Skenes Creek before arriving in the sheltered bay of Apollo Bay. The driving is an exhilarating mix of tight coastal bends and tall eucalyptus forests.
days.stay: Stay right along the main beachfront or nestled in the green hills just behind town in a relaxed motel, coastal lodge, or boutique B&B.

days.title: Past the Twelve Apostles to Warrnambool
days.summary: Tackle the breathtaking stretch over Cape Otway through lush temperate rainforest before the coastline dramatically opens up to wild southern ocean lookouts. Marvel at the sheer limestone architecture of the Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge as the road winds toward the historic maritime port of Warrnambool. This is world-class coastal touring with constantly shifting weather and epic geological formations.
days.stay: Look for accommodation near the historic Flagstaff Hill precinct or along the main commercial strip in a comfortable motel, motor inn, or serviced apartment.

days.title: Into the Grampians to Halls Gap
days.summary: Leave the coast behind and head north across the vast western Victorian plains toward the dramatic, jagged sandstone peaks of the Grampians. The approach through Dunkeld sets the stage before climbing up into the ranges via steep, winding mountain passes into Halls Gap. Expect sweeping vistas, dramatic rock formations, and abundant roadside kangaroos and emus.
days.stay: Stay close to the heart of Halls Gap within walking distance of the local hub, choosing between rustic alpine cabins, holiday parks, or woodland lodges.

days.title: Back to Melbourne via the Macedon Ranges
days.summary: Cruise across the agricultural plains back toward Melbourne, breaking up the return journey with a scenic detour into the cool, winding roads of the Macedon Ranges. Finish the loop with a refreshing climb past historic hill station estates and towering pines before descending back into the city. It is a smooth, rewarding transition from rugged wilderness back to metropolitan life.
days.stay: Stay in central Melbourne near the vibrant inner-city laneways and dining precincts in a chic boutique hotel, modern apartment, or classic grand hotel.

roads.name: Great Ocean Road

official.name: Great Ocean Road
official.description: Clifftop coastal road from Torquay to Allansford past Lorne, Apollo Bay and the Twelve Apostles, built by returned WWI soldiers

roads.why: Carved into sheer sea cliffs by returning soldiers after WWI, this globally renowned coastal drive hugs the Southern Ocean with staggering drop-offs, pristine beaches, and temperate rainforests.
roads.drive: A mix of smooth, sweeping curves and tight hairpin bends with some exposed cliffside sections. Traffic can be heavy with tour buses and campervans during midday; drive early to enjoy the rhythm of the road.
roads.tips: Drive west-to-east or east-to-west, but westbound keeps you on the ocean side for easy pull-offs. Watch out for local wildlife at dawn and dusk.

roads.name: Mount Victory Road
roads.segment: through the Grampians from Dunkeld to Halls Gap

official.name: Mount Victory Road
official.description: Through the Grampians ranges from Halls Gap past Reed Lookout and The Balconies

roads.why: A fantastic mountain pass traversing the rugged Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park, offering dramatic elevation changes, tight curves, and sweeping lookouts over ancient sandstone ridges.
roads.drive: Steep grades and tight switchbacks require attentiveness, but the road surface is well-maintained and rewarding for enthusiasts.
roads.tips: Watch for cyclists and wildlife, particularly kangaroos and emus grazing on the verges. Fuel up in Dunkeld or Halls Gap before heading into the park.

roads.name: Mount Macedon Road

official.name: Mount Macedon Road
official.description: Winding climb through the Macedon Ranges northwest of Melbourne

roads.why: A wonderfully winding climb through dense native forests and historic 19th-century estate gardens in the Macedon Ranges northwest of Melbourne.
roads.drive: A fun succession of smooth elevation gains and sweeping bends under a dense canopy of trees. Can be misty and slick after rain.
roads.tips: Great weekend driving road; watch for weekend cyclists and local traffic around the summit township.

spots.name: Twelve Apostles
spots.why: World-famous limestone stacks rising majestically from the turbulent Southern Ocean surf.

spots.name: Loch Ard Gorge
spots.why: A dramatic enclosed sea gorge with a tragic shipwreck history and stunning coastal walking tracks.

spots.name: Mount Abrupt
spots.why: A challenging climb offering jaw-dropping panoramic views across the southern Grampians plains.

spots.name: MacKenzie Falls
spots.why: One of the largest and most spectacular waterfalls in Victoria, flowing year-round into a deep gorge.

spots.name: Reeds Lookout and The Balconies

spots.name: Ballarat Botanical Gardens

spots.name: Memorial Cross Mount Macedon

plan.title: Victorian High Country & Great Alpine Road Loop
plan.summary: A 3-day alpine adventure looping northeast from Melbourne into the dramatic peaks of the Great Dividing Range. Experience Australia's highest sealed roads, sweeping mountain descents, and lush fern forests.

days.title: Through the Black Spur to the High Country
days.summary: Leave the city behind and tackle the legendary curves of the Black Spur before crossing the foothills into the High Country. The road winds through towering mountain ash forests and alpine valleys, offering a masterclass in sweeping bends and changing elevation. After a scenic push past Mansfield, you will finish the day surrounded by crisp mountain air as you roll into Bright.
days.stay: Stay in the heart of Bright near the Ovens River, where charming boutique motels, guesthouses, and historic pubs put everything within walking distance.

days.title: Over Mount Hotham on the Great Alpine Road
days.summary: Conquer Australia's highest sealed road as you climb directly over the spine of Mount Hotham. The landscape shifts dramatically from lush river valleys to stark, windswept alpine ridges with sweeping views across the Victorian Alps. After descending through the rugged high country to Omeo, the road smooths out as it winds down toward the coastal plains of Bairnsdale.
days.stay: Stay in central Bairnsdale along the Princes Highway, offering a range of comfortable roadside motels, heritage stays, and motor inns.

days.title: Gippsland Backroads and Grand Ridge
days.summary: Cruise west through the rolling green hills and farming communities of Gippsland, taking in the relaxed pastoral scenery. As you loop back toward the capital, you will traverse sections of the Grand Ridge Road through South Gippsland's ranges. The drive finishes with an easy cruise back into Melbourne via the freeway network.
days.stay: Stay in central Melbourne near the inner-city neighborhoods or the Yarra River, featuring a wide range of boutique hotels, chic apartments, and historic lodges.

roads.name: Black Spur

official.name: Black Spur
official.description: Winding stretch of the Maroondah Highway through towering mountain ash forest between Healesville and Narbethong

roads.why: Renowned among motorcyclists and drivers for its wall of towering mountain ash trees, tree ferns, and a relentless sequence of beautifully cambered tight curves.
roads.drive: A smooth, well-sealed two-lane highway with gentle grades, though morning fog and weekend traffic, including cyclists and tourist buses, require patience. Driving north from Healesville to Narbethong allows you to climb gently through the best of the tightest turns.
roads.tips: Watch out for wandering wildlife at dawn and dusk. Fuel up in Healesville before hitting the curves.

roads.name: Great Alpine Road
roads.segment: from Bright over Mount Hotham to Bairnsdale

official.name: Great Alpine Road
official.description: Australia's highest year-round sealed road, from Wangaratta over Mount Hotham to Bairnsdale

roads.why: Australia's highest year-round sealed road treats drivers to an incredible alpine traverse featuring steep drop-offs, hairpin turns, and panoramic vistas above the tree line.
roads.drive: Demanding mountain driving with sustained steep grades (up to 1-in-10), sharp hairpins, and sudden weather shifts, especially near Mount Hotham. Driving south from Porepunkah over the summit to Omeo offers the most dramatic alpine ascent and descent.
roads.tips: Carry snow chains during the declared snow season from June to October, as they are legally required on Mount Hotham. Check for winter closures and fuel up in Bright or Omeo.

spots.name: Black Spur Inn
spots.why: A classic historic roadside stop tucked right into the forest near Narbethong, perfect for a quick coffee before the real climbs begin.

spots.name: Lake Eildon
spots.why: Offers expansive blue water vistas framed by rolling foothills as you approach the Mansfield region.

spots.name: Mount Hotham Summit
spots.why: Stand at 1,750 meters above sea level for a breathtaking, unobstructed 360-degree panorama of the rugged Victorian Alps.

spots.name: Omeo Historic Gaol
spots.why: A fascinating glimpse into the region's harsh 19th-century gold-mining and pioneer history.

spots.name: Tyers Park
spots.why: A peaceful bushland reserve along the Thomson River providing a tranquil spot to stretch your legs away from the highway.

spots.name: Yarragon
spots.why: A charming country village famous for its antique shops, local bakeries, and craft stores, making it an ideal lunch stop.

plan.title: Queensland Hinterland and Coastal Loop
plan.summary: A 3-day driving adventure looping from Brisbane through the rainforest-clad peaks of the Gold Coast hinterland, the winding curves of Tamborine Mountain, and the scenic Blackall Range in the Sunshine Coast hinterland.

days.title: Gold Coast Hinterland and Lamington National Park
days.summary: Leave Brisbane behind and dive straight into the lush Gold Coast hinterland, climbing sharply up Tamborine Mountain before weaving through deep valleys toward Springbrook. The tarmac treats you to steep, tight hairpins and dense rainforest canopies that open up to sweeping coastal vistas. It is an intense, technical day of driving that rewards precise steering and patience behind slower tourist traffic.
days.stay: Stay in the charming country village of Canungra, nestled right at the base of the Lamington foothills, where traditional pubs and boutique B&Bs offer a warm rural welcome.

days.title: Scenic Rim to the Sunshine Coast Hinterland
days.summary: Tackle the legendary, narrow ascent to O'Reilly's through the ancient Gondwana rainforest before cutting across the agricultural Scenic Rim and climbing the Great Dividing Range via Cunningham's Gap. After dropping into Warwick, you will jump onto the fast highway miles that whisk you north past Brisbane toward the serene Blackall Range. It is a massive driving day combining tight, single-lane rainforest tracks with high-speed transit and mountain passes.
days.stay: Settle into the ridge-top hinterland village of Maleny, known for its misty mornings and artisan cottage accommodations overlooking the dramatic peaks of the Glass House Mountains.

days.title: Blackall Range and Return to Brisbane
days.summary: Cruising the famous Blackall Range Tourist Drive delivers sweeping ridge-top views and effortless sweepers connecting the vibrant villages of Montville and Maleny. From there, you descend the range toward Nambour and cruise back down the highway to Brisbane to close the loop. It is a relaxed, scenic morning drive that lets you enjoy the rhythm of the car before returning to the city.
days.stay: Celebrate the end of your trip back in Brisbane, staying in the vibrant riverside cultural precinct or the historic inner city with plenty of boutique hotels and vibrant dining options.

roads.name: Tamborine Mountain Road

official.name: Tamborine Mountain Road
official.description: Steep, twisting climb from Oxenford onto Tamborine Mountain in the Gold Coast hinterland

roads.why: A rapid altitude gain featuring tight hairpins and dense subtropical foliage that makes you feel worlds away from the coast.
roads.drive: Steep, twisting climb with sharp bends and occasional tourist buses; best driven early in the morning before traffic builds up.
roads.tips: Watch out for cyclists on weekends and keep an eye on your brake temperatures on the descent.

roads.name: Springbrook Road

official.name: Springbrook Road
official.description: Up the escarpment from Mudgeeraba to Springbrook's waterfalls and the Best of All Lookout

roads.why: A dramatic wall of green scaling the escarpment with incredible rock cuttings and glimpses of distant waterfalls.
roads.drive: Narrow, undulating sections with steep grades and tight corners that demand active gear selection.
roads.tips: Fuel up before leaving the coastal plain; amenities on the plateau are limited.

roads.name: Lamington National Park Road

official.name: Lamington National Park Road
official.description: Narrow mountain road from Canungra to O'Reilly's in the Gondwana rainforest of Lamington National Park

roads.why: One of Queensland's most revered driving roads, featuring a narrow, winding, single-lane-width ribbon of tarmac through towering eucalyptus and rainforest.
roads.drive: Incredibly narrow with blind crests, sheer drop-offs, and cattle grids; requires total concentration and frequent use of pullouts to let locals pass.
roads.tips: Drive slowly, cover your horn for blind corners, and watch for local wildlife like pademelons and lyrebirds.

roads.name: Cunningham's Gap

official.name: Cunningham's Gap
official.description: The Cunningham Highway's pass over the Great Dividing Range through Main Range National Park, between Aratula and Warwick

roads.why: A classic historic highway pass slicing right through the volcanic peaks of Main Range National Park.
roads.drive: A well-paved highway with steady, long gradients and sweeping curves that allow for a great driving rhythm.
roads.tips: Heavy freight trucks use this route, so maintain good spacing on the climbs.

roads.name: Blackall Range Tourist Drive

official.name: Blackall Range Tourist Drive
official.description: Ridge-top drive through the Sunshine Coast hinterland villages of Montville and Maleny, with views to the Glass House Mountains

roads.why: A gorgeous ridge-top cruise offering panoramic lookouts over the Sunshine Coast and farming valleys below.
roads.drive: Gentle sweepers, rolling hills, and frequent 50-60 km/h zones through artisan villages with pedestrian traffic.
roads.tips: Popular with weekend motorcycle groups; watch for sudden stops as drivers pull over for viewpoints.

spots.name: Tamborine Rainforest Skywalk
spots.why: Walk high above the forest floor on steel bridges through a canopy rich with native birdlife.

spots.name: Best of All Lookout
spots.why: A short, mossy walk leads to a breathtaking cliffside view stretching all the way to Byron Bay on a clear day.

spots.name: Natural Bridge, Springbrook
spots.why: A stunning geological formation where a waterfall crashes through the roof of a basalt cave.

spots.name: O'Reilly's Rainforest Retreat
spots.why: Historic mountain lodge famous for wild king parrots landing on your shoulders and the thrilling treetop walk.

spots.name: Cunningham's Gap Lookout
spots.why: Dramatic views framed by Mount Cordeaux and Mount Mitchell in the heart of the Scenic Rim.

spots.name: Montville Village
spots.why: A quaint European-style village packed with craft shops, art galleries, and fantastic bakeries.

spots.name: Mary Cairncross Scenic Reserve
spots.why: Offers an unmatched, postcard-perfect view of the iconic Glass House Mountains rising from the flatlands.

plan.title: Tasmania Wild East Coast & Cradle Mountain Loop
plan.summary: A 6-day driving adventure looping from Hobart up Tasmania's scenic east coast via Freycinet and the Bay of Fires, returning inland through the rugged rainforests of the west coast and Cradle Mountain.

days.title: Hobart to Swansea via East Coast
days.summary: Head out from Hobart across the Tasman Bridge and take the coastal route north through rolling farmland and ocean vistas. The highlight is the sweep along the Great Oyster Bay toward the Freycinet Peninsula, offering soaring views of the Hazards mountains. The drive has a relaxed touring pace with sweeping coastal curves.
days.stay: Stay in Swansea near the waterfront in a local coastal motel, cottage, or bed and breakfast with views across to the Hazards.

days.title: Swansea to St Helens and Bay of Fires
days.summary: Cruise north past quiet surf beaches and granite coves before tackling the climb over Elephant Pass or St Marys Pass. The reward is dropping down to the stunning, orange-lichen granite rocks of the Bay of Fires near St Helens. It is an effortless coastal and mountain-edge driving day.
days.stay: Stay in St Helens right by the fishing port or Georges Bay in a comfortable motel, holiday rental, or waterfront cabin.

days.title: St Helens over Weldborough Pass to Launceston
days.summary: Leave the coast behind and wind inland through the dense canopy and historic hop fields over Weldborough Pass. The road twists through temperate rainforest and fertile valleys before opening up toward Launceston. Expect tight forested switchbacks at the pass giving way to pastoral cruising.
days.stay: Stay in central Launceston near the historic Cataract Gorge in a boutique hotel, heritage inn, or stylish apartment.

days.title: Launceston to Cradle Mountain
days.summary: Head west through rolling agricultural land before climbing sharply onto the rugged central plateau toward Cradle Mountain. The final approach on the C132 cuts through dramatic alpine moorland and glacial valleys. Watch for sudden weather shifts and native wildlife along the tarmac.
days.stay: Stay near the Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park boundary in an alpine wilderness lodge, eco-cabin, or rustic chalet.

days.title: Cradle Mountain through West Coast Rainforest to Queenstown
days.summary: Descend through the wild West Coast rainforest, passing historic mining towns framed by steep, rugged peaks. The road through Zeehan and Rosebery features undulating terrain and dense, misty native forest. It is a moody, atmospheric drive into the historic mining heartland of Queenstown.
days.stay: Stay in Queenstown in a restored historic mining hotel, retro motel, or guesthouse surrounded by the stark, scarred hills.

days.title: Queenstown across Central Highlands back to Hobart
days.summary: Conclude the loop with an unforgettable crossing of the Central Highlands on the Lyell Highway. You will traverse the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park, climbing past vast lakes and buttongrass plains before descending back to sea level. The route finishes with a fast run down the midlands into Hobart.
days.stay: Stay in central Hobart near the historic waterfront or Salamanca Place in a luxury harbor hotel or boutique heritage property.

roads.name: Tasman Highway
roads.why: It links Hobart to the dramatic east coast and winds over interior mountain passes like Elephant Pass, offering a mix of coastal straightaways and tight, forested hairpins.
roads.drive: Generally well-paved two-lane highway with some steep, winding sections over the coastal ranges. Can have tourist traffic in summer; drive with care and use pullouts to let locals pass.
roads.tips: Check for local roadworks on the passes. Fuel is readily available in larger coastal towns like Bicheno and St Helens.

roads.name: Cradle Mountain Road

official.name: Cradle Mountain Road
official.description: From Moina to Cradle Mountain and Dove Lake through alpine moorland
official.wiki: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park

roads.why: Famous alpine drive climbing through rolling sheep country up onto the exposed moorlands approaching the national park boundary.
roads.drive: Winding two-lane mountain road with steep grades and tight bends. Prone to ice, snow, and heavy mist year-round; watch out for wombats and wallabies.
roads.tips: Carry national park entry permits and be prepared for rapidly changing mountain weather.

info.title: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park

roads.name: Murchison Highway

official.name: Murchison Highway
official.description: Through the rainforest of the west coast from Zeehan and Rosebery north toward Burnie

roads.why: A remote, rugged highway cutting deep through the wet temperate rainforest and steep gorges of Tasmania's wild west coast.
roads.drive: Undulating and heavily twisty in sections with steep descents. Heavy transport trucks and logging vehicles use this route, so maintain concentration on blind curves.
roads.tips: Fill up with fuel before leaving Cradle Mountain or Rosebery; stations are sparse on this remote stretch.

roads.name: Lyell Highway

official.name: Lyell Highway
official.description: Hobart to Queenstown across the Central Highlands and the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers country, ending with the bare hills above Queenstown

roads.why: One of Australia's great driving roads, slicing straight through the heart of the UNESCO wilderness area with epic sweepers, bridge crossings, and stark mountain vistas.
roads.drive: Challenging twisty sections with steep climbs out of Queenstown (including the famous 97 bends) opening up into fast, rolling high-plateau sweepers.
roads.tips: Allow extra time for weather delays and photography stops. Watch for black ice in winter and early spring.

spots.name: Spiky Bridge
spots.why: A convict-built stone bridge featuring unique vertically-laid fieldstone parapets resembling spikes.

spots.name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
spots.why: A world-famous viewpoint overlooking the pristine curved white beach and turquoise waters of Freycinet Peninsula.

spots.name: Douglas-Apsley National Park
spots.why: Offers a quick side trip to dramatic dry-country gorges, waterfalls, and eucalyptus forests.

spots.name: Bay of Fires
spots.why: Striking coastal landscape featuring crystal-clear blue water contrasting with massive granite boulders covered in bright orange lichen.

spots.name: Pub in the Paddock
spots.why: A classic, historic country pub where a resident pig famously drinks beer from a bottle.

spots.name: Bridestowe Lavender Estate
spots.why: Home to the world's largest commercial lavender farm with stunning purple rows and famous lavender ice cream.

spots.name: Cataract Gorge
spots.why: A stunning natural river gorge just minutes from downtown Launceston with walking trails and a suspension bridge.

spots.name: Great Lake Honey
spots.why: Great stop to sample rare leatherwood honey and local Tasmanian artisanal products.

spots.name: Dove Lake
spots.why: Iconic glacial lake sitting directly beneath the jagged peak of Cradle Mountain.

spots.name: Montezuma Falls
spots.why: Tasmania's tallest waterfall reached via a scenic rainforest walking trail crossing a dramatic suspension bridge.

spots.name: Iron Blow Lookout
spots.why: Overlooks Australia's first commercially mined open-cut copper mine, showcasing an eerie, colorful crater.

spots.name: Lake St Clair
spots.why: Australia's deepest freshwater lake, carved by glaciers and surrounded by dense alpine wilderness.

spots.name: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
spots.why: Offers sweeping vistas over untouched river valleys, dense huon pine forests, and dramatic quartzite peaks.

spots.name: Wall in the Wilderness
spots.why: A monumental handcrafted art project depicting the history of the Central Highlands carved entirely in Huon pine panels.

plan.title: Fiordland Alpine Escape
plan.summary: A breathtaking two-day journey from Queenstown through the dramatic Southern Alps and across the Eglinton Valley to the iconic depths of Milford Sound. Experience world-class alpine vistas and the legendary Milford Road.

days.title: Through the Southern Alps to Te Anau
days.summary: Leave Queenstown and climb away from Lake Wakatipu before tracking south through undulating high-country farmland toward the gateway to Fiordland. The landscape transitions quickly from golden tussock hills to dense, moody native beech forests as you approach the shores of Lake Te Anau. It is an easygoing driving day designed to position you perfectly for tomorrow's early alpine push.
days.stay: Stay right in the heart of Te Anau within easy walking distance of the lakefront and local restaurants. Accommodation options range from lakeside motels and comfortable lodges to boutique B&Bs and holiday parks.

days.title: Milford Sound and Return to Queenstown
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Milford Road early in the morning to beat the tour buses, sweeping through the massive glacial-carved Eglinton Valley and plunging down the steep Cleddau switchbacks. The return journey gives you a completely different perspective of the towering granite peaks, hanging valleys, and waterfalls rushing off the sheer rock faces. It is a long, highly demanding, and utterly breathtaking driving day.
days.stay: Return to Queenstown for your final night, staying close to the vibrant downtown waterfront or in the quieter hillside suburbs. Choose from alpine resort hotels, luxury lakeview lodges, or self-contained apartments.

roads.name: Milford Road
roads.segment: from Te Anau to Milford Sound

official.name: Milford Road
official.description: Te Anau to Milford Sound through Fiordland: the Eglinton Valley, the Homer Tunnel and switchbacks down the Cleddau to the fiord

roads.why: Universally regarded as one of the most stunning alpine drives on earth, cutting straight through the heart of the Fiordland National Park with sheer granite cliffs, towering waterfalls, and primeval rainforests.
roads.drive: A challenging alpine highway featuring steep grades, the narrow single-lane Homer Tunnel with its internal switchbacks, and tight hairpin bends descending into Milford Sound. Watch out for heavy tourist coach traffic, roaming kea parrots, and potential avalanche hazards in cooler months.
roads.tips: Depart Te Anau by 07:00 to get ahead of the tour buses. There is no mobile reception or fuel beyond Te Anau, so fill up your tank completely before starting.

spots.name: Devil's Staircase, Otago
spots.why: A dramatic cliffside viewpoint offering sweeping, elevated vistas across the deep blue southern waters of Lake Wakatipu framed by the jagged Remarkables mountain range.

spots.name: Lake Te Anau
spots.why: New Zealand's second-largest lake provides a tranquil waterfront setting with pebble beaches and a peaceful backdrop of misty, forest-clad mountains.

spots.name: Eglinton Valley
spots.why: A breathtakingly vast, flat-bottomed glacial valley covered in golden tussock grass and flanked by sheer, glacier-carved mountain walls.

spots.name: Mirror Lakes, New Zealand
spots.why: A short, easy boardwalk takes you to small roadside forest lakes that perfectly reflect the surrounding Earl Mountains on a calm day.

spots.name: Homer Tunnel
spots.why: An engineering marvel carved entirely through solid granite rock in the Darran Mountains, marking the dramatic transition into the Cleddau Valley.

spots.name: Milford Sound
spots.why: A world-famous fiord dominated by the iconic, rising cone of Mitre Peak and cascading waterfalls that plunge hundreds of meters straight into the sea.

plan.title: Scottish Highlands and North Coast 500 Adventure
plan.summary: A magnificent 7-day loop from Edinburgh through the dramatic Scottish Highlands, conquering legendary routes like the North Coast 500, Bealach na Bà, and Glen Coe. This journey balances challenging single-track mountain passes with breathtaking coastal vistas and historic lochs.

days.title: From Edinburgh into Glen Coe
days.summary: Leave Edinburgh behind as the urban sprawl quickly gives way to the dramatic peaks and deep lochs of the Highlands. The highlight is the breathtaking run through Glen Coe, where towering volcanic walls frame the road. Expect sweeping bends, moody weather, and a true sense of entering the wild north.
days.stay: Stay in Fort William near the shores of Loch Linnhe, where traditional stone B&Bs and welcoming local inns offer a hearty Highland welcome.

days.title: Road to the Isles and Skye
days.summary: Drive the legendary Road to the Isles past the Glenfinnan Monument to Mallaig, then take the scenic ferry across to the Isle of Skye. The afternoon winds through the dramatic landscapes of Sleat and northward to Portree under the shadow of the Cuillin mountains. It is a cinematic drive of sea lochs and jagged peaks.
days.stay: Stay in central Portree within walking distance of the colorful harbor, choosing from cozy guesthouses or traditional small hotels.

days.title: Over Bealach na Bà to Ullapool
days.summary: Conquer the legendary Bealach na Bà, a single-track mountain pass featuring severe hairpins and sweeping alpine views before descending to Applecross. The route continues along the stunning coastal waters of Loch Torridon and north to Ullapool. This is one of the most technical and rewarding driving days in Britain.
days.stay: Stay in Ullapool close to Loch Broom, featuring charming waterfront inns, friendly bed and breakfasts, and great seafood spots.

days.title: Far North to Durness
days.summary: Venture into the far northwest along the undulating, roller-coaster tarmac of the North Coast 500 through breathtaking coastal vistas and remote moorland. Pass by the dramatic Kylesku Bridge and deep lochs before reaching the rugged northern coastline at Durness. The remote, edge-of-the-world atmosphere is truly unmatched.
days.stay: Stay near Durness in a local lodge, B&B, or coastal inn overlooking the wild Atlantic waves.

days.title: Top of Scotland to John o' Groats
days.overnight: John o' Groats, Scotland, United Kingdom
days.summary: Cruise across the top of Scotland along sweeping coastal roads passing vast golden beaches, historic Dunnet Head, and windswept cliffs. The journey culminates at John o' Groats, the iconic northeastern tip of the British mainland. Enjoy fast, open stretches with stunning views of the Pentland Firth and Orkney Isles.
days.stay: Stay around John o' Groats in a comfortable guesthouse or local hotel offering uninterrupted views toward the northern seas.

days.title: Down the East Coast to Inverness
days.summary: Head south down the rugged northeast coastline via Wick and Helmsdale, before joining the faster A9 past rolling agricultural land and sweeping coastal fringes. The drive offers a nice mix of open straights and gentle coastal curves leading into the Highland capital of Inverness. It serves as a smooth and scenic transition back toward the south.
days.stay: Stay in central Inverness near the River Ness, with plenty of boutique hotels, guesthouses, and vibrant evening dining options.

days.title: Snow Roads to Edinburgh
days.summary: Take on the Snow Roads Scenic Route over the Cairnwell Pass through Braemar and Blairgowrie, traversing Britain's highest public roads. The driving is exhilarating with steep gradients, wide mountain vistas, and challenging twists before descending into the Lowlands. Finish the loop back in Edinburgh with unforgettable memories of Highland tarmac.
days.stay: Stay in Edinburgh city center, celebrating the end of the trip in a historic Georgian townhouse hotel or stylish central apartment.

roads.name: Glen Coe
roads.why: Framed by towering, glacier-carved volcanic peaks and steeped in tragic clan history, it offers some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in the UK.
roads.drive: A wide, fast A-road with sweeping curves that allows for a smooth, rhythmic drive, though heavy tourist traffic in summer requires patience.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning to beat the tour buses and enjoy the mist rolling off the peaks. Fuel up in Crianlarich before entering the glen.

roads.name: Road to the Isles
roads.why: Winds past shimmering sea lochs, historic viaducts, and rugged hillsides, opening up gorgeous maritime vistas toward the Inner Hebrides.
roads.drive: A well-maintained trunk road with a mix of fast straights and pleasant coastal curves, transitioning to single-track roads once across on Skye.
roads.tips: Check ferry timetables between Mallaig and Armidale in advance, especially during peak summer months.

roads.name: Isle of Skye
roads.byway: Isle of Skye (A87 and the Trotternish loop) (A87)
roads.segment: from Armidale to Portree and Uig
roads.why: Breathtaking coastal cliffs, dramatic rock formations like the Old Man of Storr, and the majestic backdrop of the Cuillin range.
roads.drive: A combination of fast coastal stretches and narrow single-track sections with passing places. Watch for wandering sheep on the tarmac.
roads.tips: Drive respectfully on single-track roads by utilizing passing places correctly and pulling over to let locals pass.

roads.name: Bealach na Bà

official.name: Bealach na Bà
official.description: Single-track pass to Applecross with hairpins and 20% grades, climbing 626 m from sea level; not for caravans or learners

roads.why: Britain's ultimate driving challenge, featuring alpine hairpins, extreme elevation changes, and panoramic views over the Isle of Skye.
roads.drive: A legendary single-track mountain pass with 20% gradients, hairpin turns, and a summit of 626 meters. Unforgiving exposure and blind corners.
roads.tips: Strictly unsuitable for caravans, large motorhomes, or inexperienced drivers. Check weather conditions as snow or high winds close the pass easily.

roads.name: North Coast 500
roads.segment: from Ullapool to Durness and John o' Groats

official.name: North Coast 500
official.description: The famous loop from Inverness around the far north of Scotland: Applecross, Torridon, Ullapool, Durness and John o' Groats

roads.why: Celebrated as one of the world's great coastal drives, connecting pristine white-sand beaches, towering cliffs, and deep fjord-like lochs.
roads.drive: A mix of fast two-lane sections and technical single-track stretches with blind crests and undulating dips that demand full concentration.
roads.tips: Fuel stations can be sparse in the far north; always top up when you see an open pump. Avoid driving late at night due to wildlife on the road.

roads.name: Snow Roads Scenic Route

official.name: Snow Roads Scenic Route
official.description: Blairgowrie to Grantown-on-Spey over the Cairnwell Pass and the Lecht, Britain's highest public roads

roads.why: Traverses the rugged heart of the Cairngorms, featuring Britain's highest public road pass (Cairnwell Pass) and remote alpine moorland.
roads.drive: Challenging mountain driving with steep inclines, sharp switchbacks, and wide open exposure subject to rapid weather shifts.
roads.tips: Can experience severe winter weather even in spring. Stop at the art installations along the route to take in the viewpoints.

plan.title: Lake District and Yorkshire Dales Driving Loop
plan.summary: A 3-day driving enthusiast loop from Manchester through England's most challenging and scenic northern national parks. Experience legendary mountain passes including Kirkstone, Honister, Hardknott, Wrynose, and Buttertubs.

days.title: Into the Lake District via Kirkstone Pass
days.summary: Leave the industrial sprawl of Manchester behind and head north on the M6 before climbing straight into the heart of the Lake District. The highlight is the ascent of the A592 over Kirkstone Pass, offering sweeping vistas of Windermere and Ullswater. It's a dramatic, highly scenic transition from highway cruising to proper mountainous driving.
days.stay: Stay in the bustling market town of Keswick near Derwentwater, known for its traditional Lakeland inns and friendly B&Bs.

days.title: Hardknott, Wrynose and Honister Passes
days.summary: A truly intense day of Lake District pass-storming, tackling the brutal gradients of Hardknott and Wrynose before heading east over Honister Pass. Expect narrow single-track roads, sheer drops, and breathtaking high-altitude solitude before descending into the rolling green hills of the Yorkshire Dales. It demands total concentration and rewards with unforgettable scenery.
days.stay: Stay in the historic market town of Hawes in Wensleydale, featuring cozy stone-built inns and traditional Yorkshire bed and breakfasts.

days.title: Buttertubs Pass and the Peak District back to Manchester
days.summary: Start with the sweeping dips and dramatic limestone drops of Buttertubs Pass before cruising across the Dales and cutting south through the Peak District. The final flourish is the legendary Snake Pass over the Pennine moors, delivering sweeping curves and moody moorland vistas right back toward Manchester. It is a fantastic finale combining high-speed sweepers and technical moorland tarmac.
days.stay: Finish your trip back in vibrant Manchester, staying in the central districts or Northern Quarter for great restaurants, bars, and industrial heritage hotels.

roads.name: Kirkstone Pass

official.name: Kirkstone Pass
official.description: The Lake District's highest pass road, from Windermere to Ullswater past the Kirkstone Pass Inn

roads.why: As the Lake District's highest pass road, it delivers magnificent panoramic views of glacial valleys, deep lakes, and rugged fells right from the tarmac.
roads.drive: Features sustained steep climbs with gradients reaching 1-in-4 (25%) and sweeping curves. Can get busy with tourists and coaches during peak hours, so go early.
roads.tips: Drive north from Windermere to Ullswater for the best viewing angles. Can be treacherous in winter snow and ice.

roads.name: Honister Pass

official.name: Honister Pass
official.description: From Borrowdale over to Buttermere past the slate mine, one of the Lake District's great passes

roads.why: Steeped in slate-mining history, this dramatic pass links the lush valley of Borrowdale to the quieter shores of Buttermere through a dramatic, narrow mountain trough.
roads.drive: Involves severe gradients up to 1-in-4 and tight, unforgiving hairpins. Visibility can drop quickly if cloud cover rolls over the top.
roads.tips: Watch for sheep wandering onto the road and allow space for descending traffic on the single-track sections with passing places.

roads.name: Hardknott and Wrynose Passes

official.name: Hardknott and Wrynose Passes
official.description: The Lake District's steepest roads, with 30% grades and tight hairpins between Eskdale and Little Langdale

roads.why: Widely regarded as the most extreme and thrilling driving road in England, featuring Roman fort ruins and relentless roller-coaster topography.
roads.drive: Infamous 30% (1-in-3) grades, blind crests, and immediate hairpin turns with no safety barriers. Requires absolute clutch control in manuals and total commitment.
roads.tips: Absolute no-go in snow or heavy ice. Best driven early in the morning before tourist traffic clogs the passing places.

roads.name: Buttertubs Pass

official.name: Buttertubs Pass
official.description: Yorkshire Dales road from Hawes to Swaledale, nicknamed England's only true mountain road by Jeremy Clarkson

roads.why: A magnificent Dales ribbon flanked by deep limestone potholes known as the buttertubs, offering a classic rollercoaster driving experience across open moorland.
roads.drive: Fast, undulating sections with excellent sightlines, though crosswinds can be strong on the exposed plateau.
roads.tips: Popular with cyclists and motorcyclists, so keep speeds sensible over blind crests.

roads.name: Snake Pass

official.name: Snake Pass
official.description: The A57 over the Peak District moors between Glossop and the Ladybower Reservoir

roads.why: A legendary trans-Pennine route cutting through the Dark Peak landscape of the Peak District, beloved by generations of petrolheads for its rhythm and elevation changes.
roads.drive: A mix of fast sweepers and technical hairpins across open moorland. Prone to sudden weather changes and heavy commuter and lorry traffic.
roads.tips: Frequently closed in winter due to snowdrifts; check local travel reports before setting out.

spots.name: Windermere Lake

spots.name: Kirkstone Pass Inn
spots.why: Historically the highest pub in the Lake District, offering a welcome refuge at the summit of the pass.

spots.why: A spectacular 70-foot waterfall cascading through a wooded glen just down from the shores of Ullswater.

spots.name: Honister Slate Mine
spots.why: Working mine perched at the top of the pass offering underground tours and industrial heritage.

spots.name: Hardknott Roman Fort
spots.why: The atmospheric ruins of a 2nd-century Roman auxiliary fort perched high and isolated on the fellside.

spots.name: Eskdale Green
spots.why: A peaceful wooded valley village offering a great spot to catch your breath after descending the pass.

spots.name: Wensleydale Creamery

spots.name: Hardraw Force

spots.name: Swaledale

spots.name: Ladybower Reservoir
spots.why: A dramatic Y-shaped reservoir set amidst the rugged moors of the Peak District, famous for its overspill plug holes.

plan.title: Swiss Alps Triple Pass Loop
plan.summary: A breathtaking 2-day loop from Zurich tackling three of Switzerland's legendary high-altitude alpine passes. Experience dramatic glacier views, sweeping switchbacks, and engineering marvels on roads celebrated by driving enthusiasts worldwide.

days.title: Zurich to Andermatt
days.summary: Leave Zurich behind quickly on the highway before climbing deep into the central Swiss Alps via the legendary Susten Pass. The road treats you to sweeping granite walls, glacier views, and immaculate sweepers that build anticipation for the high alpine terrain. It is a masterclass in mountain engineering and an absolute joy for drivers who love rhythmic curves.
days.stay: Stay in the historic core of Andermatt near the station, where traditional alpine chalets meet modern high-end mountain architecture. Expect upscale boutique lodges, historic alpine inns, and comfortable hotels catering to outdoor enthusiasts.

days.title: Andermatt to Zurich
days.summary: Tackle the trifecta of classic Swiss passes starting with the tight hairpin bends of the Furka Pass, made famous by James Bond. Descend into the deep Rhône valley before climbing the rugged lunar landscape of the Grimsel Pass and returning north via the Susten approach. The day is packed with dramatic elevation changes, iconic switchbacks, and jaw-dropping gorge views.
days.stay: Return to Zurich and stay in the lively Old Town (Altstadt) along the Limmat River, close to the central station and vibrant lakefront promenades. Choose from historic grand hotels, design-focused city lodges, and chic boutique properties.

roads.name: Susten Pass

official.name: Susten Pass
official.description: Innertkirchen to Wassen with tunnels, glacier views and wide sweeping bends at 2,224 m

roads.why: Famed for its sweeping, modern alpine alignment, deep glacial valley views, and the massive Stein Glacier hanging right above the road. It offers some of the best high-speed sweepers and visibility in the Swiss Alps.
roads.drive: Wide, well-paved two-lane road with moderate 9-percent grades, sweeping curves on the lower stretches, and tighter switchbacks near the summit. Exposure is moderate, traffic can include tourist buses and cyclists, and driving west from Wassen provides the most dramatic ascent.
roads.tips: Open typically from June to October depending on snow clearance; check local pass status before departure and watch for morning mist.

roads.name: Grimsel Pass

official.name: Grimsel Pass
official.description: Innertkirchen to Gletsch past granite and dam lakes at 2,164 m, usually paired with the Furka

roads.why: Features a stark, high-altitude granite landscape dotted with massive deep-blue hydroelectric reservoirs that look like alpine fjords. The raw, barren scenery gives it an otherworldly, almost cinematic feel.
roads.drive: Steep and narrow in sections with tight hairpin turns dropping down towards Gletsch, featuring classic stone parapets and granite tunnels. Traffic is generally lighter than the Furka, and driving south from Innertkirchen reveals the most imposing rock faces.
roads.tips: Combine with the adjacent passes; early morning offers empty tarmac and the best light reflecting off the Grimselsee.

roads.name: Furka Pass

official.name: Furka Pass
official.description: Gletsch to Realp at 2,429 m, past the Rhône Glacier and the hotel Belvédère from Goldfinger

roads.why: A legendary driving road steeped in motoring history and immortalized by the James Bond film Goldfinger, offering dramatic views down to the retreating Rhône Glacier.
roads.drive: The eastern ramp out of Realp features famous, perfectly stacked hairpin turns held up by ancient dry-stone walls. The road is narrow with minimal guardrails in places, requiring precise steering and respect for oncoming traffic.
roads.tips: Drive early in the day to avoid tour buses; stop at the Hotel Belvédère hairpin for the classic photo angle.

spots.name: Wassen Church
spots.why: The iconic white church perched on a rocky outcrop is famously seen from multiple railway tiers and the start of the Susten climb.

spots.name: Stein Glacier Viewpoint
spots.why: A breathtaking roadside pullout offering direct, up-close views of the retreating blue ice and roaring waterfalls.

spots.name: Susten Pass Summit
spots.why: The high point of the pass features a long tunnel, wide parking areas, and staggering panoramic views of the surrounding peaks.

spots.name: Furka Pass Eastern Hairpins
spots.why: The legendary zig-zag road ascending from Realp offers a classic framing for automotive and landscape photography.

spots.name: Hotel Belvédère
spots.why: The abandoned historic hotel sits dramatically on the curve overlooking the Rhône Glacier ice cave entrance.

spots.name: Grimsel Hospiz
spots.why: A historic mountain inn perched above the reservoir offering hearty Swiss food, local pastries, and incredible terrace views.

plan.title: Innsbruck to Lake Como via Stelvio and the Dolomites
plan.summary: This 4-day driving enthusiast trip crosses legendary Alpine passes from Innsbruck through the dramatic peaks of the Dolomites and over the famous Stelvio Pass into Italy's lake district. Experience tight hairpins, deep valleys, and world-class mountain roads.

days.title: Through the Dolomites to Cortina
days.summary: Leave Innsbruck behind and climb into the Austrian Alps before dropping across the Italian border toward the jagged peaks of the Dolomites. The driving highlight is transitioning from wide alpine valleys onto the sweeping stretches of the SS48 as it leads you past Dobbiaco and into the heart of the mountains. Expect dramatic limestone walls framing the road and an effortless, high-altitude alpine flow.
days.stay: Stay in the scenic center of Cortina d'Ampezzo near the main pedestrian promenade, choosing between family-run alpine lodges, boutique chalet-style hotels, or cozy traditional B&Bs.

days.title: Great Dolomite Road to Bolzano
days.summary: Tackle the legendary Great Dolomite Road from east to west, conquering high mountain passes like the Falzarego and the Pordoi. The road serves up relentless hairpin turns, plunging valley views, and towering rock faces that change color in the shifting light. It is an engineering masterpiece and a playground for drivers who love rhythmic, technical elevation changes.
days.stay: Stay in central Bolzano within walking distance of the historic arcades and squares, with a great selection of modern design hotels, historic inns, and comfortable alpine-urban guesthouses.

days.title: Over the Stelvio Pass
days.summary: This is the ultimate bucket-list driving day, ascending the northern ramp of the Stelvio Pass up its famous 48 numbered stone-wall hairpins. The grade is steep and the exposure is real, but the reward at the 2,757-meter summit is one of the most breathtaking panoramas in the Alps. The descent toward Bormio brings you through tunnels and fast sweepers into Lombardy.
days.stay: Stay in historic central Bormio near the thermal baths, featuring traditional mountain hotels, thermal resort lodges, and classic Italian family-run guesthouses.

days.title: Down to Lake Como
days.summary: Wind down from the high peaks by cruising south along the Valtellina valley toward Tirano before cutting across toward Lecco and the shores of Lake Como. The road shifts from dramatic alpine gorges to sparkling lakeside avenues framed by cypress trees and historic villas. It is a scenic, relaxed finale that lets you enjoy the transition from rugged peaks to Mediterranean-style blue water.
days.stay: Stay in Como's old town near the lakefront promenade, choosing from grand historic hotels, elegant boutique properties, or charming lakeside bed and breakfasts.

roads.name: Great Dolomite Road

official.name: Great Dolomite Road
official.description: Bolzano to Cortina d'Ampezzo over the Costalunga, Pordoi and Falzarego passes through the Dolomites

roads.why: It connects Bolzano to Cortina through some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in the world, offering continuous panoramic views of vertical limestone cliffs, deep green valleys, and high-altitude alpine passes.
roads.drive: A well-paved two-lane mountain highway featuring numerous switchbacks, tunnels, and sustained grades up to 10%. It requires smooth throttle and brake control, especially when sharing the road with cyclists, tour buses, and motorbikes.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning to beat the heavy tourist traffic and camper vans. The road is typically fully open from late spring through October, but snow can temporarily close high passes outside of summer. Keep an eye on your fuel gauge as stations are spaced out.

roads.name: Stelvio Pass
roads.segment: from Prato allo Stelvio to Bormio

official.name: Stelvio Pass
official.description: From Prato allo Stelvio up 48 numbered hairpins to 2,757 m, then down to Bormio: the most famous pass road in the Alps

roads.why: It is the highest paved mountain pass in the Eastern Alps, legendary among driving enthusiasts and cyclists for its iconic wall of 48 numbered hairpins on the northern side and stunning views of the Ortler massif.
roads.drive: Narrow, steep (up to 11% grade), and exposed with no guardrails on many upper turns. The northern ascent from Prato allo Stelvio demands total concentration, precise steering, and respect for oncoming traffic, particularly large buses and sports cars.
roads.tips: Tackle this climb right at 8:00 AM before the cyclists and heavy traffic arrive. Open strictly seasonally from roughly late May to October, weather permitting. Check local conditions for sudden snow closures, and ensure your brakes are in top condition.

spots.name: Brenner Pass
spots.why: The historic and major low pass across the Alps that marks the border between Austria and Italy.

spots.name: Lago di Braies
spots.why: A stunning emerald-green alpine lake framed by the sheer vertical cliffs of the Dolomites, famous for its historic wooden boathouses.

spots.name: Passo di Falzarego
spots.why: A dramatic high mountain pass offering sweeping vistas of jagged peaks, fortifications from the First World War, and a soaring cable car.

spots.name: Passo Pordoi
spots.why: One of the four famous passes of the Sella Ronda loop, offering a sweeping parking area right beneath the massive Sella and Marmolada groups.

spots.name: Stelvio Pass Summit
spots.why: Stand at 2,757 meters surrounded by snow-dusted peaks, grab a famous local hot sausage, and look down at the dizzying expanse of hairpin turns.

spots.name: Bagni Vecchi di Bormio
spots.why: Historic thermal baths carved into the rock face with panoramic outdoor pools overlooking the Bormio basin.

spots.name: Santuario di Our Lady of Tirano
spots.why: A magnificent Renaissance basilica in Tirano known for its ornate marble facade and stunning interior artwork.
spots.wiki: Santuario della Beata Vergine di Tirano

spots.name: Lecco Lakefront
spots.why: A scenic vantage point where the Adda river exits Lake Como's southeastern branch, backed by the dramatic limestone peak of Monte Resegone.
