plan.title: Pacific Coast Odyssey: Seattle to San Diego
plan.summary: Embark on an epic 8-day journey down the West Coast, tracing the legendary Pacific Coast Highway. Experience dramatic coastal cliffs, sweeping ocean views, towering redwoods, and iconic California beach towns.

days.title: Seattle to Tillamook
days.summary: Starting from Seattle, you head south on I-5 before cutting across to the rugged Washington coast via Aberdeen. The drive picks up its true coastal character as you cross the massive Astoria-Megler Bridge into Oregon, finishing with a cruise down the Pacific Coast Scenic Byway to Tillamook. Expect a mix of fast highway cruising, sweeping river valleys, and your first taste of dramatic ocean bluffs.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Tillamook or a cozy coastal B&B nearby, where you can easily find welcoming motels and lodges close to the famous local dairy creamery.

days.title: Tillamook to Gold Beach
days.summary: Today is a marathon of raw Pacific coastline, winding you past endless sandy beaches, rocky headlands, and dense evergreen forests. You will pass through quiet harbor towns like Newport and Florence, where the road hugs dramatic sea cliffs and crosses massive coastal bridges. The atmosphere transitions from misty northern timberlands to the wild, windy shores of southern Oregon.
days.stay: Stay in Gold Beach near the mouth of the Rogue River, choosing from classic riverfront motels or cozy roadside lodges.

days.title: Gold Beach to Fort Bragg
days.summary: Crossing into California, the road plunges you immediately into the majestic, towering gloom of the Redwood National and State Parks. The driving transitions from coastal bluffs to tight, twisting passages canopied by ancient giants before you reconnect with Route 1 at Leggett. The final stretch to Fort Bragg delivers you to rugged northern California cliffs and crashing surf.
days.stay: Stay near the historic downtown or coastal bluffs of Fort Bragg, featuring charming Victorian inns, boutique motels, and ocean-view lodges.

days.title: Fort Bragg to Half Moon Bay
days.summary: You wind southward along California Route 1 through the artsy village of Mendocino and past sleepy fishing coves before hitting the urban density of San Francisco. After navigating the Golden Gate, the route continues down the Peninsula past Half Moon Bay. It is a day of dramatic contrasts, moving from remote redwood-shaded cliffs to bustling bayside metropolitan roads.
days.stay: Stay in Half Moon Bay near the downtown historic district or along the scenic coastal bluffs, enjoying local inns and comfortable beachside motels.

days.title: Half Moon Bay to Big Sur
days.summary: Leaving Half Moon Bay, you cruise past Santa Cruz and Monterey before entering the crown jewel of the Pacific Coast Highway: Big Sur. Here, the road clings precariously to sheer vertical cliffs dropping straight into the churning blue ocean. The driving is technical, slow, and endlessly jaw-dropping as you cross iconic spans like Bixby Creek Bridge.
days.stay: Stay in a rustic mountain cabin or luxury cliffside lodge nestled within the majestic redwoods and dramatic slopes of Big Sur.

days.title: Big Sur to San Simeon
days.summary: Continuing south through the remainder of the Big Sur coast, the road unwinds slightly as it approaches the sunny central coast. You will experience more breathtaking cliffside vistas, rocky coves where sea lions lounge, and a noticeable warming of the weather. The day ends around San Simeon, where the mountains begin to recede into rolling golden hills.
days.stay: Stay near San Simeon or the nearby coastal village of Cambria, choosing from charming vintage motels or pine-shaded country lodges.

days.title: San Simeon to Santa Barbara
days.summary: Cruising past Morro Bay and Pismo Beach, you transition from Route 1 back onto the faster US-101 corridor toward Santa Barbara. The landscape shifts to sun-drenched valleys, agriculture, and Spanish colonial architecture framed by the Santa Ynez Mountains. It is a relaxed, sun-soaked drive with wide multi-lane stretches and classic southern California coastal vibes.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Santa Barbara or near the waterfront, where Spanish-style boutique hotels, cozy inns, and upscale resorts abound.

days.title: Santa Barbara to San Diego
days.summary: Your final stretch takes you past the iconic beaches of Malibu, through the sprawling urban energy of Los Angeles, and down the fast-paced I-5 corridor. The traffic picks up significantly, demanding your full attention as you navigate major interstate junctions. You finish the journey by dropping into the vibrant, sun-drenched coastal cityscape of San Diego.
days.stay: Stay in downtown San Diego or near the historic Gaslamp Quarter, offering everything from chic urban hotels to classic coastal resorts.

roads.tips: Drive northbound if possible to stay in the lane closest to the ocean for easy pullouts, and always check for major winter storm closures.

roads.tips: Great for sunset cruising, but keep an eye out for wildlife viewing traffic near elephant seal rookeries.

plan.title: Utah Mighty Five and Scenic Byway 12 Adventure
plan.summary: This 6-day loop from Salt Lake City explores Utah's most spectacular red rock national parks. Experience the thrill of driving Scenic Byway 12, Zion Canyon, and the dramatic landscapes of Capitol Reef and Arches.

days.title: From Salt Lake City to Zion National Park
days.summary: You head south out of Salt Lake City on the interstate, watching the Wasatch Range flatten into the vast desert expanses of central Utah. The final stretch brings you into the dramatic red rock canyons of Zion via a winding approach. It is a transition from high-altitude city life straight into the glowing sandstone towers of the southwest.
days.stay: Stay right in Springdale for immediate access to the park entrance and restaurants within walking distance. Look for cozy riverside lodges or boutique motels that offer shaded patios and stunning views of the surrounding cliffs.

days.title: Through Zion and Bryce Canyon
days.summary: Today involves climbing out of Zion's deep gorges through the historic switchbacks and descending into high-desert pine forests. You will cruise past open range country toward the sprawling amphitheaters of Bryce Canyon. The feel is a stunning contrast between plunging canyon floors and dizzying high-altitude rims.
days.stay: Stay near Bryce Canyon City to catch sunset and sunrise over the hoodoos without dealing with a long evening drive. Options lean toward rustic western-themed lodges, cabin rentals, and well-equipped local motels.

days.title: The Journey on Scenic Byway 12
days.summary: You will tackle one of America's absolute crown jewel highways, crossing narrow hogbacks with sheer drop-offs on both sides. The route sweeps through the stark grandeur of Grand Staircase-Escalante before climbing forested mountain passes down into Torrey. Expect heart-pounding ridges and sweeping geological layers that change every few miles.
days.stay: Stay in the quiet farming community of Torrey, which acts as the peaceful western gateway to Capitol Reef. Choose from charming historic motels, rustic cabins, or local inns offering dark-sky stargazing.

days.title: Capitol Reef to Moab
days.summary: This leg takes you through the waterpocket folds of Capitol Reef before opening up into vast, martian expanses around Hanksville. After connecting to the interstate, you roll into Moab, the adrenaline capital of eastern Utah. The drive shifts from remote geological wonders to a bustling hub of adventure.
days.stay: Stay right in downtown Moab to be close to the lively local restaurants, gear shops, and brewpubs. Expect a mix of modern adventure hotels, classic roadside motels, and resort properties.

days.title: Exploring Arches and Canyonlands
days.summary: A day dedicated to exploring the immense stone arches and staggering river canyons flanking Moab. You will wind your way up along the Colorado River gorge on a paved ribbon set against towering crimson cliffs. The driving is relaxed, leaving maximum time to stare up at natural rock architecture.
days.stay: Stay again in Moab, giving you a second night to settle in and enjoy the evening restaurant scene after a full day on the trails. Consider local lodges or comfortable inns with gear-washing stations and secure parking.

days.title: Return to Salt Lake City
days.summary: You head north out of Moab, joining the transcontinental interstate before cutting west through stark desert valleys and high mountain passes. The final stretch brings you back down into the Salt Lake Valley, closing the loop. It is an efficient highway run that lets you process a week of incredible scenery.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Salt Lake City or the surrounding valley to enjoy top-tier urban dining and craft breweries. Choose from modern boutique hotels, historic properties, or convenient airport-adjacent lodgings.

official.name: Zion Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic route through Zion Canyon, the Mt. Carmel Tunnel, and the red rock country of southern Utah

roads.why: It winds directly through the heart of Zion Canyon and climbs sheer sandstone cliffs via the historic Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel. Drivers rave about the dramatic lighting on the towering rock walls and the tight, carved rock windows.
roads.drive: Features a steep climb with tight switchbacks and a narrow, unlit historic tunnel where oversized vehicles require escorts. Traffic can be heavy with tourists and buses, so best driven early in the morning.
roads.tips: Watch for cyclists and pedestrians, especially near park shuttle stops. Keep your headlights ready for the tunnel.

official.name: Scenic Byway 12 (Journey Through Time)
official.description: Scenic drive through canyons, plateaus, and valleys

roads.why: Widely considered one of the greatest driving roads in North America, traversing high alpine forests, deep red canyons, and the legendary Hogback ridge. The combination of sweeping curves and exposed razor-edge drop-offs delivers pure driving excitement.
roads.drive: Includes steep grades, tight switchbacks, and sections with zero shoulders perched atop narrow sandstone fins. Traffic is generally light compared to national parks, allowing a steady rhythm.
roads.tips: Check weather reports as parts of the road exceed 9,000 feet and can experience sudden snow or high winds. Fill up with gas in Escalante or Boulder.

plan.title: Appalachian Ridges and Curves
plan.summary: This 3-day loop combines the winding spine of the Blue Ridge Parkway with the legendary curves of the Tail of the Dragon and the soaring ridgetops of the Cherohala Skyway. Experience the best motorcycle and sports car driving roads in the American Southeast, balanced with comfortable mountain towns.

days.title: Blue Ridge Parkway to Cherokee
days.summary: Begin your journey climbing onto the ridge from Asheville, meandering south along the scenic crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The landscape transitions from dense forests to sweeping pastoral valleys, with the best stretch running along the high elevations near Mount Pisgah. Expect a relaxed pace with numerous scenic overlooks as you trace the contour of the ancient ridge.
days.stay: Stay in Cherokee near the reservation entrance, choosing from comfortable mountain motels, riverside lodges, or local bed and breakfasts.

days.title: Tail of the Dragon and Cherohala Skyway
days.summary: Tackle legendary tarmac today, transitioning from the sweeping curves of the Dragon to the soaring ridgetop vistas of the Cherohala Skyway. The drive features dense tree canopies, deep river valleys, and an intense succession of tight, technical turns followed by vast panoramic mountain views. It is an adrenaline-filled day for driving enthusiasts set in the remote Southern Appalachians.
days.stay: Rest in Robbinsville in a cozy local lodge, rustic cabin rental, or classic roadside motel offering easy access to the surrounding passes.

days.title: Back to Asheville via Great Smokies
days.summary: Conclude your loop by traversing the high passes of the Cherohala Skyway and cutting through the heart of the Great Smoky Mountains along US 441. The day features dramatic elevation changes, winding descents into Tennessee, and a scenic climb back toward North Carolina. The feel is a rewarding mix of wilderness solitude and vibrant mountain culture before returning to Asheville.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Asheville near the South Slope or historic districts, featuring boutique hotels, historic B&Bs, and stylish urban inns.

roads.name: Blue Ridge Parkway

official.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
official.description: Scenic drive along America's longest linear park and the winding spine of the Blue Ridge Mountains

roads.why: Renowned for its engineering marvel, gentle continuous curves, and uninterrupted views across endless ridge lines without commercial billboards.
roads.drive: Smooth asphalt with a strict 45 mph speed limit, rolling grades, numerous short tunnels, and occasional heavy tourist traffic or fog at higher elevations.
roads.tips: Go early in the morning to avoid slow-moving RV traffic; check for winter or weather-related gate closures before setting out.

roads.name: Tail of the Dragon
roads.segment: from Fontana Dam to Deals Gap

official.name: Tail of the Dragon
official.description: US 129 at Deals Gap: 318 curves in 11 miles, America's most famous road for motorcycles and sports cars

roads.why: World-famous for having 318 curves in just 11 miles, offering an intense test of machine and driver concentration.
roads.drive: Tight, relentless second- and third-gear switchbacks with no intersecting driveways, bordered by steep drop-offs and dense forest walls.
roads.tips: Ride or drive on weekday mornings to avoid aggressive sports car and motorcycle crowds; stay entirely in your lane.

roads.name: Cherohala Skyway

official.name: Cherohala Skyway
official.description: Ridgetop drive in the Appalachians

roads.why: A masterpiece of modern highway engineering soaring above 5,000 feet, delivering breathtaking panoramic views of deep wilderness valleys.
roads.drive: Wide sweeping sweepers, long gentle grades, excellent sightlines, and very little commercial traffic compared to nearby routes.
roads.tips: Temperatures drop significantly at the highest elevations, so pack an extra layer even in summer; watch out for wandering wildlife.

plan.title: Vancouver to Calgary through the Rockies
plan.summary: This 4-day road trip takes you from the Pacific coast into the heart of the Canadian Rockies, featuring legendary alpine passes, turquoise lakes, and dramatic coastal cliffs. Experience some of the finest driving roads in North America, including the Sea-to-Sky Highway and the Icefields Parkway.

days.title: Vancouver to Cache Creek
days.summary: This incredible drive transitions from coastal ocean views up the Sea-to-Sky corridor into the dramatic alpine forests of Whistler, before dropping into the arid, desert-like canyons around Lillooet. The best stretch is the winding ascent of Duffey Lake Road, offering sweeping mountain vistas and pristine glacier lakes. It feels like a rapid transition through multiple distinct climate zones in just a few hours.
days.stay: Stay in Cache Creek to experience a classic highway stopover, where comfortable roadside motels and rustic motor inns cater well to road-trippers.

days.title: Cache Creek to Golden
days.summary: You will trace the historic routes carved through the rugged British Columbia interior, following swift-flowing rivers and massive mountain ranges. The best stretch cuts through Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park, where the towering snow-capped peaks dwarf the highway. The day feels like a masterclass in Canadian engineering and raw wilderness scale.
days.stay: Stay in Golden near the Kootenay Rockies area, choosing between cozy mountain lodges, modern alpine chalets, and well-equipped motels.

days.title: Golden to Jasper
days.summary: This is widely considered one of the absolute greatest road trips in the world, driving the spine of the Canadian Rockies on the Icefields Parkway. The best stretch runs past the massive Columbia Icefield, where ancient glaciers spill down right toward the asphalt. The feel of the day is humbling and awe-inspiring, surrounded by endless walls of ice and rock.
days.stay: Stay in Jasper for a true mountain town atmosphere, offering alpine cabins, charming bed and breakfasts, and forest lodges.

days.title: Jasper to Calgary
days.summary: The final push takes you back south down the legendary Icefields Parkway before crossing over high alpine passes and descending into the rolling foothills of Alberta. The best stretch is tackling Highwood Pass, the highest paved highway in Canada, sweeping past pristine alpine meadows. It finishes with a transition from remote wilderness directly into the energetic urban vibe of Calgary.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Calgary or the vibrant inner-city neighborhoods, featuring a wide variety of boutique hotels and modern urban apartments.

roads.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway

official.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway
official.description: Vancouver to Whistler and Pemberton along Howe Sound, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief, climbing into the Coast Mountains

roads.why: It clings dramatically to the cliffside above Howe Sound before climbing into the Coast Mountains, offering continuous ocean and mountain panoramas.
roads.drive: A well-paved, multi-lane highway with sweeping curves, moderate grades, and occasional heavy commuter traffic near Vancouver.
roads.tips: Watch out for wildlife and heavy weekend tourist traffic; start early to enjoy the best views.

roads.name: Duffey Lake Road

official.name: Duffey Lake Road
official.description: Highway 99 beyond Pemberton to Lillooet: steep grades, tight switchbacks and glacier-fed Duffey Lake, a favourite loop for Vancouver drivers

roads.why: A fantastic winding mountain road that offers incredible elevation changes, tight switchbacks, and stunning turquoise lakes.
roads.drive: Steep grades and tight corners demand attention, but the road surface is generally good with light traffic compared to the coast.
roads.tips: Fill up in Pemberton as services are sparse until Lillooet; check for seasonal rockfall alerts.

roads.name: Fraser Canyon Highway

official.name: Fraser Canyon Highway
official.description: The Trans-Canada from Hope through the Fraser Canyon to Cache Creek, through tunnels above the river and past Hell's Gate

roads.why: Follows the historic gold rush trail through deep, dramatic river canyons carved by the Fraser River.
roads.drive: Fast highway stretches interspersed with winding canyon sections, tunnels, and railway crossings.
roads.tips: Keep an eye out for falling rocks and slow freight trucks navigating the grades.

roads.name: Icefields Parkway

official.name: Icefields Parkway
official.description: Lake Louise to Jasper along the Continental Divide past Bow Lake, Peyto Lake and the Columbia Icefield, one of the world's great drives

roads.why: World-renowned for its uninterrupted views of over a hundred ancient glaciers, roaring waterfalls, and jagged peaks.
roads.drive: Wide two-lane highway with gentle sweepers and long sightlines, though grades can be steep and winter weather can strike anytime.
roads.tips: No cell service along the entire route; fuel up in Lake Louise or Jasper before heading out.

roads.name: Highwood Pass
roads.why: The highest paved pass in Canada takes you deep into Kananaskis Country above the tree line with breathtaking alpine bowl views.
roads.drive: Steep climbs and sharp turns with stunning drop-offs; very quiet compared to the main trans-Canada route.
roads.tips: Closed seasonally from December to mid-June for wildlife conservation; bring a jacket as it is always cold at the top.

spots.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
spots.why: A famous swaying footbridge high above the forest floor providing a dramatic start to the journey.

spots.name: Shannon Falls Provincial Park
spots.why: The third highest waterfall in British Columbia plunges dramatically right off the highway cliff.

spots.name: Whistler Village
spots.why: A world-class alpine resort town with incredible mountain backdrops and great dining options.

spots.name: Duffey Lake Provincial Park
spots.why: Offers an easily accessible lakeside viewpoint reflecting the massive peaks of the Cayoosh Range.

spots.name: Revelstoke Railway Museum
spots.why: Showcases the rich history of the Canadian Pacific Railway through Rogers Pass.

spots.name: Giant Cedars Boardwalk Trail
spots.why: A short, easy loop through an ancient inland cedar rainforest with massive centuries-old trees.

spots.name: Glacier National Park of Canada
spots.why: Protects the heart of the Columbia Mountains and the legendary Rogers Pass.

spots.name: Emerald Lake
spots.why: A stunning turquoise alpine lake nestled in Yoho National Park just off the main route.

spots.name: Lake Louise
spots.why: Famous for its vibrant turquoise glacial waters framed by Mount Victoria.

spots.name: Bow Lake
spots.why: A classic photo stop where Crowfoot Glacier feeds a crystal-clear mountain lake.

spots.name: Columbia Icefield
spots.why: One of the largest non-polar ice fields in North America, feeding multiple major rivers.

spots.name: Sunwapta Falls
spots.why: A powerful pair of waterfalls fed by the Sunwapta River plunging into a limestone canyon.

spots.name: Athabasca Falls
spots.why: A breathtaking waterfall renowned for its sheer force and carved gorge views.

spots.name: Banff National Park
spots.why: Canada's oldest national park featuring unmatched mountain scenery and abundant wildlife.

spots.name: Kananaskis Country
spots.why: A massive provincial park system offering pristine wilderness and dramatic mountain passes away from the crowds.

spots.name: Calgary Tower
spots.why: Provides a panoramic view of the city skyline and the distant Rocky Mountains.

plan.title: Southern Alps Grand Alpine Loop
plan.summary: Experience the majestic landscapes of New Zealand's South Island, traversing alpine passes, turquoise glacier-fed lakes, and the wild West Coast. Drive across Arthur's Pass, view Aoraki Mount Cook, and journey through Haast Pass down to Queenstown.

days.title: Christchurch to Fox Glacier
days.overnight: Fox Glacier, West Coast, New Zealand
days.summary: Cross the Canterbury Plains before climbing into the dramatic gorges of Arthur's Pass, where the road carves through the Southern Alps. Descend past the Otira Gorge rockfall shelter into the lush rainforests of the West Coast before heading south to Fox Glacier.
days.stay: Stay near the village center close to the glacier access points in alpine motels, rainforest lodges, or holiday parks.

days.title: Fox Glacier to Mount Cook Village
days.overnight: Mount Cook Village, Canterbury, New Zealand
days.summary: Leave the West Coast and travel through dense native forest before winding up the Haast Pass into the stunning lakes district of Otago. Conclude the drive by turning onto the legendary Mount Cook Road, running parallel to the startling turquoise waters of Lake Pukaki.
days.stay: Stay within the alpine settlement of Mount Cook Village at traditional lodges, motels, or the historic Hermitage area.

days.title: Mount Cook Village to Haast
days.summary: Depart Mount Cook Village and sweep past Lake Tekapo across the high tussock-covered plains of the Mackenzie Basin. Head south toward Omarama, enjoying the wide-open skies and sweeping glacial valley panoramas.
days.stay: Stay in central Omarama near the soaring gliding country, choosing from comfortable motels, motor lodges, or local B&Bs.

days.title: Haast to Omarama
days.summary: Navigate the rolling hills of the Waitaki Valley before climbing up and over the stark, golden alpine landscape of the Lindis Pass. Descend into the vibrant lakeside resort town of Wānaka for stunning views of the surrounding peaks.
days.stay: Stay near the Wānaka lakefront in boutique hotels, serviced apartments, or lakeside motels.

days.title: Omarama to Queenstown
days.summary: Drive from Wānaka over the Crown Range Road—New Zealand's highest sealed main highway—featuring breathtaking switchbacks and panoramic lookouts. Finish the journey by descending into the bustling adventure capital of Queenstown nestled beside Lake Wakatipu.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Queenstown close to the Steamer Wharf for easy access to restaurants, lake cruises, and alpine lodges.

roads.name: Arthur's Pass

official.name: Arthur's Pass
official.description: The Great Alpine Highway from Christchurch over the Southern Alps, past Castle Hill and over the Otira Viaduct to Greymouth

roads.why: It is a dramatic alpine crossing featuring massive viaducts, roaring rivers, and a stark transition from eastern tussock to western rainforest.
roads.drive: Steep grades, sweeping curves, and the famous Otira Viaduct with some exposed sections. Watch for changing weather and keas.
roads.tips: Check road conditions before starting, as snow can close the pass in winter. Fill up in Darfield or Springfield.

roads.name: Great Coast Road

official.name: Great Coast Road
official.description: Westport to Greymouth along the wild Tasman coast past the Pancake Rocks at Punakaiki

roads.why: Renowned for its wild Tasman Sea coastal vistas, dramatic rock formations, and dense native nikau palm forests right beside the highway.
roads.drive: A mix of rolling coastal curves and gentle straights with occasional sea spray on the windshield during high tides and storms.
roads.tips: Allow extra time for photography stops at the coastal viewpoints. Keep headlights on.

roads.name: Haast Pass

official.name: Haast Pass
official.description: Wānaka past Lakes Hāwea and Wānaka, over the Haast Pass and down past the Blue Pools and waterfalls to the West Coast

roads.why: A pristine rainforest highway cutting through Mount Aspiring National Park, offering access to numerous waterfalls and deep gorge rivers.
roads.drive: Narrow sections with tight bends, dense bush canopy, and several one-way bridges. Drive defensively and mind campervans.
roads.tips: Cell service is non-existent here. Fuel up before entering the pass at Haast or Makarora.

roads.name: Lindis Pass

official.name: Lindis Pass
official.description: Tussock-covered pass between the Mackenzie Basin and Central Otago, one of the South Island's great open roads

roads.why: Offers a surreal, sweeping desert-like alpine landscape covered in golden tussock grass that changes colors dramatically with the light.
roads.drive: A smooth, well-graded highway with long sweeping curves and a steady climb to over 900 meters of elevation.
roads.tips: Can experience severe winter gales and black ice; drive with caution during frost season.

roads.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook Road
roads.segment: from Twizel to Mount Cook Village

official.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook Road
official.description: Along turquoise Lake Pukaki straight at Aoraki / Mount Cook, ending at the village under New Zealand's highest peak

roads.why: Provides arguably the most photogenic approach in the world, driving straight toward the towering mass of Aoraki/Mount Cook framed by Lake Pukaki.
roads.drive: Mostly flat and straight with wide shoulders, but high crosswinds can occur near the lake edge.
roads.tips: Pull over only in designated view areas; do not stop on the active roadway to take photos.

plan.title: Desert & Mountain Loop: LA to Death Valley
plan.summary: An unforgettable desert and mountain loop exploring the twists of Angeles Crest Highway and the vast, otherworldly landscapes of Death Valley National Park.

days.title: Through the San Gabriel Mountains to Barstow
days.summary: Escape the LA basin by climbing the legendary Angeles Crest Highway into the crisp alpine air of the San Gabriel Mountains. After sweeping through high-altitude pine forests and past deep canyon drop-offs, descend into the Mojave Desert and cruise northeast toward Barstow. It is a thrilling transition from urban gridlock to vast open highway.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Barstow or near the I-15 corridor, where you will find classic roadside motels and standard chain hotels offering easy access for an early morning push into the desert.

days.title: Into Death Valley National Park
days.summary: Dash north up the interstate before cutting across the stark Mojave desert toward the dramatic entrance of Death Valley. Drop below sea level via lonely desert byways, watching the landscape shift into vast salt flats and painted badlands. The drive offers a true sense of remoteness as you plunge into the lowest basin in North America.
days.stay: Stay right in the heart of Furnace Creek at historic desert lodges or resort-style accommodations that put you within walking distance of the oasis palms.

days.title: Exploring Central Death Valley
days.summary: Spend the day exploring the surreal subterranean and desert landscapes of central Death Valley, driving along the edge of massive salt pans and colorful volcanic driveways. The routes are wide, flat, and endlessly expansive, letting you soak in the intense scale of the desert floor. Finish the day drifting westward toward the towering sand dunes of Stovepipe Wells.
days.stay: Stay at the rustic desert village in Stovepipe Wells, where cozy motel rooms and a legendary saloon provide a genuine old-school frontier outpost experience.

days.title: Out of the Basin to Ridgecrest
days.summary: Climb out of the Death Valley basin via dramatic mountain passes that test your car's cooling system and reward you with sweeping views of Panamint Valley. The road unfurls across wide desert floors before rising steadily toward the aerospace hub of Ridgecrest. It is a stark, cinematic drive through some of California's most isolated backcountry.
days.stay: Stay in Ridgecrest where you will find reliable modern hotels, reliable chain motels, and local eateries clustered along the main thoroughfare.

days.title: Back to Los Angeles
days.summary: Head south down CA-14 through the high desert wind farms of Mojave and the aerospace expanse of Palmdale before diving back through the mountain passes toward the Los Angeles basin. The final stretch is a straightforward highway run that transitions from sparse Joshua tree country back into the sprawling metropolis. It is an efficient and varied return trip to complete the loop.
days.stay: Stay in central Los Angeles or near your departure neighborhood to easily unpack and reflect on your desert and mountain adventure.

roads.name: Angeles Crest Highway
roads.segment: from La Cañada Flintridge to Wrightwood

official.name: Angeles Crest Highway
official.description: La Cañada Flintridge through the San Gabriel Mountains to Wrightwood, Los Angeles' favourite mountain drive

roads.why: Renowned among Southern California driving enthusiasts for its endless succession of sweeping curves, perfect asphalt, and dizzying mountain ridges.
roads.drive: Involves constant elevation changes, tight switchbacks, and steep drop-offs with minimal guardrails in places. Watch out for cyclists and weekend sports cars, and drive it northbound from La Cañada for the best rhythm.
roads.tips: Check for rockslide closures after winter storms, start early to beat the traffic, and top off your fuel before leaving La Cañada.

roads.name: Death Valley Scenic Byway
roads.segment: from Death Valley Junction to Panamint Springs

official.name: Death Valley Scenic Byway
official.description: Scenic drive through the expansive desert basin of the lowest place in North America

roads.why: Offers an otherworldly journey through extreme geological contrasts, sweeping from towering mountain ranges down to below-sea-level salt flats.
roads.drive: Generally wide, long, straight desert stretches interspersed with occasional sweeping grades and tight canyon passes. Heat management is critical.
roads.tips: Carry plenty of drinking water, watch your vehicle's temperature gauge, and fill up on fuel whenever an opportunity arises.

plan.title: Norway Fjord and Alpine Adventure
plan.summary: This six-day expedition takes you through the heart of Norway's iconic landscapes, traversing deep fjords, the famous Trollstigen pass, and the dramatic Atlantic Ocean Road. Experience the blend of coastal culture and high-mountain engineering on some of the world's most spectacular scenic routes.

days.title: Bergen to Flåm
days.summary: Begin your journey leaving the cultural hub of Bergen behind, cutting inland through dramatic tunnels and lush valleys toward the deep waters of the Sognefjord. The drive offers a steady introduction to Norwegian engineering and sweeping mountain passes before descending into the dramatic fjord arms. Expect a smooth cruise on well-paved trunk roads with steadily intensifying coastal and mountain scenery.
days.stay: Stay right down by the fjord in Flåm within walking distance of the harbor, choosing between boutique fjord hotels, cozy guesthouses, or traditional wooden cabins.

days.title: Flåm to Loen
days.summary: Tackle the high plateau of the Snow Road before dropping down toward the inner reaches of the Nordfjord to reach Loen. The transition from barren, snow-patched alpine heights to lush green valleys is one of the most striking contrasts in the region. The driving involves navigating steep mountain walls and narrow stretches that demand full attention.
days.stay: Stay near the edge of the lake in Loen, opting for historic resort hotels, modern fjord-side lodges, or well-equipped family campsites.

days.title: Loen to Geiranger
days.summary: Traverse the scenic Gamle Strynefjellsvegen old mountain road if open, where hand-stacked stone walls frame ancient glaciers and rugged peaks. Finish the day by dropping down the famous Eagle Road switchbacks into the legendary Geirangerfjord. This is a day defined by monumental scale, sheer cliffs, and cascading waterfalls around every blind corner.
days.stay: Stay perched on the steep slopes overlooking the Geirangerfjord in Geiranger, where you can find upscale fjord hotels, traditional chalets, or scenic hillside campsites.

days.title: Geiranger to Åndalsnes
days.summary: Ascend from Geiranger on steep winding roads and take the ferry across the Norddalsfjorden before conquering the iconic Trollstigen mountain road. The eleven hairpin turns dropping down a sheer cliff face past the thundering Stigfossen waterfall provide a masterclass in civil engineering. The day ends with a gentle descent into the dramatic valley of Åndalsnes.
days.stay: Stay in the mountaineering hub of Åndalsnes near the train station or fjord shore, choosing from comfortable town hotels, climbers' lodges, or local guesthouses.

days.title: Åndalsnes to Kristiansund
days.summary: Roll northward toward the coast, crossing bridges and fjords until you hit the cinematic Atlantic Ocean Road that hops across wave-lashed skerries. The drive combines sheltered inland fjords with exposed ocean architecture where the sea spray can reach the tarmac on windy days. It is a thrilling coastal route that feels like driving on the edge of the world.
days.stay: Stay in the historic fishing town of Kristiansund on the harbor front, selecting from modern city hotels, classic coastal inns, or converted wharf apartments.

days.title: Kristiansund to Ålesund
days.summary: Conclude your trip with a scenic coastal transit featuring ferry crossings and sweeping island bridges leading into the Art Nouveau city of Ålesund. The final stretch balances tranquil coastal waters with grand mountain backdrops reflecting in the sea. Finishing in Ålesund rewards you with some of the finest architectural urban scenery in Scandinavia.
days.stay: Stay right in the central Art Nouveau district of Ålesund within walking distance of the canal, enjoying design hotels, historic brick inns, or cozy central B&Bs.

roads.name: Aurlandsvegen
roads.why: Known as the Snow Road, this national tourist route takes you over an Arctic-like barren plateau far above the fjords with lingering snowbanks even in summer.
roads.drive: Narrow single-lane sections with passing places, steep inclines from Aurland, exposed drops without guardrails in places, and closed during winter and spring.
roads.tips: Check local road status for snow accumulation before heading up; fuel up in Aurland as there are no services on the mountain.

roads.name: Geiranger and the Eagle Road

official.name: Geiranger and the Eagle Road
official.description: Down the Ørnesvingen hairpins to the Geirangerfjord and up to Dalsnibba's viewpoint at 1,500 m; the classic link to Trollstigen

roads.why: Offers breathtaking plunging views over the UNESCO-listed Geirangerfjord and features eleven dramatic hairpin bends scaling the mountain wall.
roads.drive: Steep 10 percent gradients with tight hairpins, heavy tourist bus traffic in peak summer, best driven ascending from Geiranger for maximum visual impact.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning or late evening to avoid tour bus queues at the hairpin viewpoints.

roads.name: Trollstigen

official.name: Trollstigen
official.description: Eleven hairpins up a sheer valley wall past the Stigfossen waterfall, between Åndalsnes and Valldal; closed in winter

roads.why: Norway's most famous mountain road, celebrated for its gravity-defying switchbacks, stone bridges, and roaring waterfalls.
roads.drive: Extremely steep with an 9 percent gradient, sharp hairpin turns, sheer drops, and narrow road width requiring careful maneuvering around large vehicles.
roads.tips: Strictly seasonal opening from late spring to autumn; check weather forecasts and brake gently on the descent to avoid overheating.

roads.name: Atlantic Ocean Road

official.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
official.description: A string of low bridges and causeways hopping across skerries in the open sea between Molde and Kristiansund

roads.why: An engineering marvel that snakes across an archipelago of flat islets and skerries in the open Norwegian Sea, connected by sweeping bridges.
roads.drive: Exposed coastal driving with sweeping curves and undulating bridges that can feel like rollercoasters when ocean swells are high.
roads.tips: Can be extremely windy; watch out for sudden gusts and enjoy the designated parking pullouts for photography.

spots.name: Tvindefossen
spots.why: A multi-tiered cascading waterfall right off the main road that has inspired myths of eternal youth.

spots.name: Flåm Railway
spots.why: One of the steepest standard-gauge railway lines in the world, plunging through dramatic mountain tunnels.

spots.name: Stegastein Viewpoint
spots.why: A spectacular wooden viewing platform jutting 30 meters out over the cliff edge, 650 meters above the Aurlandsfjord.

spots.name: Loen Skylift
spots.why: One of the steepest cable cars in the world, lifting visitors from the fjord to Mount Hoven in minutes.

spots.name: Gamle Strynefjellsvegen
spots.why: A historic hand-built mountain road passing raw stone walls, blue lakes, and summer snowfields.

spots.name: Flydalsjuvet
spots.why: A famous rocky outcrop providing the quintessential postcard view down into the Geirangerfjord.

spots.name: Ørnesvingen
spots.why: The Eagle's Bend viewpoint looks straight down onto Geiranger village and cruise ships far below.

spots.name: Trollstigen Visitor Centre
spots.why: Modern architectural masterpiece featuring cantilevered viewing platforms hanging over the abyss.

spots.name: Storseisundet Bridge
spots.why: The most dramatic and photographed bridge on the Atlantic Ocean Road, curving gracefully over the sea.

spots.name: Kjeungskjær Lighthouse
spots.why: An octagonal red stone coastal lighthouse sitting on a tiny islet in the stormy waters.

spots.name: Aksla Viewpoint
spots.why: Overlooks the entire Art Nouveau town of Ålesund, the surrounding islands, and the majestic Sunnmøre Alps.

spots.name: Jugendstilsentre
spots.why: Museum dedicated to the stunning Art Nouveau architecture that defines downtown Ålesund.

plan.title: Iceland Ring Road Adventure
plan.summary: This 8-day circumnavigation of Iceland showcases the island's dramatic contrast between black-sand beaches, vast glaciers, and volcanic fields. Experience the iconic Ring Road, visiting the majestic waterfalls of the South Coast, the remote fjords of the East, and the geothermal wonders of the North.

days.title: South Coast Waterfalls
days.summary: Begin your journey along the dramatic south coast, passing through sweeping coastal plains framed by towering glaciers and cascading waterfalls. The best stretch brings you beneath the towering cliffs of Vík, where crashing waves meet striking black sand beaches. The driving is relaxed and straightforward on well-paved tarmac, offering constant coastal views.
days.stay: Vík offers cozy guesthouses and boutique countryside lodges nestled right against the dramatic sea cliffs.

days.title: Glaciers and Lagoons
days.summary: Drive past massive glacial tongues and sprawling outwash plains that showcase the raw power of Vatnajökull. The highlight is the ethereal floating iceberg lagoon at Jökulsárlón, where you can watch chunks of ancient ice drift out to sea. The road here is wide and fast, hugging the coastline with majestic mountain backdrops.
days.stay: Höfn is a charming fishing village where you can find comfortable guesthouses and family-run hotels.

days.title: The East Fjords
days.summary: Tackle the winding coastal roads of the East Fjords, where steep, rust-colored mountains drop straight into deep blue waters. The best stretch wraps closely around the jagged shoreline of Berufjörður, providing sweeping vistas at every turn. Expect narrow stretches and sweeping curves that demand your full attention.
days.stay: Egilsstaðir serves as the regional hub, offering modern hotels, cozy guesthouses, and excellent lakeside camping.

days.title: Northern Wonders
days.summary: Traverse the stark, Martian-like volcanic interior of the north before witnessing the staggering scale of Dettifoss. The driving changes from coastal curves to vast, windswept plateaus dominated by geothermal activity and ancient lava fields. The road is smooth and allows for steady progress across the barren highlands.
days.stay: Mývatn features comfortable nature hotels and geothermal spa lodges situated amidst volcanic wonders.

days.title: Arctic Coast to Akureyri
days.summary: Cruise through fertile northern valleys and make a stop at the majestic 'Waterfall of the Gods' before reaching the vibrant capital of the north. The driving is easygoing, characterized by rolling green hills and wide river valleys. Enjoy a relaxed pace as you approach the picturesque shores of Eyjafjörður.
days.stay: Akureyri is a lively cultural hub offering stylish boutique hotels, apartments, and welcoming guesthouses.

days.title: Northwest Landscapes
days.summary: Journey along the rugged Arctic coast and through scenic mountain passes that cut across the northern peninsulas. The best driving involves sweeping coastal curves overlooking the deep blue waters of Húnaflói. The route is peaceful and uncrowded, giving you a true sense of remote Icelandic wilderness.
days.stay: Laugarbakki provides quiet countryside hotels and comfortable lodge-style accommodations ideal for a restful evening.

days.title: Snæfellsnes Peninsula
days.summary: Explore the miniature wonderland of the Snæfellsnes Peninsula, flanked by jagged peaks and the imposing Snæfellsjökull glacier. The highlight is driving right along the ocean's edge with Kirkjufell mountain dominating the horizon. The road undulates gently through lava fields and sleepy fishing villages.
days.stay: Stykkishólmur offers charming historic guesthouses and harbor-view accommodations in a colorful coastal town.

days.title: Return to Reykjavik
days.summary: Complete your epic island loop by cutting back south across rolling moorlands and through the long Hvalfjörður tunnel. The final stretch brings you back into the lively urban atmosphere of the world's northernmost capital. The road is fast, modern, and entirely paved, bringing your grand road trip to a smooth close.
days.stay: Reykjavik features a wide variety of accommodations, from luxury design hotels to cozy guesthouses right in the city center.

roads.name: Ring Road

official.name: Ring Road
official.description: Around the whole island: south-coast waterfalls and black beaches, glacier lagoons, the East Fjords and the lava fields of the north

roads.why: It is the legendary highway that circumumnavigates the entire island, offering access to glaciers, black sand beaches, fjords, and volcanic fields all from a single ribbon of asphalt.
roads.drive: Mostly two-lane paved road with occasional single-lane bridges, sweeping curves, and changing weather conditions. Best driven counter-clockwise to tackle the south coast first.
roads.tips: Check weather and road conditions daily on road.is; fuel stations are frequent in the south and west but sparse in the east and north.

roads.name: Snæfellsnes Road

official.name: Snæfellsnes
official.description: Iceland in miniature: Kirkjufell, lava fields, black-sand coves and the Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano

roads.why: Often called 'Iceland in miniature,' this coastal road loops past dramatic sea cliffs, volcanic craters, and the iconic pyramid peak of Kirkjufell.
roads.drive: Well-paved, rolling coastal highway with some tight turns around fjords and headlands. Can be very windy.
roads.tips: Watch for sudden gusts of wind when passing mountains; allow extra time for frequent photo stops.

spots.name: Seljalandsfoss
spots.why: A famous waterfall that you can actually walk completely behind for a unique perspective and great photos.

spots.name: Skógafoss
spots.why: Massive 60-meter high waterfall thundering down ancient sea cliffs, with a staircase leading to panoramic views above.

spots.name: Reynisfjara
spots.why: Striking black sand beach featuring dramatic basalt column formations and offshore sea stacks.

spots.name: Skaftafell
spots.why: A stunning wilderness area nestled against the edge of Vatnajökull glacier with incredible hiking trails.

spots.name: Jökulsárlón
spots.why: A breathtaking glacial lagoon filled with giant floating icebergs calving off the retreating Breiðamerkurjökull glacier.

spots.name: Diamond Beach
spots.why: Black sand shore where sparkling chunks of glacial ice wash ashore, creating a stunning contrast against the dark sand.

spots.name: Djúpivogur
spots.why: A tranquil historic fishing village featuring charming harbor buildings and unique outdoor art installations.

spots.name: Dettifoss
spots.why: Reputed to be the most powerful waterfall in all of Europe, cascading down into the rugged Jökulsárgljúfur canyon.

spots.name: Hverir
spots.why: An otherworldly geothermal area bubbling with mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and vibrant mineral deposits.

spots.name: Goðafoss
spots.why: The 'Waterfall of the Gods' curves in a magnificent horseshoe shape steeped in early Icelandic history.

spots.name: Akureyri Church
spots.why: Prominent modernist Lutheran church dominating the hillside overlooking the scenic Eyjafjörður fjord.

spots.name: Varmahlíð
spots.why: A charming hillside village known as the heart of Iceland's horse country and scenic river valleys.

spots.name: Kirkjufell
spots.why: The most photographed mountain in Iceland, famously framed alongside a winding double waterfall.

spots.name: Stykkishólmur
spots.why: A picturesque harbor town characterized by well-preserved old wooden houses and dramatic volcanic islands offshore.

spots.name: Borgarnes
spots.why: A historic coastal settlement rich in Viking sagas, offering great views across the Borgarfjörður fjord.

spots.name: Hallgrimskirkja
spots.why: Reykjavik's iconic expressionist parish church offering towering architectural design and panoramic city views from its top.

plan.title: Wild Atlantic Way: Galway to the Ring of Kerry
plan.summary: This 5-day journey explores the rugged beauty of Ireland's Atlantic coast, taking you through the limestone landscapes of the Burren and the dramatic peninsulas of the southwest. Experience some of the island's most iconic coastal roads and mountain passes before culminating in the lush scenery of the Ring of Kerry.

days.title: Galway to Ennistymon
days.summary: Begin your journey leaving Galway behind and driving south along the rugged coast of County Clare. The highlight is the dramatic coastal stretch past limestone pavements where the Atlantic crashes right against the stone. Expect a scenic and leisurely drive into the heart of traditional music country.
days.stay: Stay in the vibrant town of Ennistymon, known for its historic Falls Hotel and lively local pubs. Look for charming local B&Bs or guesthouses within walking distance of the cascades.

days.title: Ennistymon to Killarney
days.summary: Drive south past dramatic cliffs and board the Shannon ferry to cross into County Kerry. The landscape shifts from desolate coastal fringes to lush green pastoral hills as you approach the iconic town of Killarney. The coastal roads offer sweeping views of the wild sea before heading inland.
days.stay: Stay near the center of Killarney or close to the national park entrance to easily access the evening atmosphere and dining. Traditional B&Bs and upscale inns dominate the local hospitality scene.

days.title: Killarney to Dingle
days.summary: Tackle the dramatic heights of Conor Pass before looping around the stunning Dingle Peninsula. This day is all about narrow cliffside roads, breathtaking ocean vistas, and ancient stone monuments. The feel is remote, windswept, and intensely dramatic.
days.stay: Stay right in Dingle town to enjoy the bustling harborfront and renowned seafood restaurants. Cozy townhouses and local family-run guesthouses are your best bet here.

days.title: Dingle to Sneem
days.summary: Embark on the famed Ring of Kerry, winding past deep lakes, majestic mountains, and rugged ocean headlands. The driving is varied, alternating between wide scenic coastal stretches and tighter, forested mountain passes. The sheer scale of the landscape makes for an unforgettable day on the road.
days.stay: Stay in the picturesque village of Sneem, famous for its colorful houses and tranquil riverside setting. Look for quiet countryside lodges or friendly local B&Bs.

days.title: Sneem to Kenmare
days.summary: Conclude your trip by crossing the breathtaking Healy Pass with its mesmerizing serpentine curves. The mountain crossing delivers incredible views over sea loughs before descending into charming Kenmare. It is a triumphant final driving day that leaves you fully immersed in southwestern Ireland's wild beauty.
days.stay: Stay in the heritage town of Kenmare, celebrated for its gourmet food scene and charming architecture. Boutique hotels and high-end guesthouses provide a comfortable end to the journey.

roads.name: The Burren

official.name: The Burren
official.description: Limestone pavement country by the Atlantic, with the coast road past Black Head and the Corkscrew Hill

roads.why: Famous for its surreal, vast limestone karst landscape that resembles the surface of the moon, contrasting sharply with the crashing Atlantic waves.
roads.drive: Narrow, rolling coastal roads with minimal shoulders and frequent sheep on the tarmac. Drive from north to south for the best ocean views.
roads.tips: Watch out for cyclists and sudden gusts of wind along the coast. Fill up your tank before leaving Galway.

roads.name: Slea Head Drive

official.name: Slea Head Drive
official.description: Around the tip of the Dingle Peninsula: Atlantic cliffs, beehive huts and the Blasket Islands offshore

roads.why: Renowned as one of the most scenic coastal drives in Europe, offering dramatic cliff edges, ancient beehive huts, and panoramic views of the Blasket Islands.
roads.drive: A narrow, winding one-way loop in places with steep drop-offs and tight turns. Best driven counter-clockwise to keep the ocean on your side.
roads.tips: Tour buses must travel clockwise, so following the counter-clockwise rule prevents meeting them head-on in tight spots.

roads.name: Conor Pass

official.name: Conor Pass
official.description: Ireland's highest mountain pass, a narrow road over the Dingle Peninsula with lakes below; not for big vehicles

roads.why: It is the highest mountain pass in Ireland, offering heart-stopping drops, glacial valleys, and sweeping views of both sides of the Dingle Peninsula.
roads.drive: Extremely narrow with sheer cliffs, single-lane stretches, and steep switchbacks that require patience and concentration.
roads.tips: Avoid driving this pass in heavy fog or high winds. Large vehicles are prohibited; stick to cars.

roads.name: Ring of Kerry

official.name: Ring of Kerry
official.description: The classic loop of the Iveragh Peninsula from Killarney: Ladies View, Moll's Gap and the coast past Waterville and Sneem

roads.why: A legendary touring route showcasing Ireland's finest coastal scenery, rugged mountains, deep lakes, and historic heritage sites.
roads.drive: A mix of fast national roads and tight, winding coastal stretches that can get heavily congested with tour buses in peak season.
roads.tips: Drive counter-clockwise starting from Killorglin to avoid getting stuck behind slow-moving tour buses.

roads.name: Healy Pass

official.name: Healy Pass
official.description: Hairpins over the Caha Mountains on the Beara Peninsula with views of Glanmore Lake

roads.why: A dramatic mountain pass carved through the Caha Mountains, offering some of the most thrilling hairpin turns and cinematic vistas in the country.
roads.drive: Steep, serpentine switchbacks with no guardrails in sections and stunning exposure. Best driven from north to south.
roads.tips: Check the weather before setting out, as mist and low clouds can obscure the road and ruin the views.

spots.name: Dunguaire Castle
spots.why: A picturesque 16th-century tower house sitting dramatically on a rocky promontory overlooking Kinvara Bay.

spots.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen
spots.why: An iconic Neolithic portal tomb dating back over 5,000 years, standing defiantly in the middle of the barren limestone landscape.

spots.name: Cliffs of Moher
spots.why: Ireland's most famous natural wonder, rising over 200 meters above the churning Atlantic Ocean.

spots.name: Kilkee Cliffs
spots.why: Spectacular and less-crowded coastal cliffs offering dramatic sea stacks and roaring surf views.

spots.name: Tarbert-Killimer Ferry
spots.why: A relaxing shortcut across the Shannon Estuary that frequently features playful dolphins escorting the ferry.

spots.name: Torc Waterfall
spots.why: A stunning 20-meter-high waterfall cascading through dense woodland in Killarney National Park.

spots.name: Inch Beach
spots.why: A vast and scenic sandy spit stretching out into Dingle Bay, famous as a filming location.

spots.name: Gallarus Oratory
spots.why: An exceptionally well-preserved early Christian church built entirely from dry-stone corbelled masonry.

spots.name: Conor Pass Viewpoint
spots.why: Offers breathtaking bird's-eye views over the carved glacial valleys and distant lakes of the peninsula.

spots.name: Rossbeigh Strand
spots.why: A gorgeous sandy beach backed by dramatic cliffs, offering sweeping views across Dingle Bay.

spots.name: Molls Gap
spots.why: A high mountain pass providing magnificent panoramic vistas over the MacGillycuddy's Reeks mountain range.

spots.name: Ladies View
spots.why: A legendary vantage point overlooking the Killarney lakes, named after Queen Victoria's ladies-in-waiting who admired the scenery.

spots.name: Derreen Garden
spots.why: A magical 19th-century woodland garden featuring exotic plants, giant tree ferns, and tranquil walking trails.

spots.name: Healy Pass Summit
spots.why: The ultimate photo spot at the crest of the pass, looking down at the dramatic snake-like road below.

spots.name: Kenmare Stone Circle
spots.why: An impressive Bronze Age megalithic structure featuring a massive boulder dolmen at its center.

plan.title: Andalusia Highlights Road Trip
plan.summary: This five-day journey explores the heart of Andalusia, connecting vibrant cities with the dramatic landscapes of the Serranía de Ronda and the Sierra Nevada. You will experience legendary white towns, historic Moorish architecture, and some of Spain's most scenic mountain driving routes.

days.title: Málaga to Ronda
days.summary: You leave the Mediterranean coast behind and immediately climb into the dramatic limestone mountains of Andalusia. The highlight is the A-397, a relentless succession of sweeping curves and elevation changes that rewards drivers with sweeping views down to the sea. The day concludes with a dramatic arrival into Ronda, perched precariously over a sheer gorge.
days.stay: Stay in the historic center near the famous Puente Nuevo to experience the atmospheric old town on foot, choosing a traditional whitewashed guesthouse or a historic parador.

days.title: White Towns and Seville
days.summary: Cruising through the heart of the Sierra de Grazalema Natural Park, you navigate the breathtaking mountain pass of the A-372. The route connects iconic cliffside white villages framed by jagged peaks and rolling olive groves. By afternoon, the landscape flattens as you roll into the vibrant streets of Seville.
days.stay: Look for accommodation in the vibrant Santa Cruz or Triana neighborhoods, featuring charming boutique hotels or classic Andalusian patio apartments.

days.title: Seville Exploration
days.summary: A full day dedicated to exploring Seville on foot and discovering its world-class architectural marvels. The driving is paused, allowing you to absorb the lively street life, Moorish palaces, and shady orange groves. The feel is relaxed yet deeply culturally immersive.
days.stay: Keep your accommodation in central Seville for another night to easily enjoy the evening tapas scene without needing a taxi.

days.title: Seville to Granada
days.summary: You make fast progress eastward along the wide Andalusian plains using the A-92 highway, offering big-sky views of endless rolling hills covered in olive trees. The transition brings you toward the imposing backdrop of the Sierra Nevada mountains. The day ends in Granada, where Moorish history and modern student energy collide.
days.stay: Stay in the historic Albaicín quarter for unbeatable views of the Alhambra across the valley, typically in a converted Moorish house or charming local inn.

days.title: Granada and Sierra Nevada
days.summary: You tackle the legendary A-395, climbing steeply from Granada straight into the jagged heights of the Sierra Nevada. The asphalt winds through dramatic switchbacks and alpine scenery right up to Spain's highest highway terminus. The descent brings you back to Granada for a final celebratory evening.
days.stay: Conclude your trip in the city center near the cathedral, staying in a comfortable historic hotel that reflects the city's rich heritage.

roads.name: White Towns of Andalusia
roads.segment: from Ronda to Arcos de la Frontera

official.name: White Towns of Andalusia
official.description: Ronda, Grazalema, Zahara and Arcos de la Frontera on hilltops over the Sierra de Grazalema

roads.why: This route links some of Spain's most visually striking hilltop settlements through a rugged limestone biosphere reserve, offering thrilling driving dynamics and jaw-dropping valley overlooks.
roads.drive: The road features moderate grades, tight hairpins, and occasional agricultural traffic, best driven from east to west for optimal morning sun on the whitewashed facades.
roads.tips: Watch out for wandering livestock and cyclists, and ensure you have a full tank before leaving Ronda as stations are sparse in the park.

roads.name: Sierra Nevada

official.name: Sierra Nevada
official.description: From Granada up into Spain's highest mountains, and the Alpujarras' white villages on the southern slopes

roads.why: As the highest paved road in Spain, the A-395 offers an incredible alpine driving experience with thin air, dramatic drop-offs, and sweeping vistas stretching to the Mediterranean on clear days.
roads.drive: A relentless climb with wide sweepers, steep 10% grades, and occasional strong crosswinds near the top. Drive early in the day to avoid cloud cover.
roads.tips: Check for winter snow closures even in spring, carry extra warm layers, and watch for cyclists training on the grades.

spots.name: Balcón de Ronda
spots.why: Offers vertigo-inducing views over the El Tajo gorge and the fertile valley below.

spots.name: Puente Nuevo
spots.why: The iconic 18th-century bridge spanning the deep chasm that divides Ronda's old and new towns.

spots.name: Puerto de las Palomas
spots.why: A stunning high mountain pass offering panoramic views across the Grazalema natural park.

spots.name: Grazalema
spots.why: A postcard-perfect whitewashed village nestled dramatically beneath jagged limestone crags.

spots.name: Arcos de la Frontera
spots.why: A dramatic cliff-edge town that serves as the gateway to the Pueblos Blancos route.

spots.name: Real Alcázar of Seville
spots.why: A breathtaking royal palace showcasing stunning Mudéjar architecture and lush historic gardens.

spots.name: Seville Cathedral
spots.why: The largest Gothic cathedral in the world, housing the tomb of Christopher Columbus and the Giralda tower.

spots.name: Plaza de España, Seville
spots.why: An architectural masterpiece built for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition, featuring tiled alcoves representing Spanish provinces.

spots.name: Alcazaba of Antequera
spots.why: A historic Moorish fortress providing sweeping views over the fertile valley and the famous Torcal rock formations.

spots.name: Alhambra
spots.why: The pinnacle of Moorish art and architecture in Spain, featuring intricate palaces and the Generalife gardens.

spots.name: Mirador de San Nicolás
spots.why: The ultimate sunset photo spot offering a classic postcard view of the Alhambra backed by the Sierra Nevada.

spots.name: Pradollano
spots.why: The ski resort village perched high in the Sierra Nevada, offering striking alpine architecture and mountain air.

spots.name: Hoya de la Mora
spots.why: A high-altitude parking area and trailhead near the summit zone with sweeping views across the highest peaks of mainland Spain.

plan.title: Scenic Roads of Provence and the Verdon Gorge
plan.summary: A 5-day driving tour through the heart of Provence, taking in the dramatic limestone cliffs of the Gorges du Verdon, the lavender fields of the Luberon, and spectacular alpine and coastal routes in the south of France.

days.title: From the Coast into the Pre-Alps
days.summary: Leave the Mediterranean coast and ascend into the rugged pre-Alps through the perfume capital of Grasse. You will enjoy a winding climb through limestone landscapes before reaching the dramatic entrance of the Verdon region.
days.stay: Stay in the medieval center of Castellane, which offers charming guesthouses and small boutique hotels tucked beneath the famous Rocher de la Baume.

days.title: Around the Grand Canyon of Verdon
days.summary: This is a spectacular day navigating the rim of the Grand Canyon of the Verdon, featuring turquoise water views and sheer cliff faces. Prepare for narrow, exhilarating stretches that offer some of the most iconic vistas in all of France.
days.stay: Moustiers-Sainte-Marie is a picturesque village built into a limestone cliff; look for a cozy stone-walled inn near the village center.

days.title: Through the Luberon Valley
days.summary: Transition from the deep canyons to the rolling lavender fields and ochre villages of the Luberon valley. The pace is more relaxed today as you drive through classic Provençal countryside dotted with olive groves and vineyards.
days.stay: Stay in Gordes, ideally in a traditional bastide or a converted farmhouse offering panoramic views over the valley.

days.title: To the High Routes of the Southern Alps
days.summary: Head north toward the high peaks where the Mediterranean influence gives way to alpine grandeur. The drive features steep climbs and sweeping vistas as you transition into the gateway of the Southern Alps.
days.stay: Jausiers is a tranquil alpine village perfect for a restful stay; focus on mountain lodges or historic villas turned into charming guesthouses.

days.title: Back to the Azure Coast
days.summary: Conquer the legendary Cime de la Bonette, the highest through-road in the Alps, surrounded by moon-like landscapes. Descend back toward the coast, trading the thin alpine air for the vibrant energy of the French Riviera.
days.stay: Conclude your trip in Nice, where staying near the Promenade des Anglais or the historic Old Town provides the perfect coastal send-off.

roads.name: Route des Grandes Alpes
roads.segment: from Grasse to Castellane and Barcelonnette

official.name: Route des Grandes Alpes
official.description: Lake Geneva to the Riviera over 16 passes including the Iseran, Galibier, Izoard and Bonette

roads.why: It is the premier alpine touring route in France, crossing multiple high mountain passes with breathtaking, ever-changing scenery.
roads.drive: Expect steep gradients and sharp hairpins, particularly near the mountain passes; it is well-paved but requires constant focus.
roads.tips: Check for seasonal snow closures as many passes are only fully open from June to October; fuel up in larger towns.

roads.name: Gorges du Verdon
roads.segment: from Castellane to Moustiers-Sainte-Marie and Apt

official.name: Gorges du Verdon
official.description: Around Europe's grandest canyon on the Route des Crêtes and the D952 above the turquoise Verdon river

roads.why: Renowned for its dramatic depth and intense turquoise river, it is widely considered Europe's most spectacular canyon drive.
roads.drive: The roads are quite narrow with significant exposure, so drive conservatively, especially during high-season tourist traffic.
roads.tips: The D952 road offers the best combination of safety and views; avoid peak midday hours in July and August.

roads.name: Col de la Bonette

official.name: Col de la Bonette
official.description: Jausiers to Saint-Étienne-de-Tinée with a summit loop to 2,802 m, the highest through road in Europe

roads.why: Famous for the loop at 2,802 meters, it is the highest through road in the French Alps and a pilgrimage for driving enthusiasts.
roads.drive: High altitude driving with minimal guardrails and steep, winding ascents; expect changing weather conditions at the summit.
roads.tips: Always carry a jacket even in summer; watch for cyclists who frequent this climb.

spots.name: Fort de Tournoux

spots.name: Cime de la Bonette Summit
spots.why: The peak of your drive at over 2,800 meters with expansive views across the Southern Alps.

spots.name: Promenade des Anglais
spots.why: The iconic waterfront walkway of Nice, perfect for celebrating the end of your journey by the sea.

plan.title: Tuscany and Amalfi Coast Road Trip
plan.summary: A 5-day journey from Rome through the rolling hills of Tuscany to the dramatic cliffs of the Amalfi Coast. Experience historic roads, scenic coastal drives, and rich Italian culture.

days.title: From Rome to Florence via Chianti
days.summary: Departing Rome, you cruise north on the fast autostrada before exiting into the heart of Italy's iconic rolling hills. The landscape shifts to cypress-lined avenues, medieval hilltop towns, and endless vineyards as you approach Tuscany. The final stretch into Florence offers sweeping valley views and a gentle introduction to Tuscan driving.
days.stay: Stay in central Florence near the historic district, where charming boutique hotels and upscale bed-and-breakfasts occupy centuries-old buildings within walking distance of major monuments.

days.title: Through Tuscany to Siena
days.summary: This day is a leisurely immersion into the Chianti wine region, cruising through dense forests and terraced vineyards. The driving is relaxed, defined by sweeping curves and postcard-perfect vistas around every turn. You will finish in the stunning medieval city of Siena.
days.stay: Stay within the historic walls of Siena in a traditional Tuscan guesthouse or historic inn that puts you right on the cobblestone streets near the Piazza del Campo.

days.title: South to Rome
days.summary: Heading south back toward Rome, you traverse the rustic landscapes of southern Tuscany and northern Lazio. The route passes volcanic lakes and ancient towns perched atop sheer cliffs. It is a scenic and historically rich transit day.
days.stay: Stay in Rome's vibrant Trastevere neighborhood for an authentic Roman evening filled with lively trattorias, staying in a local guesthouse or boutique hotel.

days.title: Heading South to Naples and Sorrento
days.summary: You head south along the bustling highway before peeling off toward the stunning Bay of Naples and the Sorrento Peninsula. The scenery transitions from urban sprawl to dramatic coastal cliffs dropping into the Tyrrhenian Sea. Traffic can be heavy, but the reward is reaching the dramatic Sorrentine cliffs.
days.stay: Stay in central Sorrento near the cliffside overlooks, choosing between classic grand hotels with sea views and intimate cliffside bed-and-breakfasts.

days.title: Along the Amalfi Coast
days.summary: Tackling the legendary Amalfi Drive is a masterclass in coastal motoring, hugging sheer limestone cliffs high above the blue Mediterranean. The road is narrow and exhilarating, winding through pastel-colored cliffside villages. Every pullout offers a breathtaking photo opportunity.
days.stay: Stay in the heart of Amalfi within walking distance of the historic cathedral and the harbor, enjoying a coastal room in a traditional Mediterranean hotel.

roads.name: Via Chiantigiana
roads.why: Renowned for winding through the heart of the Chianti wine region past endless vineyards, olive groves, and historic castles.
roads.drive: Well-paved with consistent curves and moderate elevation changes. Traffic can be heavy with tourists and delivery vans during midday.
roads.tips: Drive early in the morning to beat tour bus traffic. Watch out for cyclists on weekends.

roads.name: Amalfi Drive
roads.why: Universally celebrated as one of the most dramatic and scenic coastal drives in the world, carved directly into sheer vertical cliffs.
roads.drive: Extremely narrow, single-lane in places with tight switchbacks, heavy tourist bus traffic, and sheer drops to the sea with minimal guardrails.
roads.tips: Drive from west to east so you are on the mountain side rather than the cliff edge. Yield to large buses and use pullouts.

plan.title: Croatian Coast and Lakes Road Trip
plan.summary: A stunning 5-day journey along the dramatic Adriatic coastline from Dubrovnik to Split, before heading inland through the mountains to the turquoise lakes of Plitvice. Enjoy spectacular sea views, historic walled cities, and sweeping karst landscape drives.

days.title: Dubrovnik to Makarska
days.summary: Begin your journey along the stunning Dalmatian coast, tracing the winding cliffside curves overlooking the deep blue Adriatic Sea. The standout section crosses the Pelješac Peninsula before returning to the mainland for a dramatic run into Makarska. Expect breathtaking sea vistas and a relaxed Mediterranean atmosphere as you settle in.
days.stay: Stay near the historic center of Makarska close to the waterfront promenade, where you will find charming boutique guesthouses and comfortable local apartments.

days.title: Makarska to Split
days.summary: Drive north beneath the towering Biokovo mountain range, where the road hugs sheer drops and offers sweeping views of offshore islands. The stretch near Omiš narrows as it cuts through the Cetina River canyon gorge. Enjoy a vibrant coastal drive that blends rugged limestone cliffs with bustling seaside towns.
days.stay: Look for accommodation just outside the ancient walls of Split's Diocletian Palace, choosing from stylish urban guest rooms and historic stone apartments.

days.title: Split to Zadar
days.summary: Continue along the coastal highway past historic Venetian bell towers, ancient Roman ruins, and indented bays. The road opens up as you approach Zadar, offering smooth cruising alongside island-studded waters. Experience a harmonious blend of rich cultural history and modern coastal living.
days.stay: Book a place in the Zadar Peninsula near the Sea Organ, featuring cozy family-run inns and contemporary apartments within walking distance of the historic sights.

days.title: Zadar to Plitvica Selo
days.summary: Leave the coast behind and climb inland through the dramatic, sparsely populated landscapes of the Lika region. The road winds across stark karstic plateaus and rolling green hills before descending into the lush forested world of Plitvice. It is a striking transition from Mediterranean shores to alpine highlands.
days.stay: Stay in a traditional wooden lodge or cozy B&B within Plitvica Selo, placing you just minutes away from the upper park entrance.

days.title: Plitvica Selo to Zagreb
days.summary: Wind your way north through peaceful valleys and sleepy rural villages along the historic inland route towards the capital. The traffic picks up gradually as you approach Zagreb, signaling your arrival in a lively Central European cultural hub. The drive offers a quiet, scenic finale to your Croatian adventure.
days.stay: Book a hotel or guesthouse in Zagreb's Lower Town near Ban Jelačić Square, offering easy access to museums, cafes, and historic architecture.

roads.name: Adriatic Highway
roads.why: Renowned for its continuous panoramic views of the Adriatic Sea, dramatic cliffside routing, and sweeping curves that thrill driving enthusiasts.
roads.drive: Features rolling elevation changes, tight coastal bends, and occasional heavy tourist traffic in summer; driving northbound keeps you on the seaside lane.
roads.tips: Watch out for sudden gusts of the bura wind, start early to beat the tour buses, and ensure you have fuel before leaving major towns.

roads.name: Pelješac Road
roads.why: Winds through dramatic hillside vineyards and olive groves with sweeping vistas over the Pelješac channel and surrounding islands.
roads.drive: Generally well-paved with moderate grades and sweeping curves that offer excellent visibility and an engaging rhythm for drivers.
roads.tips: Combine the drive with a stop at local wine tasting rooms in Postup or Orebić, and watch for cyclists in warmer months.

roads.name: Lika Inland Route
roads.why: Offers a complete change of scenery through empty karst plateaus, dense pine forests, and historic rural Croatian countryside.
roads.drive: Straight stretches mixed with gentle sweepers and occasional sharp mountain passes; traffic is light compared to the coastal highway.
roads.tips: Temperatures can drop significantly in the mountains compared to the coast, so keep an extra layer handy and watch for wildlife.

spots.name: Dubrovnik City Walls
spots.why: Walk the massive medieval stone fortifications for iconic aerial views over the orange rooftops and the sparkling Adriatic Sea.

spots.name: Ston City Walls
spots.why: Explore Europe's longest defensive stone wall system, stretching dramatically across the steep hills above historic salt pans.

spots.name: Oyster Farm Bota Šare
spots.why: Taste exceptionally fresh oysters harvested directly from the pristine local waters of the Mali Ston Bay.

spots.name: Biokovo Skywalk
spots.why: Step out onto a thrilling horseshoe-shaped glass platform jutting out over a sheer cliff high above the Makarska Riviera.

spots.name: Brela Stone
spots.why: Photograph the iconic pine-covered limestone rock sitting just offshore in the crystal-clear turquoise waters.

spots.name: Cetina River Gorge
spots.why: Admire where the emerald-green river carves its dramatic final path through steep limestone cliffs into the sea at Omiš.

spots.name: Diocletian's Palace
spots.why: Wander through the remarkably preserved Roman retirement palace that now forms the beating heart of Split's old town.

spots.name: Trogir Historic Core
spots.why: Stroll a medieval island town showcasing a stunning blend of Venetian architecture, Romanesque churches, and narrow alleys.

spots.name: St. James Cathedral in Šibenik
spots.why: Marvel at a magnificent UNESCO-listed stone cathedral built entirely from interlocking slabs without mortar.

spots.name: Sea Organ Zadar
spots.why: Listen to the haunting, harmonious musical chords created by sea waves pushing air through underwater pipes.

spots.name: Zrmanja River Canyon
spots.why: Look down into the breathtaking, deep canyon carved by a turquoise river famous for serving as a backdrop in Winnetou films.

spots.name: Plitvice Lakes National Park
spots.why: Hike wooden boardwalks looping around a breathtaking chain of sixteen terraced turquoise lakes connected by cascading waterfalls.

spots.name: Rastoke Water Mill Village
spots.why: Discover a fairy-tale village built over rushing waterfalls where historic wooden watermills straddle crystal-clear streams.

spots.name: Zagreb Upper Town
spots.why: Explore the historic historic district featuring cobblestone streets, colorful tile-roofed churches, and panoramic city views.
