plan.title: Salta and the Quebrada Wonders
plan.summary: This circuit explores the dramatic red-rock landscapes, high-altitude vineyards, and colorful mountain ranges of Northwest Argentina. You will drive through the stunning Quebrada de Humahuaca and the winding Cuesta del Obispo on some of the country's most spectacular regional roads.

days.title: Salta to Purmamarca
days.summary: Begin by climbing out of the lush Lerma Valley into the arid, multi-colored cliffs of the Quebrada de Humahuaca. The transition from green hills to desert canyons is dramatic, culminating in the iconic layered peaks of Purmamarca.
days.stay: Stay in the heart of Purmamarca near the main plaza, where you can find charming boutique adobe inns and guesthouses.

days.title: Humahuaca Gorge Exploration
days.summary: Traverse the deep red landscapes of the Humahuaca Gorge as you head north through historic Andean villages. The drive is punctuated by frequent stops to admire indigenous heritage and the striking geological formations that line the river valley.
days.stay: Look for a rustic lodge or a traditional homestay near the center of Humahuaca to soak in the authentic mountain town atmosphere.

days.title: High Desert to Salinas Grandes
days.overnight: San Antonio de los Cobres, Salta
days.summary: Ascend to high-altitude plateaus, crossing the dizzying Cuesta de Lipán pass before reaching the vast white expanse of the salt flats. This is a day of extreme geography and thin air, requiring careful navigation across the remote Andean volcanic landscape.
days.stay: Opt for a simple, rugged guesthouse or lodge in San Antonio de los Cobres, as accommodation here is basic to reflect the remote location.

days.title: Cuesta del Obispo and Cafayate
days.summary: Experience the legendary gravel and paved stretches of the Cuesta del Obispo, offering heart-stopping views as you descend through narrow canyons. Transition from the stark highlands into the lush vineyards of the Cafayate region by late afternoon.
days.stay: Choose a vineyard hotel or a colonial-style inn on the outskirts of Cafayate for a tranquil experience among the vines.

days.title: Quebrada de las Conchas and Return
days.summary: Drive through the spectacular Quebrada de las Conchas, where wind and water have carved surreal, towering sandstone formations into the earth. Return to the vibrant city of Salta through fertile farmland to conclude the loop.
days.stay: Stay in a historic hotel or apartment near the Plaza 9 de Julio in central Salta to enjoy the city's lively evening culture.

roads.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca Route
roads.why: A UNESCO World Heritage site featuring incredible geological color variations and a deep history of Andean civilization.
roads.drive: Well-paved but winding road; watch for heavy tourist traffic and animals near the road edges.
roads.tips: Start early to avoid tour buses; fill up in Salta or San Salvador de Jujuy.

roads.name: Andean Plateau Route
roads.segment: from Purmamarca to San Antonio de los Cobres
roads.why: This route offers an incredible transition from the Cuesta de Lipán mountain pass to the surreal white expanse of high-altitude salt flats.
roads.drive: High exposure with significant elevation gains; steep switchbacks on the Cuesta de Lipán require low gear.
roads.tips: Carry extra water and check tire pressure; fuel is very limited after Purmamarca until San Antonio de los Cobres.

roads.name: Calchaquí Valley Scenic Road
roads.segment: from San Antonio de los Cobres to Payogasta
roads.why: Regarded as one of the most beautiful and rugged stretches of the famous RN40, passing through otherworldly desert scenery and isolated mountain communities.
roads.drive: Mostly gravel road with washboard surfaces; can be difficult after heavy rain, but very rewarding for adventurous drivers.
roads.tips: Four-wheel drive is highly recommended; check local road conditions at the police station before departing.

roads.name: Cuesta del Obispo Road
roads.why: The dramatic drop from the high plateau through the 'Bishop's Slope' offers some of the most intense and scenic switchbacks in Argentina.
roads.drive: Steep, narrow, and twisting sections that require total concentration; the views are stunning but the drop-offs are steep.
roads.tips: Drive during daylight hours to safely navigate the steep gradients and avoid afternoon fog.

roads.name: Quebrada de las Conchas Road
roads.why: Famous for its extraordinary red rock formations, including 'The Amphitheater' and 'The Devil's Throat', which rise abruptly from the desert floor.
roads.drive: Excellent paved road with sweeping curves and frequent pullouts for photography.
roads.tips: The afternoon sun hitting the red rocks makes for the best photos; watch for cyclists on the narrow shoulders.

spots.name: Cerro de los Siete Colores
spots.why: This mountain exhibits a stunning palette of seven colors caused by complex geological movements.

spots.name: Pucará de Tilcara
spots.why: An impressive pre-Inca fortification set atop a hill with commanding views of the valley.

spots.name: Cuesta de Lipán
spots.why: A legendary series of switchbacks reaching over 4,000 meters in elevation.

spots.name: Salinas Grandes

spots.name: Los Cardones National Park

spots.name: El Anfiteatro
spots.why: A natural, semi-enclosed sandstone chamber with incredible acoustics and towering red walls.

spots.name: Bodega El Esteco
spots.why: A historic winery in Cafayate where you can enjoy local Torrontés wine and high-end regional cuisine.

plan.title: Peruvian Highlands: Sacred Valley and Lake Titicaca
plan.summary: This five-day journey explores the heart of the Inca Empire, traversing the dramatic Sacred Valley before crossing the high Andean plains to the shores of Lake Titicaca. Experience historic ruins, vibrant mountain landscapes, and the unique culture of the Altiplano.

days.title: Cusco to Sacred Valley
days.summary: Begin your journey descending from the historic heights of Cusco into the lush green expanse of the Sacred Valley. The road winds along the Vilcanota River, offering sweeping views of agricultural terraces and towering peaks before arriving in Urubamba. It is a scenic introduction to Andean driving with manageable traffic and breathtaking vistas.
days.stay: Stay in central Urubamba or a quiet riverside eco-lodge for a relaxing night surrounded by dramatic mountain views. Accommodations range from charming boutique lodges to rustic country inns.

days.title: Sacred Valley Exploration
days.summary: Navigate the rolling hills of the Sacred Valley toward the remarkable salt evaporation ponds of Maras and the ancient fortress town of Ollantaytambo. The drive features narrow rural lanes and panoramic mountain backdrops that transport you deep into Incan history. Enjoy a thrilling day of discovery amid impressive ruins and cobblestone streets.
days.stay: Stay near the historic center of Ollantaytambo within walking distance of the fortress ruins. Cozy family-run guesthouses and traditional adobe boutique hotels are the standard here.

days.title: Across the Abra La Raya Pass
days.summary: Embark on a high-altitude climb across the dramatic Abra La Raya pass, the highest point of the journey, where snowy peaks meet vast altiplano skies. The highway challenges drivers with sweeping curves and steep grades before leveling out into the high-altitude plains leading toward Puno. Dress warmly and watch for grazing alpacas along the windswept shoulders.
days.stay: Stay close to the Plaza de Armas in Puno to easily explore the city's lively dining scene. Options include comfortable lakeside hotels and traditional urban B&Bs.

days.title: Lake Titicaca and Uros Islands
days.summary: Spend the day on the sparkling waters of Lake Titicaca, visiting the fascinating floating islands of Uros and the cultural hub of Taquile Island. While primarily a water-based excursion, the morning drive to the port offers lovely views of the expansive blue lake meeting the horizon. The atmosphere is serene, crisp, and deeply rooted in indigenous traditions.
days.stay: Return to your accommodation in Puno for a comfortable evening near the waterfront. Choose from modern hotels with lake views or charming local inns.

days.title: Return via Sillustani
days.summary: Drive north toward Juliaca, stopping to explore the enigmatic stone chullpas funeral towers at Sillustani overlooking Lake Umayo. The final stretch rolls gently across the high plateau before concluding the journey in the bustling commercial hub of Juliaca. It is a rewarding finale blending ancient archaeology with everyday Andean life.
days.stay: Conclude your trip in central Juliaca or head directly toward the airport area for departure. Accommodations here are primarily practical business hotels and standard regional motels.

roads.name: Sacred Valley Route
roads.why: This route connects the Incan capital of Cusco with the fertile agricultural heartland of the Sacred Valley, offering dramatic canyon views and riverside driving.
roads.drive: Paved two-lane highway with some steep descents out of Cusco, occasional speed bumps near villages, and moderate traffic.
roads.tips: Watch out for stray livestock and local transport vans; fill up in Cusco before departing.

roads.name: Andean Highlands Highway
roads.why: A legendary high-altitude traverse crossing the roof of the Peruvian Andes, offering stark mountain landscapes, high passes, and remote altiplano vistas.
roads.drive: Long stretches of well-paved highway with significant elevation gains up to Abra La Raya, featuring long sweeping bends and strong crosswinds.
roads.tips: Acclimatize to altitude before driving, carry warm layers, and check weather conditions for snow or ice at the pass.

spots.name: Sacsayhuamán

spots.name: Abra La Raya

plan.title: Bangladesh Coastal and Hill Tracts Road Trip
plan.summary: Drive from Chattogram down the scenic Cox's Bazar Marine Drive to Teknaf, then climb into the lush Bandarban hills for stunning views at Nilgiri.

days.title: Chattogram to Cox's Bazar
days.summary: Begin your journey heading south from the bustling port city of Chattogram along the busy N1 highway towards the coast. The landscape transitions from urban sprawl to flat agricultural plains dotted with villages before opening up near the coast. Enjoy the steady drive as you approach the world's longest natural sea beach.
days.stay: Stay in Cox's Bazar near the beachfront zone, choosing from a wide range of modern beach resorts and coastal lodges.

days.title: Marine Drive to Teknaf
days.summary: Drive south along one of the most scenic coastal highways in South Asia, sandwiched between the steep green hills and the crashing waves of the Bay of Bengal. The pavement is generally smooth, offering uninterrupted ocean panoramas and refreshing sea breezes all the way to Teknaf. The relaxed pace makes it an unforgettable cruising experience.
days.stay: Stay in Teknaf in a modest local guesthouse or regional hotel offering a quiet atmosphere near the Naf River.

days.title: Teknaf to Bandarban
days.summary: Leave the coast behind and head north towards the rugged interior of the Chittagong Hill Tracts. The road winds through rolling green hills and rural settlements, gradually increasing in elevation as you approach Bandarban. Traffic thins out, and the tropical hill scenery becomes increasingly lush and dramatic.
days.stay: Stay in Bandarban town close to the Sangu River, where you can find comfortable hillside eco-lodges and standard tourist hotels.

days.title: Bandarban Hills to Nilgiri
days.summary: Tackle the spectacular mountain road climbing deep into the highest peaks of Bangladesh toward Nilgiri. Expect steep gradients, sharp hairpin turns, and breathtaking drop-offs with panoramic views of endless cloud-shrouded valleys. This is the crown jewel of driving in the country, demanding full attention and rewarding you with alpine-like vistas.
days.stay: Stay overnight at the hilltop resort in Nilgiri, experiencing a unique stay above the clouds in government-run tourist cottages.

days.title: Nilgiri back to Chattogram
days.summary: Descend from the misty heights of Nilgiri and retrace your route through the winding hill roads before connecting back to the northbound N1 highway. The final leg brings you out of the mountains and back through vibrant rural countryside into Chattogram. The transition from remote wilderness to city life marks the end of your adventure.
days.stay: Stay in central Chattogram near the main commercial hubs, featuring upscale business hotels and comfortable city lodgings.

roads.name: Cox's Bazar Marine Drive
roads.why: It runs uninterrupted right along the edge of the Bay of Bengal, offering rare and unobstructed ocean views for miles.
roads.drive: A well-paved, two-lane road with very little heavy vehicle traffic, making for a smooth and relaxing coastal cruise.
roads.tips: Watch out for wandering pedestrians and stray animals near local settlements. Best driven in the late afternoon for sunset views.

roads.name: Bandarban Hill Road
roads.why: It is the premier mountain driving experience in Bangladesh, cutting through the highest and most remote ranges of the Chittagong Hill Tracts with stunning ridge-line views.
roads.drive: Steep climbs, tight switchbacks, and narrow stretches with significant exposure. Four-wheel drive or a well-maintained vehicle with good brakes is essential.
roads.tips: Check local military checkpoints and permit requirements before heading deep towards Thanchi. Fuel up fully in Bandarban town.

plan.title: Malaysia West Coast and Highlands Journey
plan.summary: A six-day cultural and scenic drive from Singapore up Malaysia's historic and highland spine, taking in the colonial charm of Malacca and George Town alongside the winding tea plantations of the Cameron Highlands.

days.title: From Singapore to Historical Malacca
days.summary: Cross the causeway from Singapore and head north on the fast North-South Expressway, leaving the bustling city behind for the palm oil plantations of Johor. The final stretch brings you into historical Malacca along quieter coastal lanes where Dutch and Portuguese influences shape the landscape. Expect smooth multi-lane cruising followed by relaxed regional driving as you approach the historical core.
days.stay: Stay in the Jonker Walk area within walking distance of the heritage night markets, choosing boutique heritage guesthouses or traditional Peranakan shophouse inns.

days.title: To the Capital and Royal Selangor
days.overnight: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur
days.summary: Drive north along the scenic coastal Federal Route 5, passing quiet fishing villages, mangrove estuaries, and coconut groves before turning inland towards the sprawling capital. The coastal sections offer a breezy, laid-back atmosphere that sharply contrasts with the high-energy urban approach into Kuala Lumpur. The driving is flat and straightforward with moderate coastal traffic.
days.stay: Stay near the Golden Triangle or Bukit Bintang for easy access to dining and transport, opting for modern high-rise apartments or comfortable boutique city hotels.

days.title: Climbing into the Cameron Highlands
days.summary: Leave the lowlands behind and tackle the legendary twisty climb of the Cameron Highlands Road, ascending sharply through dense, misty jungle and steep mountain valleys. The road features endless hairpin turns and dramatic drops, eventually leveling out into emerald tea plantations and cooler mountain air. It is an exhilarating drive that demands constant focus and rewards with breathtaking views.
days.stay: Stay in the main hub of Tanah Rata close to walking trails and local eateries, choosing cozy alpine-style lodges, homestays, or Tudor-inspired boutique hotels.

days.title: Descending to the Heritage Streets of Ipoh
days.summary: Descend from the highlands via the newer, wide-sweeping curves of the Simpang Pulai Highway, which offers smoother gradients and sweeping mountain vistas compared to the old road. You will drop rapidly back into the tropical lowlands before cruising into Ipoh, famous for its limestone karst topography and historic limestone cave temples. The drive transitions from misty mountain forest to dramatic dramatic limestone cliffs.
days.stay: Stay in Ipoh Old Town near the railway station and heritage mural trails, choosing restored vintage shophouse boutique hotels or comfortable heritage inns.

days.title: Across the Bridge to Penang Island
days.summary: Cruise north along the historical Federal Route 1 trunk road through sleepy rural towns, rubber estates, and colonial-era railway stops like Kuala Kangsar and Taiping. The route runs parallel to the modern highway but offers a much more authentic look at small-town Malaysian life before you cross the massive Penang Bridge onto the island. The driving is mostly flat and leisurely with occasional town traffic.
days.stay: Stay in George Town within the UNESCO World Heritage Zone, experiencing atmospheric heritage boutique hotels set inside historic Chinese shophouses.

days.title: Exploring George Town and Heritage Coast
days.summary: Complete a full circuit of Penang Island along the coastal Federal Route 6, winding past pristine beaches, fishing villages, and lush rainforest-covered hills. The road hugs the rugged coastline of Teluk Bahang before descending through the quiet orchards and winding backroads of Balik Pulau. It is a scenic and varied drive that showcases the island's diverse natural beauty.
days.stay: Stay right in the heart of George Town's historic core to be close to the world-renowned street food scene, staying in restored colonial mansions or stylish boutique hotels.

roads.name: North-South Expressway
roads.why: The primary arterial backbone of Peninsular Malaysia, connecting the southern border to the capital and beyond with smooth, high-speed asphalt.
roads.drive: A multi-lane divided highway with gentle curves, excellent paving, and consistent high-speed traffic. Watch out for sudden tropical downpours.
roads.tips: Ensure your Touch 'n Go card or RFID tag is sufficiently loaded for toll payments. Avoid morning and evening rush hours near major cities.

roads.name: Coastal Highway
roads.why: A charming alternative to the inland expressway, offering a glimpse into traditional coastal kampung life, mangrove swamps, and Straits of Malacca views.
roads.drive: A two-lane undivided federal road with occasional local traffic, speed bumps through villages, and flat, straightforward geometry.
roads.tips: Watch for motorbikes pulling out from side roads and pedestrians in village areas. Excellent spots for fresh coconut water along the way.

roads.name: Cameron Highlands Road
roads.why: One of Malaysia's most famous driving roads, celebrated for its relentless hairpin curves, steep elevation gains, and dramatic transition into cool cloud forests.
roads.drive: A notoriously winding, narrow two-lane mountain pass with steep grades and sheer drops on one side. Can be misty with heavy tourist bus traffic on weekends.
roads.tips: Drive in the morning to avoid afternoon mountain fog and rain. Check your brakes before descending and use lower gears to manage speed.

roads.name: Simpang Pulai Highway
roads.segment: from Kampung Raja to Simpang Pulai
roads.why: A modern engineering marvel offering a much wider, smoother, and faster descent from the highlands than the old Tapah route, featuring sweeping viaducts and valley views.
roads.drive: A wide two-lane highway per direction with gentle, well-banked sweepers and long stretches of steady downhill gradients. Much less stressful than Route 59.
roads.tips: Keep an eye on your speed as the smooth tarmac and wide lanes make it easy to accelerate. Watch for occasional rockfall warning signs.

roads.name: Old Trunk Road
roads.why: A historic colonial-era highway shaded by giant rain trees, connecting old tin-mining towns and offering a nostalgic journey through Malaysia's past.
roads.drive: A flat, undulating two-lane road passing through town centers with traffic lights, roundabouts, and occasional slow commercial trucks.
roads.tips: Take your time and stop at the heritage towns along the route. Speed limits are strictly enforced near towns with automated cameras.

roads.name: Penang Island Coastal Road
roads.segment: from George Town around Batu Ferringhi and Balik Pulau
roads.why: A breathtaking coastal loop that wraps around the northern and western capes of Penang, passing beaches, national parks, and remote fruit orchards.
roads.drive: A narrow, winding coastal road with tight corners, steep jungle climbs over the ridge, and occasional holiday congestion around Batu Ferringhi.
roads.tips: Drive clockwise starting early in the morning to enjoy unobstructed coastal views and beat the tour bus traffic around the northern beaches.

spots.name: Ayer Keroh R&R

spots.name: Jonker Street

spots.name: Port Dickson Waterfront

spots.name: Royal Selangor Visitor Centre
spots.why: Home to the world's largest pewter maker, where you can tour the factory and see master craftsmen at work.

spots.name: Batu Caves

spots.name: Lata Iskandar Waterfall
spots.why: A stunning multi-tiered roadside waterfall nestled in the jungle, ideal for a refreshing break during the steep mountain climb.

spots.name: Boh Tea Plantation
spots.why: Sprawling emerald-green tea terraces cascading down the mountain slopes with a clifftop cafe overlooking the estate.

spots.name: Cameron Bharat Tea Plantation
spots.why: A picturesque valley view of terraced tea fields right by the main road, highly accessible for quick landscape photos.

spots.name: Mossy Forest
spots.why: An ancient, misty mountain forest filled with gnarled trees, ferns, and mosses along an elevated boardwalk trail.

spots.name: Sam Poh Tong Temple
spots.why: A magnificent Chinese Buddhist temple built inside a natural limestone cave within a serene karst mountain setting.

spots.name: Ipoh Railway Station
spots.why: Known as the Taj Mahal of Ipoh, this stunning British colonial-era railway station features striking Moorish architecture.

spots.name: Ubudiah Mosque
spots.why: Widely regarded as one of Malaysia's most beautiful mosques, featuring striking golden domes and neoclassical architecture in Kuala Kangsar.

spots.name: Taiping Lake Gardens
spots.why: Malaysia's first public garden, set around historic mining pools with ancient rain trees arching dramatically over the water.

spots.name: Penang Bridge
spots.why: An iconic dual-lane suspension bridge spanning the channel to connect the mainland directly to Penang Island.

spots.name: Penang Botanic Gardens
spots.why: A lush, waterfall-backed valley park established during the British colonial era, teeming with tropical flora and resident monkeys.

spots.name: Batu Ferringhi Beach
spots.why: A famous stretch of sandy coastline along the northern shore offering panoramic views of the Andaman Sea.

spots.name: Entopia by Penang Butterfly Farm
spots.why: A massive tropical butterfly sanctuary and nature discovery center located near Teluk Bahang.

spots.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
spots.why: Southeast Asia's largest Buddhist temple complex, featuring a towering seven-story pagoda and expansive hillside gardens.

plan.title: Moroccan Kasbahs and Desert Dunes
plan.summary: This 6-day loop from Marrakech traverses the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass in the High Atlas, explores the cinematic kasbahs of Aït Benhaddou, winds through the breathtaking Dades and Todra gorges, and reaches the towering sand dunes of Erg Chebbi at Merzouga before returning via the palm-filled Draa Valley.

days.title: Over the High Atlas to Aït Benhaddou
days.summary: Climbing out of the bustling city of Marrakech, the road winds dramatically over the High Atlas mountains through stunning peaks and Berber villages. The best stretch is the thrilling ascent and descent around the Tizi n'Tichka pass with its sweeping curves and panoramic vistas. The day feels like a grand alpine adventure transitioning rapidly into the arid earthen tones of the pre-Sahara.
days.stay: Stay in a traditional earthen kasbah or guesthouse near the ancient fortified village, offering quiet courtyards and views of the surrounding desert oasis.

days.title: Through the Rose Valley to Dades Gorges
days.summary: This drive follows the fertile Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs eastward before plunging into the dramatic red rock labyrinth of the Dades Gorge. The best stretch is the legendary series of hairpin turns scaling the sheer rock wall of the upper gorge. It feels like an intimate exploration of deep geological time combined with lush river valley agriculture.
days.stay: Stay in a locally run family lodge perched right on the edge of the gorge canyon walls, featuring traditional Moroccan architecture and hearty local cuisine.

days.title: To Todra Gorge and the Sahara Dunes
days.summary: The journey traverses vast desert plateaus before weaving through the towering limestone cliffs of Todra Gorge and out toward the endless sand sea of Erg Chebbi. The highlight is emerging from the rocky track to witness the massive golden dunes rising abruptly from the flat desert floor at sunset. The feel is increasingly remote, adventurous, and spellbinding.
days.stay: Stay in a desert camp or a desert-edge hotel near the dunes, offering comfortable nomadic-style tents with modern amenities and star-filled night skies.

days.title: Journey Down the Draa Valley
days.summary: Heading west, the route tracks the edge of the Sahara along arid gravel plains and through ancient caravan towns like Tazzarine and Alnif. The best stretch involves cruising the quiet desert highway flanked by distant mountain ridges and stone-strewn hamlets. The day evokes the spirit of historical trans-Saharan trade routes and rugged isolation.
days.stay: Stay in a palm grove oasis hotel or kasbah-style inn in town, providing a cool sanctuary of pools and date palms after the desert heat.

days.title: Back toward the High Atlas foothills
days.summary: Following the winding course of the Draa River, the road cuts through dramatic desert canyons and massive palm groves that stretch endlessly along the valley floor. The best stretch is the ascent out of the valley near Agdz with sweeping views of the green ribbon of life against the black mountains. The feel is relaxed, scenic, and deeply connected to rural Moroccan river life.
days.stay: Stay in a restored historic riad or film-friendly hotel in Ouarzazate, known for its cinematic heritage, comfortable courtyards, and relaxed desert hospitality.

days.title: Return over Tichka Pass to Marrakech
days.summary: The final stretch retraces the northern slopes of the High Atlas mountains back toward the vibrant chaos of the imperial city. The highlight is enjoying the changing mountain light on the return descent toward the Haouz plain. The drive feels like a satisfying full-circle loop, dropping you seamlessly from high wilderness back into bustling urban culture.
days.stay: Stay in a traditional riad in the historic medina of Marrakech, featuring intricate tilework, rooftop terraces, and easy walking access to the souks.

roads.name: Route Nationale 9
roads.why: It crosses the High Atlas mountains via the legendary Tizi n'Tichka pass, offering historic routing, incredible elevation changes, and panoramic views of steep valleys.
roads.drive: Features steep grades, numerous tight switchbacks, and occasional heavy truck traffic. Drive with patience and enjoy the sweeping mountain curves, best experienced heading from Marrakech toward Ouarzazate.
roads.tips: Check for snow or rockfall closures in winter; start early to avoid tour bus traffic on the pass; fuel up in Marrakech or Taddart.

roads.name: Route Nationale 10
roads.why: Known as the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs, it connects desert oases and historic fortified mud-brick architecture against a backdrop of the Atlas foothills.
roads.drive: Generally well-paved and rolling highway with moderate traffic, passing through numerous small towns and speed controls.
roads.tips: Watch out for pedestrians and livestock near villages; police checkpoints are frequent so adhere strictly to speed limits.

roads.name: Dades Gorge Road
roads.segment: from Boumalne Dades into the Gorge
roads.why: Renowned among driving enthusiasts and motorcyclists for its breathtaking canyon scenery and the iconic, twisting switchback road scaling the cliff face.
roads.drive: Narrow asphalt with steep drop-offs, hairpin turns, and tight sections shared with local traffic and tour vans.
roads.tips: Drive slowly and use lower gears; the upper sections can be cold in the mornings; use the numerous roadside pullouts for photos.

roads.name: Todra Gorge Road
roads.why: It funnels travelers through a dramatic river canyon where sheer limestone walls tower 300 meters above the narrow road.
roads.drive: Paved and relatively flat through the main gorge, though parts can be congested with pedestrians, climbers, and market stalls.
roads.tips: Visit early in the morning before tour buses arrive to experience the dramatic morning light hitting the canyon floor.

roads.name: Route Nationale 13
roads.why: It serves as the gateway to the Sahara desert, transitioning from scrubland and date palm valleys straight to the towering sand dunes of Erg Chebbi.
roads.drive: Straight, well-maintained desert highway with light traffic, making for an easy and scenic cruise toward the dunes.
roads.tips: Keep an eye out for blowing sand across the road in windy conditions; ensure your vehicle has a full tank before heading south toward Merzouga.

roads.name: Route Nationale 12
roads.why: A remote and striking desert highway connecting ancient oasis settlements along the southern edge of Morocco.
roads.drive: Long, flat stretches of asphalt crossing gravel plains and barren landscapes with minimal traffic.
roads.tips: Carry plenty of water and snacks as services are sparse between towns; check fuel levels in Rissani or Alnif.

plan.title: Costa Verde and Mountain Climb to São Paulo
plan.summary: Drive the stunning coastal rainforest road along Brazil's Costa Verde from Rio de Janeiro to Paraty and Ubatuba, then climb the dramatic winding mountain highway into the highlands of São Paulo.

days.title: Rio de Janeiro to Angra dos Reis
days.overnight: Angra dos Reis, Rio de Janeiro
days.summary: The journey begins by escaping the bustling metropolis of Rio de Janeiro and heading south along the magnificent Costa Verde. As you approach Mangaratiba and Angra dos Reis, the asphalt hugs the coastline with stunning views of emerald waters and forested islands. The drive has a tropical, laid-back feel with gentle coastal curves.
days.stay: Stay in the vibrant center or near the waterfront of Angra dos Reis, where you can find charming coastal inns and comfortable boutique hotels.

days.title: Angra dos Reis to Paraty
days.summary: Today's drive continues along the coastal highway past secluded beaches and dense Atlantic rainforest mountains plunging directly into the sea. The road features rolling terrain and beautiful coastal vistas leading into the historic colonial jewel of Paraty. It is a relaxing stretch that showcases Brazil's dramatic geography.
days.stay: Look for accommodation in the historic center of Paraty, opting for charming colonial-style pousadas that offer a quiet and authentic atmosphere.

days.title: Paraty to Ubatuba
days.summary: This leg weaves between lush tropical mountains and pristine bays, crossing the state line into São Paulo to reach Ubatuba. The route offers sweeping ocean views interspersed with verdant canopies and winding coastal sections. The atmosphere shifts from quiet colonial history to rugged, nature-focused coastline.
days.stay: Choose a beachfront lodge or guesthouse near one of Ubatuba's northern beaches for easy access to nature and quiet surroundings.

days.title: Ubatuba to São Paulo
days.summary: The final day trades the tranquil coast for an adventurous climb up the coastal escarpment via dramatic mountain roads before transitioning onto high-speed highways toward São Paulo. You will experience sharp elevation changes, sweeping curves through dense rainforests, and a gradual entry into the vast urban sprawl of Brazil's largest city.
days.stay: Stay in upscale neighborhoods like Jardins or Vila Madalena in São Paulo, featuring modern hotels, design-focused boutique stays, and excellent dining options.

roads.name: Rodovia Rio-Santos
roads.segment: from Rio de Janeiro to Ubatuba
roads.why: It connects Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo along one of the most breathtaking coastlines in South America, sandwiched between jungle-clad mountains and the Atlantic Ocean.
roads.drive: Mostly two-lane coastal highway with rolling hills, frequent curves, and occasional slow-moving traffic around towns. Best driven from north to south for ocean views.
roads.tips: Watch for sudden tropical downpours that can reduce visibility and cause minor rockfalls. Fuel up before leaving major towns.

roads.name: Rodovia Oswaldo Cruz
roads.why: This legendary mountain pass climbs steeply from the coastal rainforest of Ubatuba up to the cooler highlands of the Paraíba Valley, celebrated by driving enthusiasts for its tight switchbacks.
roads.drive: Very steep grades, sharp hairpins, and significant elevation gains with heavy truck traffic. Requires attentive braking and low-gear driving.
roads.tips: Avoid driving at night due to heavy fog and lack of lighting. Check vehicle brakes before starting the ascent.

plan.title: Cross-Canada Epic: Toronto to Vancouver
plan.summary: A magnificent 14-day transcontinental road trip crossing the Canadian Shield, the shores of Lake Superior, the sweeping prairies of the West, and the majestic peaks of the Canadian Rockies. Experience legendary drives like the Icefields Parkway, Sea-to-Sky Highway, and Highway 60 through Algonquin.

days.title: Toronto to North Bay
days.summary: Begin the journey escaping Toronto's urban sprawl, winding through the rolling hills of cottage country before entering the tranquil forests of Algonquin Provincial Park. The best stretch is Highway 60 as it cuts past mirror-like lakes and dense pine canopies. The day offers a peaceful introduction to the Canadian wilderness.
days.stay: Stay in North Bay near the downtown waterfront area, choosing from comfortable motels or lakeside lodges.

days.title: North Bay to Sault Ste. Marie
days.summary: Drive north alongside the rugged shores of Lake Nipissing before cutting across to the endless pine forests of the Near North. The final approach to Lake Superior offers dramatic glimpses of the great inland sea as you roll into Sault Ste. Marie. The driving is straightforward on smooth, wide highways.
days.stay: Stay close to the canal district in Sault Ste. Marie, where cozy local inns and standard roadside motels await.

days.title: Sault Ste. Marie to White River
days.summary: Tackle the legendary northern arc of Lake Superior, where the highway clings to towering granite cliffs and plunges into deep river valleys. Every corner reveals sweeping vistas of cold, blue water meeting sheer Canadian Shield rock. It is a mesmerizing and remote stretch of driving.
days.stay: Stay near the center of Wawa to experience a classic Northern Ontario hospitality town, featuring rustic motels and small family-run lodges.

days.title: White River to Thunder Bay
days.summary: Continue along the Superior shore past hidden coves, roaring waterfalls, and windswept lookouts. The terrain remains rugged and untamed, offering fantastic driving dynamics over rolling hills and long sweepers. Thunder Bay eventually emerges beneath the iconic silhouette of the Sleeping Giant.
days.stay: Stay in the downtown Port Arthur district of Thunder Bay for easy access to local eateries and comfortable boutique hotels or inns.

days.title: Thunder Bay to Kenora
days.summary: Leave the Great Lakes behind and push west through the endless granite outcrops and dark spruce forests of northwestern Ontario. The road rolls through a seemingly infinite expanse of pristine lakes and rocky cuts. The driving requires steady focus on undulating two-lane highway.
days.stay: Stay right on the waterfront in Kenora for picturesque lake views, choosing from local lakeside resorts or standard motels.

days.title: Kenora to Brandon
days.summary: Cross the provincial border onto the vast flatness of the Canadian prairies near Winnipeg, where the landscape opens up into a colossal checkerboard of farmland. The driving becomes straight and fast across seemingly endless horizons under massive prairie skies. A cruise control day that tests your patience.
days.stay: Stay along the main commercial corridor of Brandon, featuring convenient chain hotels and practical motels.

days.title: Brandon to Swift Current
days.summary: Cruise west across the endless golden wheat fields and rolling plains of southern Saskatchewan. The horizon stretches endlessly in every direction, interrupted only by historic grain elevators and passing freight trains. The Trans-Canada Highway here is wide, fast, and remarkably peaceful.
days.stay: Stay near downtown Swift Current to enjoy quiet local hospitality, with straightforward motels and comfortable roadside inns.

days.title: Swift Current to Longview
days.summary: Leave the flatlands behind as the foothills of the Rocky Mountains begin to ripple against the western horizon. Transition onto the Cowboy Trail for a scenic, undulating run through ranch country with the snowy peaks constantly in view. The driving is scenic and relaxed on rolling two-lane tarmac.
days.stay: Stay in the charming hamlet of Longview near the foothills, choosing from rustic cabins, country B&Bs, or small motels.

days.title: Longview to Banff
days.summary: Drive north toward Calgary before diving straight into the majestic heart of the Rockies along the Bow Valley Parkway. Towering limestone peaks loom overhead as you wind through thick pine forests where wildlife frequently roams. The approach to Banff is nothing short of breathtaking.
days.stay: Stay within walking distance of Banff Avenue for vibrant mountain town energy, selecting from alpine lodges, cozy cabins, or traditional inns.

days.title: Banff to Valemount
days.summary: Drive the world-famous Icefields Parkway, threading between massive glaciers, jagged peaks, and turquoise alpine lakes. The road climbs steadily over high mountain passes with sheer drops and awe-inspiring panoramas at every turn. It is widely considered one of the greatest driving roads on Earth.
days.stay: Stay in Valemount near the foot of the Cariboo Mountains, enjoying quiet mountain chalets, rustic lodges, or standard motels.

days.title: Valemount to Golden
days.summary: Navigate through deep mountain trenches and sweeping river valleys as you loop back toward the main artery of the Rockies. The road offers gentle sweepers alongside raging rivers beneath towering snow-capped summits. Traffic is well-behaved, allowing for a smooth and scenic cruise.
days.stay: Stay in the mountain town of Golden near the Kicking Horse River, choosing from rugged mountain lodges, chalets, or comfortable motels.

days.title: Golden to Kamloops
days.summary: Climb over Rogers Pass in Glacier National Park, carving through tunnels and high alpine snowsheds surrounded by jagged peaks. Descend into the interior plateau where the dramatic mountain backdrop softens into arid benchlands. The driving here is technical, engaging, and visually stunning.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Kamloops near the river confluence, with plenty of reliable motels, hotels, and urban inns.

days.title: Kamloops to Cache Creek
days.summary: Head south through the dramatic, canyon-carved landscapes of the Fraser River valley. The road hugs steep rock walls with the rushing muddy waters of the Fraser River far below. It is a historic and rugged route demanding attentive driving.
days.stay: Stay in the historic junction town of Cache Creek, featuring classic roadside motels and quiet country lodges.

days.title: Cache Creek to Vancouver
days.summary: Conclude the epic journey by tackling the dizzying twists of Duffey Lake Road before descending the legendary Sea-to-Sky Highway down to the Pacific coast. The road drops through dramatic alpine passes, past roaring fjords, and into the glittering urban harbor of Vancouver. A magnificent finale to a cross-country masterpiece.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Vancouver near the waterfront or Gastown, choosing from upscale hotels, boutique urban inns, or comfortable apartments.

roads.name: Highway 60 through Algonquin

official.name: Highway 60 through Algonquin
official.description: The Parkway Corridor across Algonquin Provincial Park, lakes and forest with moose sightings and famous fall colour

roads.why: It serves as the scenic gateway through Ontario's oldest and most famous provincial park, offering dense forests and pristine lakes.
roads.drive: A gentle, rolling two-lane highway with moderate curves, light park traffic, and excellent paved surfaces.
roads.tips: Watch out for wandering wildlife, especially moose at dawn and dusk. Park permit required.

roads.name: Lake Superior Coast
roads.segment: from Sault Ste. Marie to Marathon
roads.why: Celebrated for its dramatic cliffs, sweeping vistas of the world's largest freshwater lake, and rugged Canadian Shield topography.
roads.drive: Undulating two-lane highway featuring long sweepers, steep grades, and occasional heavy transport trucks.
roads.tips: Weather can change rapidly off the lake; keep an eye on fuel levels between remote stretches.

roads.name: Cowboy Trail

official.name: Cowboy Trail
official.description: Foothills ranch country west of Calgary along the Rockies, through Longview, Black Diamond and Turner Valley

roads.why: A stunning alternative route running parallel to the Rockies through historic ranchlands and foothills.
roads.drive: Open, rolling two-lane road with sweeping curves, gentle elevation changes, and very light traffic.
roads.tips: Ideal for photography enthusiasts; watch for cattle and local farm traffic.

roads.name: Bow Valley Parkway

official.name: Bow Valley Parkway
official.description: Slower, wildlife-rich alternative to the Trans-Canada between Banff and Lake Louise, past Johnston Canyon

roads.why: A slower, more intimate alternative to the Trans-Canada Highway that hugs the base of the mountains through prime wildlife habitat.
roads.drive: Winding, narrow two-lane road with strict speed limits and frequent tourist stops.
roads.tips: Check for seasonal bicycle-only closures in spring and autumn; fantastic for wildlife viewing.

roads.name: Icefields Parkway

official.name: Icefields Parkway
official.description: Lake Louise to Jasper along the Continental Divide past Bow Lake, Peyto Lake and the Columbia Icefield, one of the world's great drives

roads.why: Consistently rated among the top scenic drives in the world for its uninterrupted views of ancient glaciers, icefields, and turquoise lakes.
roads.drive: High-altitude mountain highway with steep climbs, sweeping turns, and potential for sudden winter weather even in summer.
roads.tips: Fill up your tank before starting; gas stations are extremely sparse and expensive along the route.

roads.name: Fraser Canyon Highway

official.name: Fraser Canyon Highway
official.description: The Trans-Canada from Hope through the Fraser Canyon to Cache Creek, through tunnels above the river and past Hell's Gate

roads.why: A historic trading route clinging to sheer canyon walls above the rushing turquoise waters of the Fraser River.
roads.drive: Winding canyon road with tunnels, rocksheds, and steep rock faces on one side.
roads.tips: Watch for falling rock warning signs and maintain a safe following distance behind large transport trucks.

roads.name: Duffey Lake Road

official.name: Duffey Lake Road
official.description: Highway 99 beyond Pemberton to Lillooet: steep grades, tight switchbacks and glacier-fed Duffey Lake, a favourite loop for Vancouver drivers

roads.why: A thrilling mountain pass offering high-alpine vistas, pristine lakes, and exhilarating descending switchbacks.
roads.drive: Steep grades, tight hairpins, and dramatic drop-offs requiring good brakes and attentive steering.
roads.tips: Winter tires are legally required here from October to April; cell service is non-existent.

roads.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway

official.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway
official.description: Vancouver to Whistler and Pemberton along Howe Sound, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief, climbing into the Coast Mountains

roads.why: Spectacular engineering feat hugging the sheer granite cliffs of Howe Sound with panoramic ocean and mountain views.
roads.drive: A modern, wide highway featuring sweeping multi-lane curves, tunnels, and dramatic coastal drops.
roads.tips: Can be very busy with commuter and tourist traffic around Whistler and Squamish; avoid rush hours.

plan.title: From Dallas to the Teton Rockies
plan.summary: This epic 7-day road trip takes you from Dallas across the plains, climbing into the majestic Colorado Rockies via the Million Dollar Highway and Trail Ridge Road, before heading north through Wyoming's dramatic landscapes to Yellowstone and Grand Teton National Parks.

days.title: Dallas to Amarillo
days.summary: Begin with a flat, open drive across the rolling plains of North Texas before crossing into the sweeping grasslands of the panhandle. The final stretch on US-287 offers wide horizons and big sky views as you approach the high plains of Amarillo. It is a classic transition day from urban sprawl to rural emptiness.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Amarillo near historic Route 66 to enjoy local steakhouses and eclectic motels, or choose a quiet lodge closer to Palo Duro Canyon.

days.title: Amarillo to Pueblo
days.summary: Drive northwest across the empty high-desert plains of the New Mexico panhandle before climbing steadily toward the Rocky Mountain front range. The approach to Pueblo rewards you with dramatic views of the Spanish Peaks rising sharply from the plains. It is a long, straightforward highway push that transitions from desert scrub to alpine foothills.
days.stay: Stay in Pueblo's historic Riverwalk district in a boutique hotel or cozy B&B for easy access to local green chile restaurants.

days.title: Pueblo to Grand Lake
days.summary: Conquer one of America's highest continuous paved roads, climbing high above the tree line with breathtaking alpine tundra vistas. The ascent brings you past dramatic glacial valleys before descending into the peaceful mountain basin of Grand Lake. Expect sweeping switchbacks, thin air, and awe-inspiring panoramic overlooks.
days.stay: Stay on the shores of Grand Lake in a rustic lakeside cabin or mountain lodge within walking distance of the western entrance to the park.

days.title: Grand Lake to Steamboat Springs
days.summary: Cruise westward along scenic river valleys flanked by towering pine forests and rugged canyon walls. The drive follows winding mountain passes through the Routt National Forest before opening up into the broad valley of Steamboat Springs. It is a scenic, relaxing day of mountain driving through prime Colorado wilderness.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Steamboat Springs near the historic温泉 districts in a comfortable mountain resort or local inn.

days.title: Steamboat Springs to Lander
days.summary: Head north across high desert sagebrush plateaus and rolling Wyoming ranchlands toward the rugged Wind River Range. The route climbs over South Pass via WY-28, offering historical markers and sweeping views of pioneering trails. It is a wide-open western drive defined by immense scale and remote landscapes.
days.stay: Stay in historic downtown Lander in a traditional western motel or local lodge known for its climbing and outdoor heritage.

days.title: Lander to Yellowstone National Park
days.summary: Traverse the dramatic peaks of the Absaroka Range along US-287, climbing over Togwotee Pass with incredible alpine backdrops. Descend into Jackson Hole before entering the southern gates of Yellowstone National Park. The day combines high mountain forest passes with the geothermal wonders of the world's first national park.
days.stay: Stay inside Yellowstone National Park at a historic timber lodge or park cabin situated near the main thermal basins.

days.title: Yellowstone National Park to Colter Bay Village
days.summary: Explore the geothermal heartland of Yellowstone before cruising south through the John D. Rockefeller Jr. Memorial Parkway. The grand finale features the iconic, jagged peaks of the Teton Range reflecting across pristine alpine lakes. It is a breathtaking drive capped by some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in North America.
days.stay: Stay in Colter Bay Village on the shores of Jackson Lake in a cozy wood-paneled cabin with sweeping views of the Teton Range.

roads.name: Trail Ridge Road
roads.segment: from Grand Lake to Estes Park

official.name: Trail Ridge Road/Beaver Meadow Road
official.description: America's highest continuously paved road crosses the alpine tundra of Rocky Mountain National Park

roads.why: It is the highest continuous paved road in North America, cresting at 12,183 feet and offering driving enthusiasts a true alpine motoring experience above the tree line.
roads.drive: Steep grades, tight switchbacks, and sheer drops with no guardrails in places. Wind and weather can change instantly; drive in the morning before afternoon thunderstorms.
roads.tips: Open only from late spring to mid-fall due to heavy snow. Fill up on gas before entering the park as there are no stations along the high road.

roads.name: Grand Loop Road
roads.segment: from South Entrance to Old Faithful and Canyon
roads.why: This is the primary artery linking Yellowstone's most famous geothermal features, deep canyons, and abundant wildlife viewing areas.
roads.drive: Curving two-lane roads with heavy tourist traffic, RVs, and frequent wildlife jams. Speeds are low and patience is required.
roads.tips: Watch out for bison blocking the road. Drive early in the morning or late evening for lighter traffic and better wildlife activity.

plan.title: Montreal and Gaspé Peninsula Coastal Loop
plan.summary: A 7-day scenic journey from Montreal along the historic north shore of the St. Lawrence River, looping around the wild Gaspé Peninsula via Route 132 to experience coastal villages, stunning sea rocks, and marine life.

days.title: Montreal to Tadoussac
days.summary: Start your journey heading northeast along the St. Lawrence River, passing historic villages and rolling farmlands on the Chemin du Roy. The landscape gradually opens up as you approach Quebec City before transitioning to the dramatic coastal cliffs of Charlevoix and arriving at the majestic fjord views of Tadoussac. It is a long but rewarding driving day blending heritage and big water vistas.
days.stay: Stay right in the heart of Tadoussac near the wharf to easily catch early morning whale watching tours, choosing from charming local inns or cozy historic B&Bs.

days.title: Tadoussac to Matane
days.summary: Take the ferry across the massive St. Lawrence estuary to the rugged north shore, driving along Route des Baleines through dramatic rocky landscapes. Afterward, catch another ferry across to Matane on the Gaspé Peninsula, where the dramatic sea cliffs of the Chic-Choc mountains begin to frame your drive. The feel of the day shifts from remote boreal wilderness to classic maritime coastal charm.
days.stay: Look for a comfortable waterfront motel or seaside inn near the port in Matane to unwind after a full day of maritime travel.

days.title: Matane to Gaspé
days.summary: Wind your way along the northern edge of the Gaspé Peninsula on Route 132, sandwiched between sheer cliffs and the crashing waves of the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The road twists through rugged headlands and small fishing ports with stunning lookouts at every turn. Expect sweeping ocean views and a wonderfully remote, salty coastal atmosphere.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Gaspé or near Forillon National Park in a local lodge, motel, or seasonal inn surrounded by maritime nature.

days.title: Gaspé to Amqui
days.summary: Continue your loop around the peninsula, passing the iconic pierced rock of Percé before heading south along Chaleur Bay. The coastline here is gentler, featuring warmer waters, sandy beaches, and welcoming Acadian villages. It is a scenic and relaxing driving stretch that showcases the diverse microclimates of the region.
days.stay: Book a cozy B&B or coastal motel in Carleton-sur-Mer close to the tranquil waters of Baie des Chaleurs.

days.title: Amqui to Route 362 in Charlevoix (one end)
days.summary: Leave the coast behind temporarily as you cut inland through the Matapedia Valley, following riverbeds and forested mountains up toward Amqui. The terrain offers smooth sweeping curves through dense timberland before reconnecting with the St. Lawrence river valley. Enjoy a peaceful and scenic drive dominated by northern forests and rolling hills.
days.stay: Stay in a traditional roadside motel or regional lodge around Amqui.

days.title: Route 362 in Charlevoix (one end) to Route 362 in Charlevoix (other end)
days.summary: Traverse the breathtaking Route 362 through Charlevoix, widely considered one of the most picturesque drives in eastern Canada. The road dips and climbs past dramatic clifftop viewpoints, art communities like Baie-Saint-Paul, and sweeping panoramas of the St. Lawrence. It is a driver's delight with rolling elevations and stunning visual payoff around every curve.
days.stay: Find a charming historic inn or boutique hotel perched along the scenic cliffs of Charlevoix.

days.title: Route 362 in Charlevoix (other end) to Montreal
days.summary: Complete your loop by driving the final scenic stretch back toward the vibrant urban energy of Montreal. The final miles offer a comfortable cruise along major highways, allowing you to reflect on the immense scale of the St. Lawrence and the rugged beauty of the Gaspé. Arrive back in the city by late afternoon.
days.stay: Stay in a chic downtown boutique hotel in Montreal to celebrate the end of your maritime road trip.

roads.name: Chemin du Roy

official.name: Chemin du Roy
official.description: Canada's oldest road, along the north shore of the St. Lawrence from Montreal to Quebec City through historic villages

roads.why: Canada's oldest highway offers a rich historical journey passing centuries-old stone houses, rural Quebec farmlands, and heritage villages alongside the St. Lawrence River.
roads.drive: A gentle two-lane rural and regional highway with moderate traffic, light rolling grades, and numerous small-town speed zones. Best driven heading northeast.
roads.tips: Watch out for local cyclists and agricultural vehicles. Plan fuel stops in larger towns along the route.

roads.name: Route 362 in Charlevoix

official.name: Route 362 in Charlevoix
official.description: Rollercoaster coast road from Baie-Saint-Paul to La Malbaie high above the St. Lawrence

roads.why: Widely praised by road trip enthusiasts for its breathtaking clifftop vistas, artisan villages, and undulating rollercoaster profile over the ancient meteorite crater rim.
roads.drive: A remarkably scenic roller-coaster road featuring steep drops, sharp curves, and incredible visual exposure overlooking the St. Lawrence River.
roads.tips: Drive west-to-east or vice versa for optimal sunlight on the water; watch for tourists at viewpoint pullouts.

roads.name: Route des Baleines
roads.why: This northern coastal corridor treats drivers to expansive views of the St. Lawrence estuary where whales frequently breach close to the rocky shoreline.
roads.drive: A well-paved secondary highway featuring long straight stretches interspersed with sweeping coastal curves and occasional steep grades.
roads.tips: Keep your camera ready for marine wildlife pullouts and check ferry timetables in advance.

roads.name: Gaspé Peninsula
roads.segment: from Matane around the peninsula to Carleton-sur-Mer
roads.why: Renowned for its dramatic combination of towering Appalachian mountains plunging directly into the blue waters of the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
roads.drive: A classic coastal highway with sweeping curves, rolling hills, tight cliffside switchbacks, and dramatic elevation changes, especially along the northern shore.
roads.tips: Summer and early autumn are ideal; watch for wildlife crossing the road at dusk and dawn.

plan.title: Historical Wonders of Turkey: Cappadocia to Ephesus
plan.summary: Explore the surreal rock formations of Cappadocia, the ancient Silk Road trading posts of Konya, the stunning Mediterranean coast of Antalya, the white terraces of Pamukkale, and the magnificent ruins of Ephesus over seven immersive days.

days.title: Magical Landscapes of Cappadocia
days.summary: Begin your journey amidst the otherworldly fairy chimneys and deep ravines of Cappadocia, driving through dramatic volcanic landscapes. The best stretch winds around Ürgüp where rock-cut formations tower above the road, offering an immersive feel of ancient history meeting natural wonder.
days.stay: Stay in central Göreme within walking distance of the rock formations, choosing from charming cave hotels or boutique B&Bs.

days.title: Across the Anatolian Steppe to Konya
days.summary: Cross the vast, wide-open expanses of the Anatolian Steppe where flat horizons stretch endlessly under huge skies. The driving is smooth and fast on long straightaways, giving a stark, meditative feel before you reach the historic city of Konya.
days.stay: Stay in downtown Konya near the Mevlana Museum, featuring comfortable modern hotels and traditional guesthouses.

days.title: Over the Taurus Mountains to Antalya
days.summary: Climb steeply out of the plateau and over the rugged spine of the Taurus Mountains, tackling sweeping alpine curves and deep pine-scented valleys. The descent toward the Mediterranean coast opens up breathtaking panoramic views of the turquoise sea far below.
days.stay: Stay in the old harbor district of Antalya (Kaleiçi) for atmospheric boutique hotels set in restored Ottoman-era mansions.

days.title: Mediterranean Coast to Fethiye
days.summary: Drive the legendary coastal highway that clings precariously to sheer cliffs plunging straight into the Mediterranean Sea. You will navigate relentless, thrilling curves and pass hidden coves before finishing in the vibrant harbor town of Fethiye.
days.stay: Stay near the Fethiye harbor or the quiet marina area, choosing from cozy seaside lodges, apartments, or boutique hotels.

days.title: Through the River Valleys to Pamukkale
days.summary: Leave the coast behind and wind north through fertile river valleys and rolling agricultural hills toward the interior. The route transitions from sea breezes to the stark, blinding white travertine terraces of Pamukkale.
days.stay: Stay close to the thermal pools of Pamukkale in family-run thermal hotels or quiet local bed-and-breakfasts.

days.title: Onward to the Historic Town of Selçuk
days.summary: Follow the Meander River valley westward through lush orchards and olive groves framed by gentle hills. The road offers an easy, relaxing cruise that leads straight to the historic town of Selçuk, surrounded by ancient heritage.
days.stay: Stay in central Selçuk near the old aqueducts, opting for traditional pensions, family-run inns, or boutique hotels.

days.title: Exploring Ephesus and Surrounds
days.summary: Take a short, scenic morning drive through hillside villages to Şirince before cruising north on the multi-lane highway toward the bustling Aegean metropolis of İzmir. The final stretch balances quiet rural charm with vibrant coastal city driving.
days.stay: Stay in the Alsancak or Konak districts of İzmir for lively waterfront access, stylish urban hotels, and great dining.

roads.name: Cappadocia Highway Route
roads.why: Weaves through iconic volcanic rock formations, fairy chimneys, and deep historical valleys.
roads.drive: Well-paved two-lane road with gentle grades and moderate local tourist traffic.
roads.tips: Watch out for slow agricultural vehicles and tourists stopping abruptly for photos.

roads.name: Anatolian Highway
roads.why: Crosses the vast, high-altitude central Turkish plateau with dramatic open skies.
roads.drive: Long, straight, multi-lane divided highway allowing for sustained cruising speeds.
roads.tips: Fuel up before departing major towns as stretches between service stations can be long.

roads.name: Taurus Mountain Road
roads.why: Spectacular high-elevation pass offering thrilling hairpin turns and dramatic mountain scenery.
roads.drive: Steep grades, tight switchbacks, and potential snow or ice at high passes during shoulder seasons.
roads.tips: Check vehicle brakes before descending; drive in lower gears to manage engine braking.

roads.name: Mediterranean Coastal Road
roads.why: One of the world's great coastal drives, hugging cliff edges with endless sea vistas.
roads.drive: Twisting, narrow two-lane road with sheer drops, tight corners, and occasional heavy tourist traffic.
roads.tips: Drive west towards Fethiye to keep the sea views on your side of the road; watch for blind corners.

roads.name: Aegean Interior Link
roads.why: Connects coastal resort areas to interior agricultural basins through scenic mountain passes.
roads.drive: Well-maintained asphalt with moderate winding sections and comfortable driving grades.
roads.tips: Keep an eye out for speed cameras near town entries.

roads.name: Denizli Highway
roads.why: Traverses rolling hills and rural farmland leading directly to world-famous thermal phenomena.
roads.drive: Standard regional highway with smooth pavement and light to moderate traffic.
roads.tips: Best driven in the morning to catch the morning mist over the river valleys.

roads.name: Ephesus Route
roads.why: Connects major historical heritage sites along the fertile Aegean coastal corridor.
roads.drive: Fast divided highway transitioning into busier urban approaches near İzmir.
roads.tips: Traffic increases significantly as you approach İzmir; allow extra time during rush hours.

spots.name: Göreme Open-Air Museum
spots.why: Explore incredible rock-cut Byzantine churches adorned with remarkably well-preserved medieval frescoes.

spots.name: Uçhisar Castle
spots.why: Climb to the highest point in Cappadocia for a staggering 360-degree panorama of the valleys.

spots.name: Pasabag Monks Valley
spots.why: Walk among some of the most striking, multi-headed fairy chimneys in the region.

spots.name: Sultanhani Caravanserai
spots.why: Step back in time at the largest medieval caravanserai on the historic Silk Road.

spots.name: Mevlana Museum
spots.why: Visit the striking turquoise-domed mausoleum of the famous Sufi mystic Rumi.

spots.name: Konya Ethnography Museum
spots.why: Discover rich local history, traditional Seljuk costumes, and regional artifacts.

spots.name: Lake Beyşehir
spots.why: Enjoy stunning views over Turkey's largest freshwater tectonic lake surrounded by mountains.

spots.name: Eşrefoğlu Mosque
spots.why: Admire a magnificent 13th-century wooden hypostyle mosque with intricate carved columns.

spots.name: Düden Waterfalls
spots.why: Watch a spectacular river plunge directly over coastal cliffs into the Mediterranean Sea.

spots.name: Kaputaş Beach
spots.why: Stop at the clifftop overlook for an iconic photo of this breathtaking turquoise cove.

spots.name: Saklıkent Gorge
spots.why: Wike through a dramatic, cool canyon carved by rushing mountain meltwater.

spots.name: Patara ruins
spots.why: Wander through extensive ancient Lycian ruins and visit the birthplace of Saint Nicholas.

spots.name: Pamukkale Thermal Pools
spots.why: Wade barefoot across the dazzling white travertine terraces filled with warm mineral waters.

spots.name: Hierapolis
spots.why: Explore the sprawling ruins of an ancient Greco-Roman spa city perched above the terraces.

spots.name: Cleopatra's Pool
spots.why: Swim among submerged ancient Roman marble columns in warm mineral-rich thermal waters.

spots.name: Temple of Artemis
spots.why: Stand at the remains of one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

spots.name: Ephesus Archaeological Site
spots.why: Marvel at the stunning facade of the Library of Celsus and the massive ancient theater.

spots.name: Basilica of St. John
spots.why: Walk the atmospheric ruins of a massive Byzantine basilica built over the apostle's tomb.

info.title: Basilica of Saint John the Theologian

spots.name: Şirince
spots.why: Stroll through a charming hillside village famous for preserved traditional architecture and fruit wines.

spots.name: İzmir Agora
spots.why: Explore the well-preserved Roman-era public square right in the heart of modern İzmir.

spots.name: Kordon
spots.why: Stroll the vibrant seaside promenade and enjoy fresh local seafood at a traditional tavern.
